questions.title: AD:RP-1.Q1
questions.text: Have conditions been identified that trigger the execution of the service continuity plan?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: This question is important to understanding under what circumstances the service continuity plan is enacted.

Question Intent: The intent of this question is to determine if the service continuity plan takes effect based on situational or environmental circumstances rather than on an ad-hoc basis.

  • Plan exists
  • Plan is regularly evaluated and updated as needed
  • Plan is regularly exercised to ensure operational capability
  • Triggering conditions for plan execution are documented within the plan

 

Service Continuity Plan: The documentation of a predetermined set of instructions or procedures that describe how an organization’s mission/business processes will be sustained during and after a significant disruption.

 

Business Continuity Plan (BCP): The documentation of a predetermined set of instructions or procedures that describe how an organization’s mission/business processes will be sustained during and after a significant disruption.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • ·       Qualities noted above are fully met

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • ·       Plan present but execution may be ad-hoc or not thoroughly exercised

Possible Evidence

  • Service continuity plan

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: SCM:G4.Q1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5:  IR-4(1), IR-4(3)
  • NIST 800-82, Rev. 2
  • NIST 800-34, Rev. 1

questions.title: AD:IM-1.Q1
questions.text: Is execution of service continuity plans reviewed?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The review of executed service continuity plans identifies plan shortcomings and needed improvements.

Question Intent: To determine if the execution of service continuity plans is reviewed.

  • Unforeseen circumstances that arise during the execution are to be documented and addressed.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The execution of each service continuity plan that supports the critical service is reviewed.
     OR
  • If service continuity plans have not been executed, reviews of executed plans are required as part of a standard process.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The execution of some service continuity plans is reviewed.

Possible Evidence

  • A formal report or correspondence that demonstrates service continuity plans have been reviewed.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: SCM:G4.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4, CP-2

questions.title: AD:CO-1.Q1
questions.text: Are incident status and response communicated to public relations staff and external media outlets?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Appropriate communications to external stakeholders is an important element in managing the impact of a cybersecurity incident. Timely updates and a conveyed impression of transparency can help defuse tensions that may build as a result of an incident.

Question Intent: To determine if incident status and response are communicated to public relations staff and external media outlets.

  • Incident status and response should be communicated in a controlled and regular manner to internal and external stakeholders.
  • Incident status and response should be managed throughout the incident lifecycle.

The incident communication process should include:

  • the stakeholders with whom communication about incidents are required
  • the level of communication appropriate to various stakeholders
  • special controls over communication (i.e., encryption or secured communications) that are appropriate for some stakeholders
  • the frequency and timing of communication

Examples of stakeholders that may need to be included in incident communication:

  • internal staff who have incident handling and management responsibilities
  • asset owners and service owners
  • information technology staff
  • business continuity staff
  • affected customers or suppliers
  • local, state, and federal emergency management staff
  • support functions such as legal, audit, and human resources
  • legal and law enforcement staff (including federal agencies), if the incident may have legal ramifications
  • external media outlets
  • regulatory and governing agencies
  • local utilities (power, gas, telecommunications, water, etc.)

Criteria for “Yes” Response

  • The organization communicates incident status and response to all public relations staff and external media outlets.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response

  • The organization communicates incident status and response to some public relations staff and external media outlets. (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence:

  • Organization-level communications plan
  • Incident communications plan
  • Example of past communications

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: IM:G4.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4(15)

questions.title: AD:CO-2.Q1
questions.text: Do recovery plans include measures to repair reputation?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Cybersecurity incidents can damage the reputation of an organization or critical service, thereby undermining its effectiveness. The presence of plans to repair reputation will allow an organization to begin that work more quickly after an incident occurs, thus minimizing the long-term impact of an incident.

Question Intent: To determine whether an organization’s recovery plans include measures to repair the reputation of an organization or service following a cybersecurity incident.

Reputation should be interpreted broadly and could include the standing of an organization or service with the general public, other departments within the organization, government agencies, or commercial entities, to name just a few examples.

The plans need not detail every potential contingency and stakeholder but should be sufficient to guide activities in a meaningful way.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Recovery plans include measures to repair reputation with all primary stakeholders in anticipated incident scenarios.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Recovery plans include measure to repair reputation with some primary stakeholders or some anticipated scenarios. (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Incident response plan
  • Organization-level communications plan
  • Incident communications plan
  • Disaster recovery plan
  • Business continuity plan

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST CSF: RC.CO-2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4(15)

questions.title: AD:CO-3.Q1
questions.text: Is there a documented communications plan for incident management and  recovery activities?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Providing appropriate information to internal and external stakeholders can reduce confusion and enhance reputation during security incidents and recovery activities. The communications plan helps ensure that the proper resources are available when needed and that individuals know their roles.

Question Intent: To determine if there is a documented communications plan associated with incident management and recovery activities.

While the communications plan need not identify all possible contingencies, it does need to include a complete work breakdown structure that documents responsibilities, stakeholders, and core activities. It should be sufficiently detailed to ensure duplicative work does not occur and that there is clarity for who is communicating to which stakeholders.

The plan should provide information on what to communicate, when to communicate it, to whom the communication should be directed, who shall do the communication, and the methods by which communication shall occur.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Communications plans include both incident management and recovery as well as all primary stakeholders and work roles.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Communications plans are present but lack detail on either incident management or recovery scenarios, stakeholders, or work roles. (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Incident response plan
  • Organization-level communications plan
  • Incident communications plan
  • Disaster recovery plan
  • Business continuity plan

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • ISO/IEC 27001:2013, 7.4 Communication
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4

questions.title: AD:RL-1.Q1
questions.text: Use allow-listing to restrict communications to a specified set of addresses. (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: A deny-all, permit-by-exception network communications traffic policy ensures that only those system connections that are essential and approved are allowed.

Question Intent: To determine if the use of allow-lists are implemented to restrict communications with the critical service/HVA environment to a specified set of addresses.

  • Ensure that cyber resources are used consistently with mission or business function purposes and approved uses. Avoid “mission creep,” which can increase a system’s attack surface.
  • Identify IP addresses/ranges authorized to communicate with the system.
  • Employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy to allow the communications with authorized IP addresses/ranges.
  • Denying by default and allowing by exception applies to inbound and outbound network communications traffic.
  • General source address validation techniques are applied to restrict the use of illegal and unallocated source addresses as well as source addresses that should only be used within the system.
  • Review and update the list of authorized IP addresses/ranges at an organization-defined frequency.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Allow-lists have been implemented on all appropriate technology assets to restrict communications with the critical service/HVA environment to a specified set of addresses.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Allow-lists have been implemented on some appropriate technology assets to restrict communications with the critical service/HVA environment to a specified set of addresses.

Possible Evidence

  • Documented allow-lists that have been implemented on all appropriate technology assets or system components.
  • Documentation detailing the implementation and configuration of the allow-lists on all appropriate technology assets or system components.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-7(11)

options.text: The organization does not restrict communications to specified addresses.

questions.title: AD:RL-2.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis for organization-defined systems, system components, or system services?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Criticality analysis is a key risk management tenant and informs the prioritization of mission critical services/functions, associated systems and system components, and informs the prioritization of protection and sustainment requirements and activities.

Question Intent: To determine if a criticality analysis of the critical service/HVA environment has been completed and as a result the critical system components and functions have been identified and documented.

  • Not all system components, functions, or services necessarily require significant protections.
  • The identification of critical system components and functions considers applicable laws, executive orders, regulations, directives, policies, standards, system functionality requirements, system and component interfaces, and system and component dependencies.
  • Systems engineers conduct a functional decomposition of a system to identify mission-critical functions and components. The functional decomposition includes the identification of organizational missions supported by the system, decomposition into the specific functions to perform those missions, and traceability to the hardware, software, and firmware components that implement those functions, including when the functions are shared by many components within and external to the system.
  • The operational environment of a system or a system component may impact the criticality, including the connections to and dependencies on cyber-physical systems, devices, system-of-systems, and outsourced IT services.
  • System components that allow unmediated access to critical system components or functions are considered critical due to the inherent vulnerabilities that such components create.
  • Component and function criticality are assessed in terms of the impact of a component or function failure on the organizational missions that are supported by the system that contains the components and functions.
  • Criticality analysis is performed when an architecture or design is being developed, modified, or upgraded.
  • If such analysis is performed early in the system development life cycle, organizations may be able to modify the system design to reduce the critical nature of these components and functions, such as by adding redundancy or alternate paths into the system design.
  • In addition to criticality analysis for systems, system components, and system services, criticality analysis of information is an important consideration.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has completed and documented the results of a criticality analysis and as an outcome identified all critical system components and functions of the critical service/HVA environment.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization is in the process of performing a criticality analysis and has partially documented the results.

Possible Evidence

  • Documented results from the criticality analysis detailing the identified critical system components and functions.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-9

questions.title: AD:RL-3.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization replace obsolete system components prior to the end of support or service agreements?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The use of obsolete, nearing obsolete or low assurance implementations of technology may increase the security and privacy risks.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization replaces obsolete and unsupported system components as needed and prior to the end of support or service agreements.

  • Replace low-assurance or poorly understood implementations with trustworthy implementations
  • Technology refresh planning may encompass hardware, software, firmware, processes, personnel skill sets, suppliers, service providers, and facilities.
  • Technology refreshes typically occur during the operations and maintenance stage of the system development life cycle.
  • The use of obsolete or nearing obsolete technology may increase the security and privacy risks associated with:
  • unsupported components
  • counterfeit or repurposed components
  • components unable to implement security or privacy requirements
  • slow or inoperable components
  • components from untrusted sources
  • inadvertent personnel error
  • or increased complexity

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization replaces all system components designated as obsolete or unsupported prior to the end of support or service level agreements.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization replaces some system components designated as obsolete or unsupported prior to the end of support or service level agreements.

Possible Evidence

  • A documented list or inventory of system components considered to be obsolete or unsupported
  • Updated inventory showing replacement components and updated asset descriptions.
  • Copies of support or service level agreements showing the term of the agreement.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SA-3(3), SA-22, SI-13(1)

questions.title: AN:AR-1.Q1
questions.text: Are reconfiguration tasks performed at times that minimize potential negative impacts to systems?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Performing system maintenance or reconfiguration increases the likelihood of a system outage that may disrupt mission essential functions.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization has identified and implemented the use of appropriate outage windows. 

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has identified appropriate times to perform system reconfiguration which will minimize negative impacts to the system and adhere to those maintenance windows.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has identified appropriate times to perform system reconfiguration but does not fully adhere to them.   

Possible Evidence

  • Configuration Management Plan

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4(2)

questions.title: AN:AR-2.Q1
questions.text:
Does the organization have the capability to manage capacity, bandwidth, or other
redundancy to limit negative impacts?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Service or application outages may be caused by over utilization.

Question Intent: Write here what the question is trying to ascertain. 

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization employs techniques for balancing all critical application and service application resources.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has a mechanism in in place

Possible Evidence

  • Specific implementation details in a System Security Plan (SSP).

Reference to standards/source assessments

questions.title: AN:AR-3.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization deploy a solution that can automatically disable host or user access?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Anomalous user or system account behavior can be an indicator of compromise. The ability to limit access to or from potentially compromises environments may aid in securing the overall system.

Question Intent: Determine if the system possesses the ability to automatically disable access. Organizations plan for the dynamic deactivation of system accounts by establishing trust relationships, business rules, and mechanisms with appropriate authorities to validate related authorizations and privileges.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The system has the capability to automatically disable accounts or isolate hosts based on parameterized rule sets.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The system has the capability to disable user accounts or host accessibility but does not do so automatically.

Possible Evidence

  • System Security Plans

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-2(8)

questions.title: AN:BE-1.Q1
questions.text: Has the organization defined its role in the supply chain and reviewed it for updates at least annually?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Defining the organization’s role in the supply chain is important to then determine appropriate protections against supply chain threats to the system. 

Question Intent: Determine if the organization has defined its role in the supply chain.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has defined its role in the supply chain by documenting its supply chain dependencies, and
  • The organization conducts an annual review.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has defined its role in the supply chain but there is no periodic review.

Possible Evidence

  • A document listing all supply chain dependencies for the given system. ISA/MOUs for third party interconnections. SLAs for third parties. Indications of periodic review. Supply Chain Risk Management Plan.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SR-1

questions.title: AN:BE-2.Q1
questions.text: Has the organization's place in critical infrastructure been identified?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Identifying the organization’s place in critical infrastructure is important to then determine appropriate protection strategies for critical infrastructure.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization has identified its place in critical infrastructure.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has identified its place in critical infrastructure in appropriate documentation.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The place in critical infrastructure is identified but there is no periodic review.

Possible Evidence

  • A critical infrastructure and key resources protection plan has been developed, documented, and is kept updated

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PM-8

questions.title: AN:BE-3.Q1
questions.text: Are the Organization’s Critical Services formally documented?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Identification of critical services would be a result of prioritization efforts.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization has identified its critical services or HVAs.

Critical Services:   Services are activities the organization carries out in the performance of a duty or in the production of a product. Critical services are services on which the success of the organization’s mission depends.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • A list of critical services and HVAs is kept current (reviewed and updated at least annually).

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A list of critical services or HVAs is available, but ignored, or out of date.

Possible Evidence

  • A list of critical services, a list of HVAs

  • IMR: EH:G1.Q1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-9

questions.title: AN:BE-4.Q1
questions.text: Are the associations between assets and the critical service they support documented and updated as needed at least annually?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Documenting the relationship between assets and the critical services they support enables effective development, implementation, and management of resilience strategies supporting the organization’s mission.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization documents associations between assets and the critical services they support.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a list of high-value services and associated assets which is current (updated at least annually)

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • List of high-value services without associated assets, or less than 30% of services having associated assets identified.

Possible Evidence

  • List of high-value services and associated assets

  • CRR: AM:G3.Q1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-16, CM-8, CP-2(8)

questions.text: Are confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements established for each service-related asset?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: CIA requirements should be documented to ensure their resilience needs are planned for.

Question Intent: Whether confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements are established for each service-related asset?

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • A list of confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements is established for each critical service-related asset

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A list of confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements is established for only for a partial list (more than 40% but less than 75%) of critical service-related assets

Possible Evidence

  • List of confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements established for each critical service-related asset

questions.title: AN:CA-1.Q1
questions.text: Is capacity management and planning  (managing system and capacity, network bandwidth, or other redundancy aspects) performed?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Managing capacity ensures that sufficient capacity is available to counter flooding attacks. Managing capacity includes establishing selected usage priorities, quotas, partitioning, or load balancing.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization conducts capacity management and planning. Specifically, does the organization consider the potential impact of flooding attacks, and has it deployed countermeasures to prevent or recover from these types of attacks?

  • Definition of any key words with examples
  • Flooding attack

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • (1) The organization has a documented process for conducting capacity management and planning. (2) The organization has conducted an analysis to identify and characterize the types of flooding attacks that might occur. (3) The organization has deployed countermeasures to prevent or recover from these types of attacks.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization performs 1 or 2 of items 1), 2), or 3) in “Criteria for Full Implementation Response.”
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Capacity management and planning document (policy or procedure), SC-5(2) control implementation description

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-5(2)

questions.title: AN:CA-2.Q1
questions.text: Is information about threat actors, indicators, and potential, predicted and observed events stored and disseminated  to all stakeholders?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Threat intelligence is a key component of a cybersecurity program. The identification and characterization of the threat enables cyber defenders to plan and execute defensive operations at the right time, with the right resources.

Question Intent: Does the organization have a dedicated threat intelligence capability? What products does it produce and who consumes the products?

  • Definition of any key words with examples
  • Indicator of Compromise

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has personnel dedicated to threat intelligence analysis and threat intelligence production/dissemination. Threat intelligence informs the planning and execution of cybersecurity operations.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has personnel that perform threat intelligence functions as an additional duty or on a part-time basis. Threat intelligence is disconnected from operational planning and execution.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Threat intelligence procedures, concepts of operations, list of threat intelligence sources, examples of threat intelligence products produced by the threat intelligence element.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PM-16

questions.title: AN:CP-1.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization conduct an impact-level prioritization of organizational systems to obtain additional granularity on system impact levels?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Considering the impact of IT Systems from a top-down approach, and evaluating them as a whole, sometimes will reveal that the security categorizations of individual devices are inaccurate when they are a component of a larger organizational system.

Question Intent: to determine if the organization conducts impact-level prioritization of organizational systems to obtain additional granularity on individual system impact levels.

The impact level of an individual system can raise or lower the impact level prioritization of an organizational system. Just as an individual systems location within an organization system can raise its own impact level, therefore, both organizational systems and individual information systems should be evaluated keeping the other in mind.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization conducts impact-level prioritizations of all organizational systems for the purpose of obtaining additional granularity on system impact levels.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization conducts impact-level prioritizations of some organizational systems for the purpose of obtaining additional granularity on system impact levels.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Documentation demonstrating impact levels of organizational systems.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IA-2(6)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:CP-2.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization coordinate cybersecurity activities across system, mission, and organizational levels?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The implementation of an organization’s cybersecurity strategy will vary depending on the business units responsible for its execution, therefore it is useful to consider how it is operationalized in different contexts across the organization.

Question Intent: This question is seeking to learn more about how the organization coordinates cybersecurity activities across systems, missions, and organization levels.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The respondent is confident in their response, demonstrates clear knowledge of cybersecurity activities across the organization, and provides an example of how activities are implemented at each level.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The respondent is timid in their answer; However, they provide a brief response as to how cybersecurity activities are embedded in the organization’s business practices. More information could be provided on specific implementation with regards to the system, mission, and organization levels.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Organizational cybersecurity or information security strategy.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IA-1, PM-1, CP-4(1)
  • NIST 800-160, Rev. 1

questions.title: AN:CP-3.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization plan for the continuance of  essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Business continuity planning is critical to minimize losses.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has a business continuity plan in place to provide the continuance of essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity.

  • Business continuity planning requires organizations to perform business process analyses (BPAs), business impact analyses (BIAs), and risk assessments. These need to be performed to identify essential mission and business functions that require minimal or no loss of operation, so they can then be prioritized when planning for business continuity capabilities.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a fully documented and developed business continuity function that provides for the continuance of essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has a partially documented and developed business continuity function that provides for the continuance of essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Business continuity plan, business process analyses (BPAs), business impact analyses (BIAs), risk assessments

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2(5)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:CP-4.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization conduct practical exercises (e.g., social engineering attempts) in literacy training that simulate events and incidents?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Social engineering exploits human trust to obtain access to organizational assets or resources that wouldn’t otherwise be granted. Many attacks use social engineering techniques such as phishing or vishing to obtain initial entry into systems, therefore it is crucial to train organizational personnel to recognize when social engineering attempts are taking place.

Practical exercises include no-notice social engineering attempts to collect information, gain unauthorized access, or simulate the adverse impact of opening malicious email attachments or invoking, via spear phishing attacks, malicious web links.

Question Intent: This question ascertains if the organization uses practical exercises to train employees on how to recognize social engineering attempts as they occur.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All organizational personnel receive practical exercises to help them to recognize social engineering attempts.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  •  Some organizational personnel receive practical exercises to help them to recognize social engineering attempts.
  • Or, all organizational personnel receive training in how to recognize social engineering attempts however the training does not include practical exercises.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Curriculum from organizational security training that covers social engineering and provides a practical interactive component.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AT-2(1)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:DI-1.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization obtain alternate telecommunications services from providers that are separated from primary service providers to reduce susceptibility to the same threats?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Alternate telecommunications services are used to minimize common mode failures, particularly threat events that exploit common vulnerabilities.

Question Intent: This question determines if alternate telecommunications services from providers that are separated from primary service providers are in use to reduce susceptibility to the same threats and enhance the resilience of the mission critical business service.

Threats that affect telecommunications services are defined in organizational assessments of risk and include natural disasters, structural failures, cyber or physical attacks, and errors of omission or commission.

Organizations can reduce common susceptibilities by minimizing shared infrastructure among telecommunications service providers and achieving sufficient geographic separation between services.

Organizations may consider using a single service provider in situations where the service provider can provide alternate telecommunications services that meet the separation needs addressed in the risk assessment and meet the critical service requirements.

Obtaining alternate telecommunications services can also reduce the likelihood of sharing a single point of failure with primary telecommunications services.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has identified all primary telecommunication services used to support the critical business service and has obtained an alternate service for each of the identified primary communication services.
  • And, each alternate service is separated from the associated primary telecommunication service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has obtained an alternate service for some of the identified primary telecommunication services.
  • Or, only some of the alternate telecommunication services are separated from the associated primary telecommunication service.

Possible evidence:

  • Listing of all primary and alternate telecommunications providers and associated documentation showing service separation.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-8(3)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:DI-1.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization provide the capability to employ  organization-defined alternative communications protocols in support of maintaining continuity of operations?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Employing alternate communication protocols can minimize common mode failures, particularly threat events that exploit common vulnerabilities and can be incorporated as part of an overall resilience strategy.

Question Intent: This question determines if an organization employs alternative communications protocols in support of maintaining continuity of operations to enhance the resilience of the mission critical business service.

Use multiple sets of technical standards, different technologies, and different architectural patterns to minimize common mode failures, particularly threat events that exploit common vulnerabilities.

Contingency plans and the contingency training or testing associated with those plans incorporate an alternate communications protocol capability as part of establishing resilience in organizational systems.

Switching communications protocols may affect software applications and operational aspects of systems. Organizations should assess the potential side effects of introducing alternate communications protocols prior to implementation.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has developed and documented the capability to employ organization-defined alternative communication protocols for maintaining continuity of operations.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization is in the process of developing and documenting the capability to employ organization-defined alternative communication protocols

Possible evidence:

  • Architectural documentation
  • Contingency plans documenting the use of alternative communication protocols

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-11

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:DI-1.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization identify alternative sources of information for organization-defined essential functions and services and use alternative information source for the execution of essential functions or services on organization-defined systems or system components when the primary source of information is corrupted or unavailable?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: identifying and using alternative information source that is necessary for a mission critical service to operate will allow the service to continue to operate when the primary source of information is not available. Use of information from different sources can also reveal adversary injection or modification.

Question Intent: This question determines if alternative sources of information necessary for the delivery of the mission critical service have been identified and are being used by the organization if the primary information source has been corrupted or is unavailable. 

Actions taken by a system service or function are often driven by the information it receives. Corruption, fabrication, modification, or deletion of that information could impact the ability of the service function to properly carry out its intended actions. 

By having multiple sources of input, the service or function can continue operation if one source is corrupted or no longer available. Use multiple sources for the same information when possible.

It is possible that the alternative sources of information may be less precise or less accurate than the primary source of information. But having such sub-optimal information sources may still provide a sufficient level of quality that the essential service or function can be carried out, even in a degraded or debilitated manner.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Alternative sources for all key information assets that are required for the delivery of the mission critical service or high value system have been identified
  • And, those alternative sources of key information assets are actively being used when necessary.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Alternative sources for some key information assets that are required for the delivery of the mission critical service or high value system have been identified and are being used when necessary
  • Or, alternative sources for all key information assets that are required for the delivery of the mission critical service or high value system have been identified but only some of those sources are available to be used when necessary.

Possible Evidence

  • A documented list of alternative sources for all key information assets required for the delivery of the service.
  • Setup documentation showing that the alternate sources are in place and available for use in a time of stress.
  • Implementation procedures showing how the alternate sources of information assets would be integrated into the system architecture when needed.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-22

questions.title: AN:DI-1.Q5
questions.text: Does the organization use different designs for  organization-defined critical systems or system components to satisfy a common set of requirements or to provide equivalent functionality?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Different designs employed for organization-defined critical systems or system components can present different attack surfaces and thereby enhance the resilience of the mission critical business service.

Question Intent: This question determines if an organization employs different designs for organization-defined critical systems or system components in support of presenting different attack surfaces. 

Within the context of a given architecture, parallel design teams can solve the same problem in different ways, thus producing different attack surfaces.

Design diversity is achieved by supplying the same requirements specification to multiple developers, each of whom is responsible for developing a variant of the system or system component that meets the requirements. 

Variants can be in software design, in hardware design, or in both hardware and a software design. 

Hardware design diversity includes making different decisions about what information to keep in analog form and what information to convert to digital form, transmitting the same information at different times, and introducing delays in sampling (temporal diversity). 

Design diversity is commonly used to support fault tolerance.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented and employed the use of different designs for organization-defined critical systems or system components.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization is in the process of documenting and employing the use of different designs for organization-defined critical systems or system components.

Possible Evidence

  • Design documentation
  • Implementation documentation showing the use of alternate designs.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-22

questions.title: AN:DI-2.Q1
questions.text:
Does the organization:
(a) Allow the use of authentication factors that are different from the primary authentication factors after the number of organization-defined consecutive invalid logon attempts have been exceeded; and
(b) Enforce a limit of consecutive invalid logon attempts through use of the alternative factors by a user during an organization-defined time period.
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The use of alternate authentication factors improves the availability of the mission critical service for a valid user by allowing a user who has inadvertently been locked out to use additional authentication factors to bypass the lockout.

Question Intent: This question determines if alternate authentication factors are in use to assist users who have inadvertently been locked out of their accounts. 

The use of alternate authentication factors supports the objective of availability and allows a user who has inadvertently been locked out to use additional authentication factors to bypass the lockout.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has implemented additional authentication factors that are different from the primary authentication factors
  • And, the additional authentication factors are employed when number of organization-defined consecutive invalid logon attempts have been exceeded
  • And, the organization enforces a limit on the number of consecutive invalid logon attempts during an organization-defined time period.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization is in the process of implementing additional authentication factors that are different from the primary authentication factors
  • Or, the organization has implemented additional authentication factors, but the organization does not enforce a limit on the number of consecutive invalid logon attempts
  • Or, the organization does enforce a limit of consecutive invalid logon attempts during an organization-defined time period but has not implemented additional authentication factors.

Possible Evidence

  • Configuration documentation showing the enforcement of a limit for consecutive invalid logon attempts.
  • Configuration documentation showing the establishment and use of alternate authentication factors after the limit of consecutive invalid logon attempts has been reached.
  • Examples of each that may have been found in regular reviews for items such as excessive invalid logion attempts.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-7(4)

questions.title: AN:DI-3.Q1
questions.text: Has the organization developed a plan for managing supply chain risks associated with organizational systems and system components; and is the plan updated within the organization-defined frequency?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The dependence on products, systems, and services from external providers, as well as the nature of the relationships with those providers, present an increasing level of risk to an organization. Threat actions that may increase security or privacy risks include unauthorized production, the insertion or use of counterfeits, tampering, theft, insertion of malicious software and hardware, and poor manufacturing and development practices in the supply chain.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has developed and documented a plan for managing supply chain risk and if the plan is updated on a scheduled basis. 

Supply chain risks can be endemic or systemic within a system element or component, a system, an organization, a sector, or the Nation. 

Supply chain risk management (SCRM) activities include identifying and assessing risks, determining appropriate risk response actions, developing SCRM plans to document response actions, and monitoring performance against plans. 

The SCRM plan (at the system-level) is implementation specific, providing policy implementation, requirements, constraints, and implications. 

The SCRM plan can either be stand-alone or incorporated into system security and privacy plans. The SCRM plan addresses managing, implementation, and monitoring of SCRM controls and the development/sustainment of systems across the SDLC to support mission and business functions.

Because supply chains can differ significantly across and within organizations, SCRM plans are tailored to the individual program, organizational, and operational contexts. Tailored SCRM plans provide the basis for determining whether a technology, service, system component, or system is fit for purpose and, as such, the controls need to be tailored accordingly. Tailored SCRM plans help organizations focus their resources on the most critical mission and business functions based on mission and business requirements and their risk environment. 

Supply chain risk management plans include an expression of the supply chain risk tolerance for the organization, acceptable supply chain risk mitigation strategies or controls, a process for consistently evaluating and monitoring supply chain risk, approaches for implementing and communicating the plan, a description of and justification for supply chain risk mitigation measures taken, and associated roles and responsibilities. 

Supply chain risk management plans address requirements for developing trustworthy, secure, privacy-protective, and resilient system components and systems, including the application of the security design principles implemented as part of life cycle-based systems security engineering processes (see SA-8).

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • There is documented supply chain risk (SCRM) management for the critical service or HVA system assets.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The plan is in development and partially documented.

Possible Evidence

  • Documented SCRM Plan

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SR-2
  • NIST 800-172: 3.11.7e

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:DP-1.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization use dynamic reconfiguration in organization-defined system components as part of the incident response capability?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The ability to dynamically reconfigure system components, as part of an incident response capability, demonstrates a high level of organizational maturity.

Question Intent: Is the organization mature enough to plan and deploy a solution that dynamically reconfigures system components? What are some examples of how system components might be reconfigured in response to an incident?

Definition of key words with any examples

Dynamic Reconfiguration: Changes to router rules, access control lists, intrusion detection or prevention system parameters, and filter rules for guards or firewalls.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization utilizes dynamic reconfiguration as part of its incident response capability. This capability is documented in a strategy or policy. The document should include the specific time frames for achieving the reconfiguration of systems.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has planned for and/or acquired a dynamic configuration capability but the capability is not in use.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Documents, e.g., a strategy, plan, policy, or concept of operations that describes the dynamic reconfiguration capability.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4(2)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:DP-2.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization implement the security design principle of secure distributed composition in systems or system components as needed?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The principle of secure distributed composition states that the composition of distributed components that enforce the same system security policy result in a system that enforces that policy at least as well as the individual components do. Many of the design principles for secure systems deal with how components can or should interact. The need to create or enable a capability from the composition of distributed components can magnify the relevancy of these principles. In particular, the translation of security policy from a stand-alone to a distributed system or a system-of-systems can have unexpected or emergent results. Communication protocols and distributed data consistency mechanisms help to ensure consistent policy enforcement across a distributed system. To ensure a system-wide level of assurance of correct policy enforcement, the security architecture of a distributed composite system is thoroughly analyzed.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has implemented the security design principle of secure distributed composition, as required, for systems or system components.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • For systems or system components where the principle of secure distributed composition is applicable, the organization has conducted a thorough analysis of the security architecture to ensure that individually, and collectively, the system components enforce a defined security policy. This analysis, along with relevant control implementation details, should be documented in a System Security Plan (SSP) or similar document.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has conducted a preliminary analysis of the security architecture but has not implemented the relevant controls to ensure that individually, and collectively, the system components enforce a defined security policy.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Documented security architecture analysis and relevant control implementation details.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SA-8(17)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q1
questions.text: Is there a documented policy for asset management?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should have a documented policy for asset management as it establishes organizational expectations for planning and performing the asset management process and it also communicates those expectations to the organization.

Question Intent: This question determines if a policy for performing asset management activities exists.

A policy is a written communication from the organization’s senior management to employees.

The asset management policy should address:

  • responsibility, authority, ownership, and the requirement to perform asset management activities
  • establishment of procedures, standards, and guidelines
  • establishing and maintaining an asset inventory
  • managing access to assets
  • categorizing, safeguarding, and disposing of information assets
  • measuring adherence to policy, exceptions granted, and policy violations
  • compliance with legal, regulatory, contractual, and government obligations

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented policy for performing asset management.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A policy is in development and partially documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • A Standard Operating Procedure for Asset Management or Other relevant organizational policy covering asset management.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: AM:MIL2.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-1

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q19
questions.text: Does the organization review and update the following at least once each year: IM information management plan, media relations policy, information disclosure policy, information classification schema, data retention plan, and acceptable use policy?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizational plans should be reviewed at a minimum annually to ensure they are kept current.

Question Intent: This question determines whether organizational plans and policies pertaining to incident management are reviewed at least once a year to identify and implement updates.  

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization reviews all of its policies and plans pertaining to incident management at least once a year to identify and implement updates.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization reviews some of its policies and plans pertaining to incident management at least once a year to identify and implement updates.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Document review history or correspondence that substantiates review activities have occurred at least yearly for organizational incident management plans and policies.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 1.2.2.12 Quality.
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PS-7, PM-1, PM-2

questions.title: AN:GV-3.Q1
questions.text: Are cybersecurity requirements (rules, laws, regulations, policies, etc.)  managed throughout the system's entire life cycle?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Legal and regulatory requirements regarding cybersecurity sometimes have time-based retention requirements, therefore data handling, retention, and disposal should be tracked to comply with such regulations.

Question Intent: This question determines if organizational requirements are managed throughout their entire lifecycle.

Requirements should be tracked to ensure they are kept current and relevant to the organization. However, there may be special considerations for certain legal and regulatory requirements that organizations also much be aware of.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization manages all requirements throughout their entire life cycle by using a standardized process to monitor requirements.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization manages high-importance requirements throughout their entire life cycle, though not all organizational requirements are tracked.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  •  Requirements Traceability Matrix

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: All -1 controls from all security control families, as 1b of each -1 control will address this per each policy.

questions.title: AN:GV-4.Q1
questions.text: Is there adequate funding to perform asset management activities as planned?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Funding is an indication of higher-level management support and sponsorship of asset management activities.

Question Intent: This question determines if adequate funding has been provided for asset management activities. The intent of the question is to evaluate the completeness of the funding, not the completeness of the plan.

Funding should be available to support the proper oversight, execution, and maintenance of asset management activities.

Considerations for funding planned asset management activities include:

  • defining funding needs
  • establishing a budget
  • resolving funding gaps
  • funding the process activities including staffing, tools, training, etc.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Adequate funding has been provided to perform all planned asset management activities.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The planned activities have only been partially funded.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Attestation from stakeholders regarding funding for asset management activities.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: AM:MIL3.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SA-2, PM-3, PM-7, PM-9, PM-10, PM-11

questions.title: AN:RA-1.Q1
questions.text: Has responsibility for monitoring sources of threat information been assigned?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Threat monitoring is an integral part of establishing a common operating picture for the organization.

Question Intent: This question determines if the responsibility for monitoring sources of threat information has been assigned. Effective threat monitoring requires the assignment of responsibility for threat monitoring activities.

Threat monitoring is a process of data collection and distribution with the purpose of providing timely, accurate, complete, and relevant information about the organization’s current threat environment.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The responsibility for monitoring all sources of threat information relevant to the critical service has been assigned.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The responsibility for monitoring some sources of threat information has been assigned.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Work roles or position descriptions
  • Routine/recurring reports on threat information

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: SA:G1.Q1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-5, PM-15, PM-16

questions.title: AN:RA-2.Q1
questions.text: Do personnel perform the threat monitoring activities on a routine basis?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The team should look for evidence of regular monitoring of a variety of security, news, and other trusted sites for information related to computing technologies, attacks, and threats, and for socio-political, economic, or legal information related to malicious computer security events and incidents.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has designated an individual or team to conduct information monitoring on a regular basis.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Organization has personnel assigned to preform monitoring on a routine/regular basis.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Personnel are not assigned, but monitoring is still being conducted by unassigned personnel. Monitoring is being conducted on an irregular basis.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Demonstrations of research and monitoring of identified websites
  • Records of gathered information
  • List of criteria for what to monitor

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 3.3.1.10
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-3, SI-5, PM-12, PM-16

questions.title: AN:RA-3.Q1
questions.text: Have impact areas been identified, such as reputation, financial health, and regulatory compliance?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizational impact areas identify the categories where realized risk may have meaningful and disruptive consequences. Impact areas reflect what is important to the organization and to the accomplishment of its mission. Organizational impact areas help identify how realized risk may affect the organization.

Question Intent: This question determines if impact areas have been identified, such as reputation, financial health, and regulatory compliance.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • This must be true to mark a Yes.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • There are no criteria for partial implementation. (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Business impact analysis
  • Disaster recovery plan
  • Cybersecurity incident response plan

questions.title: AN:RA-4.Q1
questions.text: Are operational risks that could affect delivery of the critical service identified?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: From the sources and categories of risk established in G1.Q1 and G1.Q2, specific risks that affect the delivery of the critical service should be identified. The organization should determine the effect on the service that could result from the realization of risk at the asset level.

Question Intent: This question determines if operational risks that could affect delivery of the critical service are identified.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Operational risks that could affect delivery of the critical service are identified and documented.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Operational risks that could affect delivery of the critical service are being identified and are partially documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • List of operational risks by service

questions.title: AN:SC-1.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization have a formal written supply chain risk management strategy or plan?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Having a documented strategy or plan is critical for operationalizing supply chain risk management activities.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has developed an organization-wide strategy or plan for managing supply chain risks.

Supply chain risk management includes considerations of the security and privacy risks associated with the development, acquisition, maintenance, and disposal of systems, system components, and system services.

The supply chain risk management strategy can be incorporated into the organization's overarching risk management strategy and can guide and inform supply chain policies and system-level supply chain risk management plans.

An organization-wide supply chain risk management strategy includes:

  •  a concise definition of the organization’s supply chain risk appetite and tolerance,
  • lists acceptable supply chain risk mitigation strategies or controls,
  • definition of processes for the continuous evaluation and monitoring of supply chain risk,
  • definition of approaches for implementing and communicating the supply chain risk management strategy, and
  • delineation of roles and responsibilities for performing supply chain risk management functions.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a formal written supply chain risk management strategy or plan that is either its own document or is incorporated into the organization’s overarching risk management strategy.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization does not have a formal written supply chain risk management strategy or plan and the organization’s overarching risk management strategy does not adequately address supply chain risk management.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • A document containing the organizations Supply Chain Risk Management strategy or plan, a section from an organizational risk management strategy that addresses how supply chain risk management is employed within the organization.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SR-1, SR-2, PM-30

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The responsibility for monitoring the performance of some external entities has been assigned

questions.title: AN:SC-3.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization have a plan for managing incidents that involve suppliers and third-party providers?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizational incident management plans enable identified risks to be mitigated, threats to be contained, and provide a playbook on how to recover from an attack and other interruptions to business operations. Knowing what resources an organization has available to them during an incident allows them to recover more quickly, hence, this question directly gets at organizational resiliency.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has a documented plan for managing incidents.

  • The organization’s plan for managing incidents should address the identification, analysis, and response to an incident.
  • An event is one or more occurrences that affect organizational assets and have the potential to disrupt operations.
  • An incident significantly impacts the critical service and requires the organization to respond to prevent or limit impact to the critical service and the organization.
  • An incident may result from an event or a series of events that requires a response that is beyond standard operating procedures for managing events.
  • An incident may result from an event or a series of events that requires a response that is beyond standard operating procedures for managing events.
  • The organization must plan for how it will:
  • identify events and incidents
  • analyze these events and incidents and determine an appropriate response
  • develop declaration criteria
  • respond to incidents
  • communicate incident information to stakeholders
  • staff the plan to meet plan objectives 
  • structure the incident management staff (including roles and responsibilities) 
  • train staff to identify, analyze, and respond to incidents

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • There is a documented plan for managing incidents relevant to the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A plan is in development and partially documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Incident management plan, contingency plan

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, CP-4, IR-3, IR-4, IR-6, IR-8, IR-9

Question Intent: To determine if a baseline of network operations for all systems and assets that support the critical service has been established.

  • Baseline configurations include information about information system components, network topology, and the logical placement of those components within the system architecture.
  • System information exchanges include connections via leased lines or virtual private networks, connections to Internet service providers, database sharing or exchanges of database transaction information, connections and exchanges with cloud services, exchanges via web-based services, or exchanges of files via file transfer protocols, network protocols (e.g., IPv4, IPv6), email, or other organization-to-organization communications.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Cloud service management console

questions.text: Does the organization have a documented continuous monitoring strategy?

Importance: Continuous monitoring of information systems and organizations is used to determine the ongoing effectiveness of controls, changes in information systems and environments of operation, and the state of security and privacy organization wide. The terms “continuous” and “ongoing” imply that organizations assess and monitor their controls and risks at a frequency sufficient to support risk-based decisions.

Develop a system-level continuous monitoring strategy and implement continuous monitoring in accordance with the organization-level continuous monitoring strategy

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

questions.title: WI:AE-5.Q1
questions.text: Have criteria for the declaration of an incident been established?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Declaration criteria guides the organization in determining when to declare an incident (particularly if incident declaration is not immediately apparent).

Question Intent: To determine if criteria for the declaration of incidents are established.

Example incident declaration criteria:

  • Is the event isolated?
  • Predefined thresholds of impact.
  • Did past occurrences of the event result in an incident declaration?
  • Is the impact of the event imminent or immediate?
  • Is the organization already suffering some effects from the event?
  • Is the life or safety of people at risk?
  • Is the integrity and operability of a facility at risk?
  • Is the integrity and operability of a high-value service or system at risk?
  • Does the event constitute fraud or theft?
  • Are there impacts, such as damage to the organization’s reputation?
  • Is there a potential legal infraction?

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented list of criteria for the declaration of incidents.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A documented list of criteria is in development and partially documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Standard Operating Procedures for Incident Response, Incident Management Plan, Incident Response Plan, Information Security Policy.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: IM:G3.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4, IR-5, IR-8

questions.title: WI:AM-1.Q1
questions.text: The inventory of assets includes: (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: A critical cyber asset inventory would include at minimum the network addresses, machine names, purpose of each service and the asset owner responsible for each device. It may also include every device with an IP address, including servers, desktops, network equipment (routers, switches, firewalls, etc.), printers, storage area networks, VOIP, multi-home addresses, virtual addresses, mobile phones, tablets, laptops, and other portable devices that store or process data.

Question Intent: To determine whether the inventory of assets includes all organization devices.

Programmable electronic devices and communication networks, including hardware, software, and data. Data and cabling are considered to exist within the framework of the cyber asset and there are not separate cyber assets.

Network – Information Service(s) implemented with a collection of interconnected components. Such components may include routers, hubs, cabling, telecommunications controllers, key distribution centers, and technical control devices.

Application – A digital application software program hosted by an information Service that functions and is operated by means of a computer, with the purpose of supporting functions needed by an asset owner.

Individuals – The key IT and security professionals within the organization. This would include:

  • Administrators
  • Users
  • Third-party contractors of the CCS

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All listed applicable assets are included in the inventory.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some, not all, listed applicable assets are included in the inventory.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Updated asset inventory list
  • Order lists for purchased assets

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-8, PM-5

Importance: To be effective, all personnel within an organization must receive cybersecurity training, including those involved in day-to-day operations. Adversaries may target organizations in a variety of ways, including through means of physical facilities access using social engineering, to combat this all employees should receive cybersecurity training specific to their role, whenever practical or possible.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

Importance: Privileged users should receive additional training that informs them of the security considerations for their specific roles and responsibilities.

Question Intent: To determine if privileged users have been trained in their specific roles and responsibilities.

Role-based security training is provided to privileged users with assigned security roles and responsibilities:

  • Before authorizing their access to the information system or before they perform their assigned duties
  • When required by information system changes
  • Periodically (frequency defined by the organization) thereafter

Comprehensive role-based training addresses management, operational, and technical roles and responsibilities.

Role-based security training also applies to contractors providing services.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All privileged users that support the critical service have been trained in their specific roles and responsibilities.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

questions.title: WI:DS-2.Q1
questions.text: Select all of the factors the organization employs when determining protection solutions for data in transit: (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: There are several laws or regulations that can influence the way an organization protects data-in-transit, some of these may make the protection of such information mandatory.

Question Intent: determine what factors the organization uses to guide the implementation of protection solutions for data-in-transit.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization can identify the factors that they consider when determining protection solutions for data-in-transit.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization determines protection solutions for data-in-transit on an ad hoc basis.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Organizational policy that covers data security or data protection for data-in-transit.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-8, SC-11, SC-12

questions.title: WI:DS-3.Q1
questions.text: Is adherence to information asset disposal guidelines monitored and enforced?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: information asset disposal guidelines are meaningless if those in the organization do not abide by them, therefore there should be monitoring mechanisms in place to gauge the efficacy of the guidelines.

Question Intent: To determine if adherence to information asset disposal guidelines is monitored and enforced.

The organization should provide oversight, such as audits or spot-check inspections to ensure that the approved methods of information disposal are being followed. Definition of any key words with examples

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization monitors and enforces adherence to disposal guidelines for all information assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Guidelines are in development and partially documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence:

  • Documentation of asset disposal procedures, such as paper logs or a ticketing system
  • Incident reports where information asset disposal guidelines were violated.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: AM:G6.Q7
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-8, MP-6, PE-16

questions.title: WI:DS-4.Q1
questions.text: Does the organization perform capacity planning to ensure availability of the critical service?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: capacity management and planning is critical to ensure that the availability of organizational systems is maintained. Organizations may need to anticipate degraded operations during contingency operations and factor such degradation into capacity planning.

Question Intent: determine the kinds of capacity management and planning that the organization performs.

  • The organization conducts capacity planning so that necessary capacity for information processing, telecommunications, and environmental support exists, including during contingency operations.
  • Capacity planning is needed because different types of threats (e.g., natural disasters, targeted cyber attacks) can result in a reduction of the available processing, telecommunications, and support services originally intended to support the organizational missions/business functions.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization performs formal capacity planning activities and documents them in writing.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization performs capacity planning in an ad hoc manner and documents it in writing.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Incident management plans or business continuity plans that cover capacity management; business impact analysis

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-4, CP-2, SC-5
