Question Intent: To determine if incident declaration criteria are based on established frameworks, standards, guidelines, or directives.

Implement an incident handling capability for incidents that is consistent with the incident response plan and includes preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery.

  • Documented policy and procedures for declaring an incident are implemented.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Documented policy and procedures for declaring an incident are in the process of being implemented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

  • SSP
  • Previous incident reports

questions.title: WI:AE-2.Q2
questions.text: Are incidents analyzed to determine if they are related to other incidents?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Sometimes, a threat event, such as a hostile cyber-attack, can only be observed by bringing together information from different sources, including various reports and reporting procedures established by organizations. Documenting incidents includes maintaining records about each incident, the status of the incident, and other pertinent information necessary for forensics as well as evaluating incident details, trends, and handling.

Question Intent: To determine if incidents are analyzed for their relationship to other incidents and events.

Analysis should be conducted to determine whether the incident correlates to other events and incidents (correlation may indicate larger issues, problems, or incidents). 

Criteria for Full Implementation Response:

  • The organization analyzes all incidents relevant to the critical service to determine if they are related to other events and incidents.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response:  

  • The organization analyzes some incidents.  

Possible evidence: Any kind of incident response dashboard that demonstrates incident correlation features or notes indicating that a manual review of the incident has considered the incidents relationship to other events and incidents.

Reference to standards/source assessments: CRR IM:G2.Q4

questions.title: WI:DS-2.Q2
questions.text: In what situations does the organization protect data in transit: (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Data-in-transit should always be protected, regardless of whether the data is travelling exclusively on organization-owned networks.

Question Intent: Determine in what environments the organization protects data-in-transit:

  • Protecting the confidentiality and integrity of transmitted information applies to internal and external networks as well as any system components that can transmit information, including servers, notebook computers, desktop computers, mobile devices, printers, copiers, scanners, facsimile machines, and radios.
  • Unprotected communication paths are exposed to the possibility of interception and modification. Protecting the confidentiality and integrity of information can be accomplished by physical or logical means,
  • Physical protection can be achieved by using protected distribution systems. A protected distribution system is a wireline or fiber-optics telecommunications system that includes terminals and adequate electromagnetic, acoustical, electrical, and physical controls to permit its use for the unencrypted transmission of critical or secure information.
  • Logical protection can be achieved by employing encryption techniques.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization protects data-in-transit in all the situations listed

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization protects data-in-transit in some of the situations listed
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Organizational policy regarding data protection mechanisms, such as VPN use and encryption.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-8, SC-11, SC-12

options.text: Data in transit is not protected

Importance: Disposal of information assets should utilize mechanisms with the strength and integrity commensurate with the security category or classification of the information. Often, this practice is guided by a regulatory requirement or policy within the organization.

Question Intent: to determine what guidelines inform the organizations data handling and disposal practices for information assets.

Opportunities for compromise during disposal affect physical and logical data, including system documentation in paper-based or digital files; shipping and delivery documentation; memory sticks with software code; or complete routers or servers that include permanent media, which contain sensitive or proprietary information.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization follows either a Formal Standard (e.g., NIST 800-88) or Management Directive to determine how information assets are to be disposed of.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization determines how information assets are to be disposed of on an ad hoc basis.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Standard Operating Procedure, management directive, or Organizational Policy pertaining to data handling that covers disposal.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-8, MP-6, PE-16

questions.title: WI:DE-1.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization prevent the discovery of specific system components that represent a managed interface?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Preventing the discovery of system components representing a managed interface helps protect network addresses of those components from discovery through common tools and techniques used to identify devices on networks.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization prevents discovery of system components representing managed interfaces.

Network addresses that are not available for discovery will require prior knowledge for access.

Preventing the discovery of components and devices can be accomplished by

  • Not publishing network addresses
  • Using network address translation
  • Not entering the addresses in domain name systems,
  • Periodically change network addresses

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Techniques are employed to prevent the discovery of all critical service/HVA system components representing a managed interface.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Techniques are employed to prevent the discovery of some critical service/HVA system components representing a managed interface.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the setup and implementation of the various methods employed to prevent the discovery of system components representing a managed interface.

questions.title: WI:DE-2.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization employ a detonation chamber capability within organization-defined system, system component, or locations?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Detonation chambers, also known as dynamic execution environments, allow organizations to open email attachments, execute untrusted or suspicious applications, and execute Universal Resource Locator (URL) requests in the safety of an isolated environment or a virtualized sandbox

Question Intent: To determine if a detonation chamber capability is implemented to protect the critical service/HVA environment.

  • Protected and isolated execution environments provide a means of determining whether the associated attachments or applications contain malicious code.
  • While related to the concept of deception nets, the employment of detonation chambers is not intended to maintain a long-term environment in which adversaries can operate and their actions can be observed. Rather, detonation chambers are intended to quickly identify malicious code and either reduce the likelihood that the code is propagated to user operational environments or prevent such propagation completely.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Detonation chambers have been developed, documented, and implemented to protect the critical service or HVA environment.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Detonation chambers are in development, partially documented and not fully implemented.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the setup and implementation of the detonation chamber used to protect the critical service/HVA.
  • Configuration and status information showing the implementation and operational status of the detonation chamber.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-44

questions.title: WI:DP-5.Q2
questions.text: Are lessons learned from incident management used to improve event detection capabilities?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Lessons learned from incident management can be leveraged to improve event detection capabilities. Indicators of compromise, malware signatures, and other information can be derived from historical incidents to inform future event detection efforts. Incidents can also reveal inefficiencies in the incident management process, therefore lessons learned can provide invaluable data on how the organization handles incidents.

Question Intent: The question seeks to determine if organizations conduct a lessons-learned review after incidents occur, and then whether the organization utilizes lessons learned to inform their event detection capabilities.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization always performs lessons learned in accordance with incident management activities, and then uses the information obtained from lessons learned to improve event detection capabilities.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization sometimes performs lessons learned in accordance with incident management activities, and then uses the information obtained from lessons learned to improve event detection capabilities.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Incident response plan that defines the process by which lessons learned from security incidents inform event detection capabilities.

  • Disable an access account that is no longer valid

NOTE: This capability includes both logical and physical access to assets.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Access privileges are modified as a result of reviews for some assets.

questions.title: WI:AC-3.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization verify the identity of users and devices prior to authorizing access?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Each action in a system needs to be associated with a specific individual and/or device so that if questions arise about an activity, investigators know exactly who or what is responsible for performing that activity.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization verifies the identity users and devices prior to authorizing access. This question seeks to determine if an organization is safeguarding against impersonation or substitution.

For people, identity verification might include verification of fingerprints, passports, or other forms of identification. Verification of devices might include checks of serial numbers or cryptographic certificates.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All users and devices are verified before access is authorized.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some users and devices are verified before access is authorized. Users and devices with access to sensitive data or systems must be verified.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Device inventory
  • User inventory
  • Procurement records
  • Human resources background checks or checklists
  • Lists of contractors or other third parties with access

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IA-2, IA-12

questions.title: WI:AC-4.Q2
questions.text: Are users authenticated before establishing connections to the system?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Unique identifiers are fundamental to an organization’s ability to associate actions with specific individuals and assets. Unique identifiers are just the first part in associating identity to activities, however. The organization also must ensure that the people ore devices using a given identifier really are who or what they claim to be. The process of verifying identity is also called authentication.

Question Intent: To determine whether users are authenticated before connecting to the system.

Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a user or device.

Authorization is the process of verifying and controlling what resources a user has access to.

Authenticators are typically grouped into three “factors:” knowledge, possession, and inherence (something you know, something you have, and something you are). At least one of these factors, preferably more, must be used to verify identity. Once identity is verified, the individual has the level of access authorized for that identity.

The system must challenge a user prior to providing access to any element except the authentication module.

This control applies to contractors and third parties as well as the organization’s employees. Users may be authenticated by a trusted third party rather than directly by the organization.

Anonymous access to public-facing websites or document repositories is not included under this control if all content at those locations is intended for public consumption.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All users are authenticated before establishing connections to the system.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Partial implementation of this control is not allowed.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • User inventory
  • Identity and Access Management solution user records
  • Employee lists
  • Lists of contractors or other third parties with access

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • HVA
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-7, AC-9, AC-11, AC-12, AC-14, IA-1, IA-2, IA-4, IA-5, IA-8, IA-9, IA-10, IA-11

questions.title: WI:IP-8.Q2
questions.text: Have external stakeholders to whom protection effectiveness information must be conveyed  (such as emergency management personnel, regulatory, and information sharing organizations) been identified?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Stakeholders such as emergency management personnel or regulatory officials need to understand the risks to the assets at the organization. Some information distribution may be required by law or regulation. Before prompt and thorough communication can occur, those stakeholders must be identified.

Question Intent: To determine if external stakeholders who must receive information on protection technology effectiveness have been identified.

External stakeholders are identified to

  • Improve communications
  • Promote threat awareness
  • Ensure that the organization is meeting legal and regulatory obligations

External stakeholders may have a stated role in communication plans or in the service continuity plans of the organization.

Examples of external stakeholders include:

  • First responders including law enforcement, fire, and medical
  • Media including newspaper, television, radio, and internet
  • Customers, business partners, and upstream suppliers
  • Local, state, and federal emergency management
  • Local utilities such as power, gas, telecommunications, and water
  • Legal, regulatory, and governing agencies

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All external stakeholders who must receive protection technology effectiveness communication have been identified and documented.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some external stakeholders have been identified and documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • List of external stakeholders and alternates
  • Stakeholder contact information

Reference to standards/source assessments

questions.title: WI:IP-9.Q2
questions.text: The organization has a defined incident response plan for handling cyber incidents, which (at a minimum) contains: (Select one)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: An incident response plan provides the organization with a roadmap for implementing its incident response capability. It is important that organizations develop and implement a coordinated approach to incident response.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization has a documented plan for handling cyber incidents.

  • The organization’s plan for managing incidents should address the identification, analysis, and response to an incident.
  • An event is one or more occurrences that affect organizational assets and have the potential to disrupt operations.
  • An incident significantly impacts the mission critical service and requires the organization to respond to prevent or limit impact to the critical service and the organization.
  • An incident may result from an event or a series of events that requires a response that is beyond standard operating procedures for managing events.
  • An effective incident handling capability includes coordination among many organizational entities (e.g., mission or business owners, system owners, authorizing officials, human resources offices, physical security offices, personnel security offices, legal departments, risk executive [function], operations personnel, procurement offices).
  • The organization must plan for how it will:
  • identify events and incidents
  • analyze these events and incidents and determine an appropriate response
  • develop incident declaration criteria
  • respond to incidents
  • communicate incident information to stakeholders
  • staff the plan to meet plan objectives
  • structure the incident management staff (including roles and responsibilities)
  • train staff to identify, analyze, and respond to incidents

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • There are documented procedures and assigned roles for cybersecurity incident response.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Documented procedures but no assigned roles for cybersecurity incident response
  • Or, assigned roles for cybersecurity incident response but no documented procedures.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Documented incident response plan for handling cyber incidents, which contains documented procedures and assigned roles for cybersecurity incident response.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: Q.25.1

options.text: Documented procedures but no assigned roles
Assigned roles but no documented procedures

questions.title: WI:IP-10.Q2
questions.text: How often does the organization test business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities that support the critical service?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Business continuity and DR capabilities require frequent testing to confirm that systems function properly and that staff thoroughly understand their roles. Untested systems cannot be fully relied upon.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization tests its business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities on a regular basis. The service continuity test schedule should meet the requirements of the mission critical service.

  • The tests should establish the viability, accuracy, and completeness of the plan.
  • The tests should also provide information about the organization’s level of preparedness.
  • The tests are performed under conditions established by the organization, and the results of the test should be recorded and documented.
  • Methods for testing contingency plans to determine the effectiveness of the plans and identify potential weaknesses include checklists, walk-through and tabletop exercises, simulations (parallel or full interrupt), and comprehensive exercises.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities are tested at least annually.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • All business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities activities are tested at a frequency of greater than once a year but at least every 2 years.
  • Or, some business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities are tested at least annually.

Possible evidence

  • Documented test results

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: Q.25.1

options.text: The organization does not test business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities

questions.title: WI:IP-11.Q2
questions.text: Does HR verify employee roles and responsibilities prior to system access being granted?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Since system access is determined by an employee’s roles and responsibilities, HR should verify those roles prior to them being implemented in the system .

Question Intent: To determine whether HR verifies employee roles and responsibilities prior to system access being granted.

HR teams should check with new hires’ managers prior to notifying the identity and access management team about what rights to assign the employee. Anticipate roles and projects often can change in the interval between initial hiring and actual account creation. The verification helps maintain the principle of least privilege in the organization.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • HR follows a documented process for reviewing the roles and responsibilities of all new hires before submitting a request to grant them access to the system.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • HR follows a documented process for reviewing the roles and responsibilities of some new hires.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Documented policies or procedures for personnel onboarding
  • Emails, checklists, or other documents related to onboarding.

questions.title: WI:MA-1.Q2
questions.text: Is the maintenance and repair of assets performed and logged in a timely manner?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Controlling system maintenance addresses the information security aspects of the system maintenance program and applies to all types of maintenance to system components conducted by local or nonlocal entities.

Question Intent: To determine if the maintenance and repair of assets are performed and logged in a timely manner.

  • Organizations should schedule, perform, document, and review records of maintenance and repairs on information system components.
  • Produce up-to date, accurate, and complete records of all maintenance, repair, and replacement actions requested, scheduled, in process, and completed.
  • Both preventative and predictive maintenance activities should be employed where feasible to help address potential failures either before they occur or before they develop into major defects.
  • All maintenance activities, whether performed on site or remotely, should be approved and monitored.
  • A process for authorizing maintenance personnel and for keeping a list of authorized personnel or maintenance organizations should be established.
  • The use of automated mechanisms to manage and control system maintenance programs and activities helps to ensure the generation of timely, accurate, complete, and consistent maintenance records

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The maintenance and repair of all assets that support the critical service/HVA environment are performed and logged in a timely manner.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The maintenance and repair of some assets that support the critical service/HVA environment are performed and logged in a timely manner.

Possible evidence

  • Maintenance records or logs detailing the maintenance and repair of critical service/HVA system components/assets.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR CCM:G2.Q9, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 MA-2, MA-3, MA-5, MA-6

questions.title: WI:NP-1.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization use one-time passwords or cryptographic nonces?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: One-time passwords and cryptographic nonces help implement the principal of non-persistence and thereby make it more difficult for an adversary to exploit organizational systems or operating environments.

Question Intent: To determine if one-time passwords and/or cryptographic nonces are implemented for the critical service/HVA.

  • In cryptography, a nonce (number once) is an arbitrary number that can be used just once in a cryptographic communication.
  • It is often a random or pseudo-random number issued in an authentication protocol to ensure that old communications cannot be reused in replay attacks.
  • A one-time password is a password that is valid for only one login session or transaction, on a computer system or other digital device.
  • A one-time password is not vulnerable to replay attacks and is more secure than a static password, especially a user-created password, which can be weak and/or reused across multiple accounts.
  • Examples:
  • Security tokens: microprocessor-based smart cards or pocket-size key fobs that produce a numeric or alphanumeric code to authenticate access
  • Mobile device applications, such as Google or Microsoft authenticator applications

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • One-time passwords and/or cryptographic nonces are implemented as part of the authentication process for all technology assets that are part of the critical service/HVA environment.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • One-time passwords and/or cryptographic nonces are in development and partially implemented.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the implementation and configuration of one-time passwords and/or cryptographic nonces for the critical service/HVA environment.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-160 Vol. 2 Examples, NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-4(1), AU-9(2), AU-9(7)

questions.title: WI:NP-2.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization take measures to automatically terminate a user session when organization-defined conditions or trigger events requiring session disconnect are met?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: An organization takes measures to automatically terminate a user session degrade an adversary’s ability to maintain a covert presence and to help prevent the spread or intended impact of attacks.

Question Intent: Whether the organization automatically terminates user sessions when defined conditions are met.

Session termination
  • Session termination addresses the termination of user-initiated logical sessions. This is in contrast to the termination of network connections associated with communications sessions (i.e., network disconnect).
  • A logical session (for local, network, and remote access) is initiated whenever a user (or process acting on behalf of a user) accesses an organizational system.
  • Such user sessions can be terminated without terminating network sessions. Session termination ends all processes associated with a user’s logical session except for those processes that are specifically created by the user (i.e., session owner) to continue after the session is terminated.
  • Conditions or trigger events that require automatic termination of the session include
  • Organization-defined periods of user inactivity,
  • Targeted responses to certain types of incidents, or
  • Time-of-day restrictions on system use.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Measures are employed to automatically terminate all user sessions established to the system when organization-defined conditions requiring session termination are met.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Measures are employed to automatically terminate some user sessions established to the system when organization-defined conditions requiring session termination are met.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the implementation and configuration of the ability to automatically terminate all user sessions established to the critical service/HVA environment when organization-defined conditions are met
  • A documented list of organization-defined conditions or trigger events that are used to guide when user sessions are terminated.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-12

questions.title: WI:NP-3.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization provide physical and/or logical disconnect of collaborative computing devices in a manner that supports ease of use?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Failing to disconnect from collaborative computing devices can result in subsequent compromises of organizational information.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization provides a method for the physical and/or logical disconnection of collaborative computing devices.

Discussion (NIST 800-53): Failing to disconnect from collaborative computing devices can result in subsequent compromises of organizational information. Providing easy methods to disconnect from such devices after a collaborative computing session ensures that participants carry out the disconnect activity without having to go through complex and tedious procedures. Disconnect from collaborative computing devices can be manual or automatic.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization provides a method (manual or automatic) for the physical and/or logical disconnect of all collaborative computing devices used to support the critical service/HVA environment.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization provides a method (manual or automatic) for the physical and/or logical disconnect of some collaborative computing devices used to support the critical service/HVA environment.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the implementation and configuration of the methods or mechanisms implemented for the physical and/or logical disconnect of all collaborative computing devices used to support the critical service/HVA environment.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53: SC-15(1)

questions.title: WI:PR-1.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization provide separate processing domains to enable finer-grained allocation of user privileges?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Use of separate processing domains complicates attackers’ ability to move laterally within the system.

Question Intent: To assess whether the organization provides separate processing domains to enable finer-grained allocation of user privileges.

Discussion: Providing separate processing domains for finer-grained allocation of user privileges includes using virtualization techniques to permit additional user privileges within a virtual machine while restricting privileges to other virtual machines or to the underlying physical machine, implementing separate physical domains, and employing hardware or software domain separation mechanisms.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Requirements for separate processing domains are identified; and
  • Separate processing domains are implemented (either physical or virtual separation)

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Only Full or No Implementation. No Partial Implementation.

Possible evidence

  • System design documentation
  • System configuration settings and associated documentation
  • Enterprise security architecture documentation
  • System segmentation architecture implementing separate physical domains, employing hardware or software domain separation mechanisms

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53, AC-6(4)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: WI:PR-2.Q2
questions.text: What types of access control does the organization employ? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Different methods of access control provide varying degrees of assurance that only those who strictly require access actually have it. Particularly critical systems require access control solutions that provide a high level of assurance.

Question Intent: Determine what types of access control the organization employs.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Depending on access control employed the following should be assessed for full implementation:

For MAC:

  • The organization defines mandatory access control policy enforced over the set of covered subjects; and
  • The organization defines mandatory access control policy enforced over the set of covered objects; and
  • The subjects to be explicitly granted privileges are defined; and
  • The privileges to be explicitly granted to subjects are defined.

For RBAC:

  • The organization defines roles upon which to base control of access are defined; and
  • Organizational users authorized to assume roles are defined.

For ABAC:

  • Attributes to assume access permissions are defined.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • This practice is either Fully Implemented or Not Implemented. No Partial Implementation.

Possible evidence

  • Access control policy; role-based access control policies; procedures addressing access enforcement; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; list of roles, users, and associated privileges required to control system access; system audit records; system security plan; privacy plan; list of subjects and objects (i.e., users and resources) requiring enforcement of attribute-based access control policies; list of subjects and objects (i.e., users and resources) requiring enforcement of mandatory access control policies.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • See AC-3(7), AC-3(3), AC-3(13), AC-6(1)

questions.title: WI:PR-3.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization create, activate, manage, and deactivate organization-defined system accounts dynamically?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Dynamic account creation reduces the attack surface of an organization, particularly of privileged accounts, by creating accounts only for limited periods of time and to perform limited roles.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization dynamically provisions accounts.

Examples would include temporary admin accounts or one-time passwords on admin accounts.

Approaches for dynamically creating, activating, managing, and deactivating system accounts rely on automatically provisioning the accounts at runtime for entities that were previously unknown. Organizations plan for the dynamic management, creation, activation, and deactivation of system accounts by establishing trust relationships, business rules, and mechanisms with appropriate authorities to validate related authorizations and privileges.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All System accounts used in support of the critical service are dynamically provisioned (created, activated, managed, and deactivated)

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some system accounts used in support of the critical service are dynamically provisioned.

Possible evidence

  • Access control policy; procedures addressing account management; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; system-generated list of system accounts; system audit records; system security plan.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-2(8)

questions.title: WI:PT-1.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization have documented procedures that implement the audit/log policy?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Having formal written procedures that implement the audit/log policy helps ensure that the policy will be carried out exactly as desired.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization has formal written procedures that implement the audit/log policy.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a formal written procedure that implements the audit/log management policy and explains how it is to be carried out.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has a formal written procedure that implements only parts of the audit/log management policy OR fails to provide sufficient guidelines for implementing the policy to fully manage and protect audit logs.

Possible evidence

  • Procedures covering implementation of audit/log management policy.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53 Rev.4 AU Family

questions.title: WI:PT-2.Q2
questions.text: Has the organization implemented controls to protect and restrict the use of removable media in accordance with policy?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The organization should protect its information systems including from possible risks introduced via removable media.

Question Intent: To determine if controls have been implemented to protect and restrict the use of removable media in accordance with policy.

  • Organizations may restrict user access to removable media to defined personnel or roles.
  • Organizations may restrict the use of certain types of removable media.
  • Physically controlling information system media includes:
  • Conducting inventories
  • Ensuring procedures are in place to allow individuals to check out and return media to the media library
  • Maintaining accountability for all stored media
  • The type of media storage should be appropriate for the security category and/or classification of the information residing on the media.
  • Media should be protected during transport outside of controlled areas using established safeguards. Safeguards can include:
  • Locked containers
  • Encryption

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Controls have been implemented to protect and restrict the use of removable media on all assets that support the critical service

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Controls have been implemented to protect and restrict the use of removable media on some assets that support the critical service.

Possible evidence

  • System media protection policy; system use policy; procedures addressing media usage restrictions; rules of behavior; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; audit records; system security plan

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR CM:G2.Q7
  • NIST 800-53 Rev.4 MP-2, MP-4, MP-5, MP-7:

questions.title: WI:PT-4.Q2
questions.text: Has the organization divided its network into sub-networks or segments?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Properly implemented network segmentation prevents a malicious actor from compromising a system with a lower security categorization and then moving laterally to compromise a system with a higher security categorization.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization has divided its network into sub-networks or segments.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization utilizes a variety of techniques to segment the network based on different levels of mission criticality or sensitivity and has created functional zones.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has implemented segmentation addressing for some of its critical services, but not all.

Possible evidence

  • Document describing the organization’s network segmentation strategy
  • Network diagram

questions.title: WI:CM-1.Q2
questions.text: Has the organization selected tools that meet its continuous monitoring requirements?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Situational awareness for threats is directly related to the critical assets of the organization as they support achievement of organizational objectives. Therefore, the organization objectives dictate the functional needs and requirements of any system. If these requirements are not satisfied with the selection and procurement of tools or utilities to support the process, then the organization could realize greater risk exposure to cyber threats.

Question Intent: This question is trying to determine if requirements for continuous monitoring are being acted upon in an appropriate manner that reduces risk exposure. Similarly, procurement alone of a tool or utility is not adequate. There must be sufficient implementation to meet the expectations of continuous monitoring as dictated by the organizational requirements.

Continuous monitoring may utilize tools that perform logging, alerting, and reporting.

Alternative terms used could include “ConMon” or an abbreviation of “Continuous Monitoring”. See also “CSM” for “Continuous Security Monitoring”.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Actual tool selection may be only part of answering this question. The assessor must consider the implementation of the tool in the organization. Specifically, the operator(s) is trained for proper use of the tool. Additionally, the operator(s) must demonstrate proper awareness and proficiency in using the tool properly.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A tool may be selected and procured. However, there are improper configurations or usage practices that would indicate that the tool is not optimized.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Procurement documentation related to third party provider or actual product delivery
  • Terms and conditions related documentation
  • Demonstration of system maintenance through OEM provision

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Not applicable

questions.title: WI:CM-2.Q2
questions.text: Are cybersecurity events related to the physical environment reported to appropriate personnel?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Security controls can be physical, technical, or administrative in nature. The physical environment must be secured to prohibit undue access to hardware and related network equipment. These controls can be resource intensive to manage and maintain as organizations face continuous flux in staffing, third party providers, and visitors as much as intruders not otherwise welcome on the site. Furthermore, these controls may provide alerts or other notifications that require action on the part of security forces.

Question Intent: This particular question tries to assess the effectiveness and capabilities of the security stack as it relates to physical controls. Event documentation and logging provides critical information that drive forensic investigation and potential prosecution where applicable. The information may also contribute to future practice and applications of lessons learned for improvement.

Cybersecurity events include theft/loss, plugging something in, leaving USB drives or other vectors.

Qualities of key idea being sought with examples

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Effective organizations track physical events with watch stander logs. These logs may be automated or manually documented by security personnel. Additional means of tracking may include regular review of camera surveillance, entry authentication via badge or biometric records, etc. Full implementation is recognized when all points of entry are monitored and logged, additional logs are documented in a standard manner, and that logs are regularly reviewed and utilized in a means that supports standard security practices.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Although the organization may be logging entry and exit of personnel or maintaining other security operation logs, the practices may be inconsistent or not documented to a sufficient extent that operational logs are incomplete. Incomplete or inconsistent logs may fail to support collection of forensic evidence or incomplete documentation of lessons learned.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy and procedures for proper log and event documentation
  • Training products related to proper event and incident documentation
  • Actual samples of security logs – automated or manual generation

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR, IM:G2.Q1. NIST 800-53: CA-7, PE-3, PE-6, PE-20

questions.title: WI:CM-3.Q2
questions.text: Are cybersecurity events related to personnel activity reported to cybersecurity personnel?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Internal threat actors can be a pernicious threat for the organization given their increased level and degree of access. In response to this threat, organizations must vet and monitor their personnel for any changes in behavior and any other related key risk indicators. The program must demonstrate considerate yet effective responsiveness in accordance with its policy and procedure.

Question Intent: This question reviews the organizational process and capability for notification of insider risk related events and incidents.

Insider threat is the potential for an insider to use their authorized access or understanding of an organization to harm that organization. This harm can include malicious, complacent, or unintentional acts that negatively affect the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of the organization, its data, personnel, or facilities. External stakeholders and customers of DHS may find this generic definition better suited and adaptable for their organization’s use.

The Cyber and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) defines insider threat as the threat that an insider will use his or her authorized access, wittingly or unwittingly, to do harm to the Department’s mission, resources, personnel, facilities, information, equipment, networks, or systems. This threat can manifest as damage to the Department through the following insider behaviors:

  • Espionage
  • Terrorism
  • Unauthorized disclosure of information
  • Corruption, including participation in transnational organized crime
  • Sabotage
  • Workplace violence
  • Intentional or unintentional loss or degradation of departmental resources or capabilities

– Defining Insider Threats

Insider Threat - A malicious insider threat is a current or former employee, contractor, or business partner who has or had authorized access to an organization's network, system, or data and intentionally exceeded or misused that access in a manner that negatively affected the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of the organization's information or information systems.

– CERT Definition

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has an established insider risk management program. The governance structure of that program enables communication and direction in response to any events. These notices must be timely and consistent to provide effective management.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may have an insider risk management program in place. However, the governance structure may not be established in such a manner that support effective communications related to insider risk events to the appropriate personnel. Communications may not be standardized leading to misunderstanding or improper escalation of events.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Related policy and procedural guidance for proper event response
  • Logs or other documentation that captures events and incidents
  • Forensic evidence that demonstrates exercise of the process

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR IM:G2.Q1. NIST 800-53: AC-2, AU-12, AU-13, CA-7, CM-10, CM-11

questions.title: WI:CM-4.Q2
questions.text: How often are malware signatures updated? (Select one option that represents the longest interval among all systems.)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Malware can be identified in a variety of ways, which enables automated scanning and other methods that may prevent infections. Once identified, malware signatures are promulgated to many organizations as warning and to enable scanning activities to identify and either prevent or eliminate malware infection.

Question Intent: Since new malware is identified on a regular basis, organizations must periodically update their systems to maintain situational awareness for prevention of infections.

CISA defines malware, short for “malicious software,” as 

any software (such as a virus, Trojan, or spyware) that is installed on your computer or mobile device. The software is then used, usually covertly, to compromise the integrity of your device. Most commonly, malware is designed to give attackers access to your infected computer. That access may allow others to monitor and control your online activity or steal sensitive data.

– Malware Tip Card (cisa.gov)

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • For full implementation the frequency of malware signature updates should be at least daily.  

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The frequency for malware updates is less than daily or ad hoc.  
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy and procedure for update of malware signatures
  • Log or other related documentation that demonstrates timely update

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53: SI-3, SI-8

questions.title: WI:CM-6.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization employ contractual language that requires external service providers to report cybersecurity incidents within a predefined time span?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations must have the ability to identify and understand exposure to uncertainty. This is completed through proper risk analysis and management. Furthermore, organizations continue to raise their reliance on third party providers, which leads to external dependencies for the organization. Risk management practices must be extended to those dependencies to reduce undue exposure to operational disruption.

Question Intent: This question is trying to determine if the procurement practices of the organization require service providers take appropriate actions in the event of cyber incidents in a timely manner. This is especially applicable to third party providers that have access to organizational systems.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has policy and procedures that mandate the content of procurement contracts to require third party providers to report security incidents.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may have proper contractual requirements in place; however, they may not properly enforce those requirements. Third party providers may not be consistent in their reporting practices, or they may not be providing timely alerts.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Samples of existing contracts with related requirements
  • Logs and documentation that indicate notification of incidents by third party providers

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53: CA-7, PS-7, SA-4, SA-9, SI-4

questions.title: WI:CM-7.Q2
questions.text: Are changes to connections, devices, and software managed?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The organization will likely have a highly interconnected environment. Regardless of the complexity and degree of connectivity between devices and related software, the organization must configure those connections to reduce the risk exposure to the organization. Configuration change management will enable greater control over organizational technology to optimize cyber risk management practices.

Question Intent: This question attempts to gain a better understanding of organizational configuration change management practices.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has proper policy and procedure in place to control configuration changes within the enterprise. This may include the use of a change management control board and related process that must be implemented and demonstrating ability to control organizational risk exposure.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may have policy and procedure in place. However, the organization may not be properly following the direction in practice for any variety of reasons. For example, the organizational configuration management control board may not meet regularly. Alternatively, the risk appetite may not align with critical changes in the organization, therefore decisions made in one part of the organization may not completely align with the desires of another.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Change management control policies and procedures
  • Change management control log and associated documentation

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CERT RMM TM:SG4.SP3. 
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5:  AU-12, CA-7, CM-3, CM-8, PE-3, PE-6, PE-20, SI-4

questions.title: WI:CM-8.Q2
questions.text: What assets are scanned? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Vulnerabilities and malware, among other risk elements, can be identified in a variety of ways, which enables automated scanning and other methods that may prevent threat actors from exploiting them before being identified. Once identified, scanning information may be promulgated to many organizations as warning and to enable others to respond accordingly.

Question Intent: This question tries to gain an understanding of the scope of scanning practices performed by the organization.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization conducts scanning for malware, vulnerabilities, intrusion, endpoints, and port status on a periodic basis (see listing itemized by the question). More specifically, policy and procedures are written to direct the organization on communication processes and expected responses in accordance with the identified threats.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may conduct regular scanning for a portion of the criteria listed in the question. Alternatively, the organization may scan for all those items. However, the scanning may not be conducted on a frequent enough basis. There may also be limited or delayed response for alerts that result from these scanning activities.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Scanning tools implemented in the organization
  • Demonstration that the scanning tools are regularly updated
  • Documentation and logs that demonstrate proper and timely response to alerts from the scans

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-5

questions.title: WI:SG-1.Q2
questions.text: What technologies does the organization use to implement network segmentation? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Network segmentation contains adversary activities and non-adversarial stresses (e.g., fires, floods) to the enclave, system segment, or facility in which they have established a presence and limits the set of possible targets to which malware can be easily propagated. This question addresses the technical solutions that can be utilized to implement network segmentation to achieve this goal.

Question Intent: Evaluate the technologies that the organization utilizes to achieve its network segmentation strategy.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has developed and executed a network segmentation strategy commensurate with the sensitivity levels of the systems and data. The assessment team should determine, collectively, the optimal network segmentation strategy for the system or application under assessment. If the system or application under assessment is reasonably isolated, in accordance with the optimal strategy, utilizing appropriate technologies, the response should be graded “Full Implementation.”

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • If the system or application under assessment is reasonably isolated, but there are other technologies or solutions that would more optimally implement the network segmentation strategy, the response should be graded “Partial Implementation.”
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Network diagram depicting network segmentation, control implementation descriptions in the System Security Plan (SSP) describing the technologies used to achieve the network segmentation

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-46, SC-49, SC-50

questions.title: WI:SI-1.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization employ automated tools to check data for quality and validity before ingesting it into production systems?
questions.supplemental:
Question Intent: Determine if the organization utilizes automated tools to check data for quality and validity before ingesting it into production systems. If yes, which tools are utilized?

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization utilizes automated tools to check data for quality and validity before ingesting it into product systems. The organization identifies the tools and the way they are used. The tools and methods are documented in a policy or procedure.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization utilizes automated tools to check data for quality and validity before ingesting it into product systems. The organization identifies the tools and the way they are used. The tools and methods are not documented in a policy or procedure.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • A policy or procedure that identifies the tools and the way they are used, a network diagram that depicts devices or appliances (e.g., a proxy device or server) that receive data and perform quality and validity checks, relevant security control implementation descriptions in a System Security Plan (SSP)

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-160, Rev. 1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-10, SI-10(1), SI-10(2), SI-10(3), SI-10(4), SI-10(5), SI-10(6), SI-18(1)

questions.title: WI:SI-2.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization document, monitor, and maintain valid provenance of the systems, system components, and associated data for critical systems?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Knowing who and what is in the supply chains of organizations is critical to gaining visibility into supply chain activities. Visibility into supply chain activities is also important for monitoring and identifying high-risk events and activities. Without reasonable visibility into supply chains elements, processes, and personnel, it is very difficult for organizations to understand and manage risk and reduce their susceptibility to adverse events.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization has documented processes and procedures to maintain valid provenance of systems, system components, and data.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a policy and/or procedure that documents the process to document, monitor, and maintain the valid provenance of systems, system components, and associated data. Also, the organization presents the work products of the process.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization presents one of the items in “Criteria for Full Implementation Response
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy and/or procedure that documents the process to document, monitor, and maintain the valid provenance of systems, system components, and associated data.
  • Work products of the above process.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SR-4

questions.title: WI:SI-3.Q2
questions.text:
(a) Analyze communications traffic and event patterns for the system;
(b) Develop profiles representing common traffic and event patterns; and
(c) Use the traffic and event profiles in tuning system-monitoring devices.
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Identifying and understanding common communications traffic and event patterns help organizations provide useful information to system monitoring devices to identify more effectively suspicious or anomalous traffic and events when they occur. Such information can help reduce the number of false positives and false negatives during system monitoring.

Question Intent: Does the organization analyze communications traffic and event patterns for the system, develop profiles representing common traffic and event patterns, and use the traffic and event profiles in tuning system-monitoring devices?

Discussion: 

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a policy and/or procedures that describe the analysis of communications traffic and event patterns for the system, the development of profiles representing common traffic and event patterns, and the use of traffic and event profiles in tuning system monitoring devices.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has a policy and/or procedure, but it is incomplete, e.g., it does not describe all three of these items.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy or procedure

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-4(13)

questions.title: WI:UN-2.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization rotate roles and responsibilities among technical users with appropriate skillsets?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Rotating roles and responsibilities may cause a change in a technical user’s associated levels of access and privilege. These changes may impede an adversary from targeting the organization’s mission critical information assets. Note, sharing roles among personnel for backup purpose does not qualify as rotating roles and responsibilities from one employee to the next.  Sharing roles will not cause a change in a technical user’s associated level of access and privilege and thus not impede an adversary.  

Question Intent: To determine if the organization rotates roles and responsibilities among technical users for cyber security purposes.

  • Randomness introduces increased levels of uncertainty for adversaries regarding the actions that organizations take to defend their systems against attacks.
  • Maintain an environment of uncertainty for the adversary and keep the adversary from extrapolating from past events. Such actions may impede the ability of adversaries to correctly target an organization’s mission critical information resources.
  • Change behavior or state in ways that are determined randomly or by complex functions. Make changes randomly or unpredictably. Do not let the adversary take advantage of consistency
  • Misdirection techniques that involve randomness include
  • performing certain routine actions at different times of day,
  • employing different information technologies,
  • using different suppliers,
  • and rotating roles and responsibilities of organizational personnel (note, sharing roles among personnel for backup purposes does not qualify as rotating roles and responsibilities from one person to the next.)

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization rotates roles and responsibilities among all technical users that support the delivery of the critical service/HVA environment.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization rotates roles and responsibilities among some technical users that support the delivery of the critical service/HVA environment.

Possible evidence

  • A documented policy and/or process for rotating roles and responsibilities among technical staff.
  • Personnel records detailing the rotating roles and responsibilities among the technical staff.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-30(2)

questions.title: RE:AN-2.Q2
questions.text: Are incidents analyzed to determine if they are related to other incidents or events?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: If incidents are related to other incidents or events the appropriate response must take this into account for a holistic assessment, as correlation with other incidents may indicate that larger issues, problems, or incidents exist.

Question Intent: Determine whether incidents are analyzed to determine if they are related to other incidents or events.

  • Incident correlation can identify where activity is more widespread than originally thought, and identify any relationships among malicious attacks, compromises, and exploited vulnerabilities.
  • Often incidents are declared individually; correlation enables analysts to recognize that the underlying cause of the incident may have affected more systems in the infrastructure than identified in the single incident.
  • The organization needs to have a task in the process, either automated or manual, to perform correlation analysis of the incident.
  • Manual processes may be used to perform an examination of incident records in a routine manner to look for relationships (e.g., events or incidents related to the same IP address or time stamp, etc.). The organization may also have automated systems that perform the correlation of incidents

Types of information that can be correlated include:

  • IP addresses, hostnames, ports, protocols, and services
  • targeted applications, OSs, organizational sectors, site names, and business functions
  • common attacks and exploits

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization analyzes all incidents to determine if they are related to other incidents or events

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization analyzes some incidents to determine if they are related to other incidents or events

Possible evidence

  • A report or document that contains an analysis of incidents and their relationships to other incidents or events

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: IR:G2.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4

questions.title: RE:AN-4.Q2
questions.text: Are incidents categorized?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Incident categories can help the organization understand and communicate the severity and potential impact that the event will have on the organization.

Question Intent: To determine if incidents are categorized.

Incident categories can help the organization understand and communicate the severity and impact the incident will have on the critical service. Incidents may be categorized by:

  • type (e.g., security, safety, unauthorized access, user issue, denial of service, virus intrusion, physical access violation)
  • severity (e.g., critical, high, medium, low)
  • other categorization labels (e.g., internal, external, physical, technical)

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization categorizes all incidents relevant to the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization categorizes some incidents

Possible evidence

  • A report, list, or document that illustrates incidents being categorized in a meaningful way

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • HVA: IM.PROTECT.Q4
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4, IR-5, IR-8

questions.title: RE:AN-5.Q2
questions.text: Is the information from these sources kept current?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Vulnerability data collection is a continuous process.  Keeping information current ensures that identification of vulnerabilities happens in a timely manner, and this extends the organizations awareness of vulnerabilities.   As new vulnerability information becomes available the organization should incorporate it into the organization’s vulnerability repository and corresponding identification and analysis activities.

Question Intent: To determine if the vulnerability information obtained from the established sources is kept current.

  • Vulnerability data collection is a continuous process.
  • The information from the sources (established in VM:G2.Q1) needs to be continually updated.
  • New sources of vulnerability information must also be added to the source list as they emerge.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The vulnerability information from all of the established sources is kept current.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The vulnerability information from some of the established sources is kept current.

Possible evidence

  • List of sources of vulnerability information
  • Evidence showing sources are reviewed on a regular basis and updated as necessary

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: VM:G2.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-5, PM-15

questions.title: RE:AM-1.Q2
questions.text: Does the organization use organization-defined sources to discover, collect, and distribute indicators of compromise to relevant personnel?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: IOCs provide valuable information on systems that have been compromised.

Question Intent: to determine if the organization has defined sources or processes in place to discover, collect, and distribute indicators of compromise to relevant personnel.

  • Indicators of compromise (IOC) are forensic artifacts from intrusions that are identified on organizational systems at the host or network level.
  • IOCs can include the creation of registry key values. IOCs for network traffic include Universal Resource Locator or protocol elements that indicate malicious code command and control servers.
  • The rapid distribution and adoption of IOCs can improve information security by reducing the time that systems and organizations are vulnerable to the same exploit or attack.
  • Threat indicators, signatures, tactics, techniques, procedures, and other indicators of compromise may be available via government and non-government cooperatives, including the Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams, the United States Computer Emergency Readiness Team, the Defense Industrial Base Cybersecurity Information Sharing Program, and the CERT Coordination Center.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented, in a policy or procedure, its approach to collecting, analyzing, disseminating, and deploying IOCs, and has implemented this approach.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented, in a policy or procedure, its approach to using IOCs, but it does not cover all of the items in “Criteria for Full Implementation Response.”

Possible evidence

  • Policy or procedure, filtering device configuration file

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-4(24)

questions.title: RE:AM-3.Q2
questions.text: Is there a standard set of tools and/or methods in use to detect malicious code in assets?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should employ malicious code protection mechanisms at information system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code.

Question Intent: To determine if a standard set of tools and/or methods is in use to detect malicious code in assets.

NIST 800-53 Rev.4 SI-3:

  • The organization employs malicious code protection mechanisms at information system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code.
  • The organization updates malicious code protection mechanisms whenever new releases are available.
  • ‘The organization performs periodic scans (as defined by the organization) of the information system and real-time scans of files from external sources.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a standard set of tools and/or methods that are used to identify malicious code (e.g., anti-virus or anti-malware software, etc.), where appropriate, in all assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has a standard set of tools and/or methods that are used to identify malicious code (e.g., anti-virus or anti-malware software, etc.), where appropriate, in some assets.

Possible evidence

  • Information Security Policy, Software Inventory

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: VM:G1.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-3(10)

questions.title: RE:CO-1.Q2
questions.text: Do incident management team members receive incident response training and applicable to their respective roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: It is critical that incident management team members receive incident response training and are aware of the role that they play in the incident response process.

Question Intent: To determine if incident management team members receive incident response training and understand their roles

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All members of the incident management team have undergone incident response training and understand their roles within the larger incident management process.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some members of the incident management team have undergone incident response training and understand their roles within the larger incident management process.

Possible evidence

  • Verbal attestation from incident management team members, training records.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • HVA: IM.PREPARE.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, CP-3, IR-3, IR-8

questions.title: RE:CO-2.Q2
questions.text: Are events from those security monitoring activities reported to the Incident Management Function?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Network security monitoring is an important proactive capability that allows an organization to detect suspicious activity throughout the enterprise.

Question Intent: To ensure that, in all situations, any suspicious activity or other security-related events obtained through the organization’s security monitoring activities are reported to the appropriate incident handling and response personnel.

  • Suspicious activity also includes unauthorized, security-relevant changes to the organization’s systems and networks.
  • Events collected from security monitoring activities should be reported to the appropriate event and incident handling and response personnel.
  • If an external party performs detection activities for the organization, any suspicious activity or other security-related events obtained through the external party’s security monitoring activities should be reported to the appropriate incident handling and response personnel.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All security events obtained from the security monitoring activities are reported to the appropriate event and incident handling and response personnel

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some security events are reported to the appropriate event and incident handling and response personnel.

Possible evidence

  • Copies of any event reports, notices, or other communication sent from the security monitoring activities to the Incident Management Function

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: EH:G1.Q7
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-6, IR-6, IR-8

questions.title: RE:CO-3.Q2
questions.text: Are forensic analysis results and reports provided to the appropriate stakeholders?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Forensic analysis results can be used to determine the extent to which a system or network has been compromised or otherwise affected and to provide a better understanding of what malicious activity occurred and what other systems or services may have been affected. Such analysis can also facilitate the development and implementation of comprehensive solutions, ensuring the use of more effective protective strategies. The results of forensics analysis can also be used to prosecute malicious intruders

Question Intent: To determine if the organization provides the results of forensic analysis to the appropriate stakeholders.

  • Based on applicable requirements, the organization should develop a forensic analysis reporting process.
  • The process should describe the stakeholders to whom the results of the forensic analysis must be communicated and the means of communication.
  • Forensic analysis may be performed for law enforcement purposes, or for detailed incident analysis to determine root cause or other information about what occurred.
  • Additional sensitivities may need to be taken into consideration, because the results of forensic analysis during an incident may contain personal or organizationally sensitive data not typically encountered in incident response.
  • Staff should be trained on the organizational process for reporting the results of forensic analysis, to ensure that the appropriate stakeholder(s) receive the results.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Forensic analysis results and reports are provided to all the appropriate stakeholders.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Forensic analysis results and reports are provided to some of the appropriate stakeholders.

Possible evidence

  • Documented process for providing forensic analysis results and reports to the appropriate stakeholders. results of process audits illustrating that forensic analysis results and reports are being provided to the appropriate stakeholders

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: IR:G4.Q4
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CA-2, CA-7, CP-2, IR-4, IR-8, PE-6, RA-5, SI-4

questions.title: RE:CO-4.Q2
questions.text: Are incidents escalated to internal and external stakeholders for input and resolution?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Incidents that the organization has declared should be escalated to stakeholders who can implement, manage, and resolve the incident.

Question Intent: To determine if incidents are escalated to stakeholders for input and resolution.

Stakeholders can be internal to the organization (such as a standing incident response team or an incident-specific team) or external, in the form of contractors or other suppliers

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization escalates all incidents, relevant to the critical service, to the proper stakeholders for input and resolution.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization escalates some incidents to the proper stakeholders.

Possible evidence

  • Correspondence or incident reports that demonstrate that stakeholders were contacted.
