questions.title: WI:NP-2.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization employ virtualization techniques to support the deployment of a diversity of operating systems and applications that are changed in accordance with the organization-defined frequency?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: An organization takes measures to automatically terminate a user session degrade an adversary’s ability to maintain a covert presence and to help prevent the spread or intended impact of attacks.

Question Intent: Write here what the question is trying to ascertain.

  • Session termination addresses the termination of user-initiated logical sessions. This is in contrast to the termination of network connections associated with communications sessions (i.e., network disconnect).
  • A logical session (for local, network, and remote access) is initiated whenever a user (or process acting on behalf of a user) accesses an organizational system.
  • Such user sessions can be terminated without terminating network sessions. Session termination ends all processes associated with a user’s logical session except for those processes that are specifically created by the user (i.e., session owner) to continue after the session is terminated.
  • Conditions or trigger events that require automatic termination of the session include
  • Organization-defined periods of user inactivity,
  • Targeted responses to certain types of incidents, or
  • Time-of-day restrictions on system use.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Measures are employed to automatically terminate all user sessions established to the system when organization-defined conditions requiring session termination are met.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Measures are employed to automatically terminate some user sessions established to the system when organization-defined conditions requiring session termination are met.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the implementation and configuration of the ability to automatically terminate all user sessions established to the critical service/HVA environment when organization-defined conditions are met
  • A documented list of organization-defined conditions or trigger events that are used to guide when user sessions are terminated.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-12

questions.title: WI:NP-3.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization establish connections to the system on demand and terminate connections after completion of a request or a period of non-use?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Limiting persistent connections to systems may help prevent advanced adversaries from moving laterally through systems and potentially position themselves closer to high value assets.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization connects to the system on demand and terminates connections after completion of a request or after a period of non-use.

  • Persistent connections to systems can provide advanced adversaries with paths to move laterally through systems and potentially position themselves closer to high value assets.
  • Limiting the availability of such connections impedes the adversary’s ability to move freely through organizational systems.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All connections to the critical service/HVA system are established on demand and are terminated after completion of a request or after a period of non-use.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some connections to the critical service/HVA system are established on demand and are terminated after completion of a request or after a period of non-use.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the implementation and configuration of the methods or mechanisms used to establish on demand connections to critical service/HVA environment that are also terminated after the completion of a request or after a period of non-use.
  • Log files showing the establishment of on demand connections and their termination after the completion of a request or after a period of non-use.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53: SI-14(3)

questions.title: WI:PR-1.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization prohibit privileged access to the system by non-organizational users?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Non-organizational users may not be vetted or reviewed or trained as carefully as those within the organization. Restricting their access reduces the risk of attackers exploiting a potentially vulnerable asset.

Question Intent: To assess whether the organization prohibits privileged access to the system by non-organizational users.

Discussion: Policies and procedures for granting equivalent status of employees to individuals include a need-to-know, citizenship, and the relationship to the organization.

Definition of any key words with examples:

  • Organizational user: an employee or an individual considered by the organization to have the equivalent status of an employee; may include contractors (including managed service providers (MSP), managed security service provider (MSSP), etc.) guest researchers, or individuals detailed from other organizations.
  • Non-organizational user: a user who is not an organizational user.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Policies and procedures to ensure non-organizational users are uniquely identified and authenticated for accesses; and
  • Policies and procedures to ensure non-organizational users are prohibited from privileged access to the system.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Either Fully Implemented or No Implementation.

Possible evidence

  • Access control policy; procedures addressing least privilege; list of system-generated privileged accounts; list of non-organizational users; system configuration settings and associated documentation; audit records; system security plan.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53 AC-6(6) (also IA-8)

questions.title: WI:PR-2.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization employ dynamic data masking to restrict access to sensitive information in databases or similar systems?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Some work roles, such as database administrators, often have access to information in databases that is not required for their work roles. Organizations should safeguard that data by employing masking techniques (among other controls).

Question Intent: Determine if the organization employs dynamic data masking to restrict access to sensitive information in databases or similar systems, e.g., masking within tables, hashing db fields, etc.

Dynamic data masking aims at real-time data masking of production data so that the data requester does not get access to sensitive data, while no physical changes to the original production data take place.

An example would be restrictions on access to sensitive information (e.g., SSN) in databases or similar systems depending on the role of the user.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization defines sensitive data which must be dynamically masked; and
  • The organization implements dynamic data masking on the defined sensitive data.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization develops a dynamic data masking plan including defining sensitive data which must be dynamically masked but has not yet implemented dynamic data masking on it.

Possible evidence

  • Dynamic data masking plan; defined listing of sensitive data to be dynamically masked; details on technology being used to implement the dynamic data masking.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-160, Vol. 2., Examples

questions.title: WI:PR-3.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization automatically disable or restrict account access based on factors such as anomalous login times, impossible travel, or other indicators of potential account compromise?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Employing an automated system to restrict accounts that may be compromised reduces the ability of attackers to exploit those accounts.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization automatically disables or restricts account access based on factors such as anomalous login times, impossible travel, or other indicators of potential account compromise.

Successful implementation requires dynamic privilege management without a requirement for re-authentication or reboot AND the ability to respond to a specific trigger that might be specific to a user's/account's behavior or an overall elevated level of threat to the entire system.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Documented criteria for atypical usage (triggers) for which to monitor all accounts is defined by the organization; and
  • all critical service  accounts are monitored for atypical usage as defined by the organization; and
  • Atypical usage is used to automatically disable or restrict account access for all accounts.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Criteria for atypical usage for which to monitor account access is in development and partially documented.
  • Or, documented criteria exists but only some critical service accounts are monitored for atypical usage and automatically disabled or restricted.  

Possible evidence

  • Access control policy; procedures addressing account management; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; system-generated list of system accounts; system audit records; privacy impact assessment; system security plan; privacy plan; system-generated list of dynamic privilege management capabilities; system monitoring records; audit tracking and monitoring reports.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-2(6), AC-2(8), AC-2(12)

questions.title: WI:PT-1.Q3
questions.text: Is access to the event data repository restricted to those with a business need?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The organization and information system should protect audit information and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion.

Question Intent: To determine if access to the event data repository is restricted to those with a business need.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Access to the event data repository is authorized only to a specified subset of privileged users.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Only some of the privileged users with access to the event data repository have a verified mission need for it.

Possible evidence

questions.text: Are individual systems assigned to segments based on functionality? For example, has the organization established functional “zones”?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Properly implemented network segmentation prevents a malicious actor from compromising a system with a lower security categorization and then moving laterally to compromise a system with a higher security categorization.

Question Intent: Determine if individual systems assigned are assigned to segments based on functionality?

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All systems are assigned to segments based on their functionality.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some systems are assigned to segments based on their functionality.

Possible evidence

  • Document describing the organization’s network segmentation strategy
  • Network diagram

questions.title: WI:CM-1.Q3
questions.text: Which of the following cybersecurity measures does the organization employ for monitoring of assets and networks related to the CCS? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: This question is trying to determine if requirements for continuous monitoring are being acted upon in an appropriate manner that reduces risk exposure. This question seeks to identify and document the extent of continuous monitoring tool implementation as well as process application that leverages the tool. Ultimately, the assessor is trying to gain an appreciation for the extent of continuous monitoring practice for the organization.

Question Intent: This question is trying to ascertain the extent of capability and application for continuous monitoring throughout the organization.

Continuous monitoring may utilize tools that perform logging, alerting, and reporting.

Alternative terms used could include “ConMon” or an abbreviation of “Continuous Monitoring”. See also “CSM” for “Continuous Security Monitoring”.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Full implementation would have all aspects of the following implemented:
    • Automated security event response
    • Automated security event alerting
    • Near-real-time monitoring for malicious code
    • Near-real-time monitoring for unauthorized access
    • Near-real-time monitoring for unauthorized software
    • Near-real-time network boundary intrusion detection
    • Near-real-time network boundary traffic monitoring
    • Near-real-time host intrusion monitoring
    • Manual, non-real-time network monitoring based on audit logs
    • The organization does not monitor assets and networks

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may demonstrate some of the elements listed.
  • Alternatively, the organization may support all of the criteria listed above. However, the implementation for some may not be adequate based upon poor use of the tool, improper tool configuration, or limited resources for application implementation.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Reports that are result of the activities from the criteria listed
  • Operator demonstration of specific monitoring for any of the listed criteria
  • Automated activity that delivers the above criteria may be evident in operational logs

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: Q.20.1

options.text: Manual, non-real-time network monitoring based on audit logs
The organization does not monitor assets and networks

questions.title: WI:CM-2.Q3
questions.text: Do employees receive training in how physical security impacts cybersecurity?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Security controls can be physical, technical, or administrative in nature. The physical environment must be secured to prohibit undue access to hardware and related network equipment. These controls can be resource intensive to manage and maintain as organizations face continuous flux in staffing, third party providers, and visitors as much as intruders not otherwise welcome on the site. These forms of controls require adequate judgement and diligent application of policies and practices by security personnel. Training plays a critical role in developing those capabilities.

Question Intent: Security personnel require adequate training to carry out their duties. This question seeks evidence and demonstration that the organization is delivering training on a regular basis to maintain proficiency as much as build individual capability and necessary skills.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Regular periodic training must be delivered on a consistent basis with sufficient information as much as practical application. Further to that end, the training program should provide a means to measure performance and adoption of the information provided.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Training may be provided. However, test and assessment scores may demonstrate that the program is not effective. Incomplete training records may also show that a portion of the workforce may not be receiving adequate training. Training program content may also not be adequate given the context and requirements of the assessed organization.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Training program content and syllabi
  • Training policy and related requirements
  • Training records that show participation
  • Testing and assessment scores resulting from the training

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Not applicable

questions.title: WI:CM-3.Q3
questions.text: Do employees receive training in how to detect potential insider threat activities and how to report them?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Internal threat actors can be a pernicious threat for the organization given their increased level and degree of access. In response to this threat, organizations must vet and monitor their personnel for any changes in behavior and any other related key risk indicators. The program must demonstrate considerate yet effective responsiveness in accordance with its policy and procedure. This process will not be effective unless the organization provides effective training that enables the workforce to identify and report insider threat related activities.

Question Intent: This question seeks to emphasize the importance of workforce training with respect to insider risk. The base expectation is that the organization receives the appropriate level of awareness as much as an understanding of what to do if an insider risk event is identified.

Insider threat is the potential for an insider to use their authorized access or understanding of an organization to harm that organization. This harm can include malicious, complacent, or unintentional acts that negatively affect the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of the organization, its data, personnel, or facilities. External stakeholders and customers of DHS may find this generic definition better suited and adaptable for their organization’s use.

The Cyber and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) defines insider threat as the threat that an insider will use his or her authorized access, wittingly or unwittingly, to do harm to the Department’s mission, resources, personnel, facilities, information, equipment, networks, or systems. This threat can manifest as damage to the Department through the following insider behaviors:

  • Espionage
  • Terrorism
  • Unauthorized disclosure of information
  • Corruption, including participation in transnational organized crime
  • Sabotage
  • Workplace violence
  • Intentional or unintentional loss or degradation of departmental resources or capabilities

– Defining Insider Threats

Insider Threat – A malicious insider threat is a current or former employee, contractor, or business partner who has or had authorized access to an organization's network, system, or data and intentionally exceeded or misused that access in a manner that negatively affected the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of the organization's information or information systems.

– CERT Definition

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization must have an insider risk management program that provides comprehensive training for the employee base. Specifically, all employees must be provided a minimum awareness of the program with a range of detailed, role-based training for those employees who are working with the program. For example, human resource professionals may require additional training related to identification of insider threat risks through behavioral indicators. Regardless, the organization should also be documenting and tracking training records to ensure that the workforce receives what it needs.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Despite the organization having a program and training regimen in place, the organization may not provide the correct training, may not be tracking participation, or may not be realizing the correct results from their training efforts.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy and procedure related to insider risk management program
  • Training program documentation such as syllabi, training records, course materials, etc.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53: AC-2, AU-12, AU-13, CA-7, CM-10, CM-11

questions.title: WI:CM-4.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization employ any of the following security controls to prevent malicious code from exploiting the system? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Malicious code may be injected into an organizational code base from either internal or external sources as a matter of ignorant or malicious intent. Regardless of the vector, the organization must take action to prevent that code from exploiting the system.

Question Intent: This question looks at some fundamental controls to be put in place to alleviate the threat of malicious code.

Malicious code is unwanted files or programs that can cause harm to a computer or compromise data stored on a computer. Various classifications of malicious code include viruses, worms, and Trojan horses.

– Protecting Against Malicious Code | CISA

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has proper controls in place that provide up to date real time host-based malware software protection and network-based scanning capabilities. Furthermore, the tools are utilized in a timely manner to minimize risk exposure for the organization.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has up-to-date real-time host-based malware protection but does not have network-based protection
  • Or, network-based protection has been implemented but host-based protection has not.  
  • Or, the proper tools may be available in the organization; however, they may not be configured properly. The organization may not properly update or maintain the systems with regular periodicity.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Demonstration that the tools cited by the question are in place
  • Documentation or logs that demonstrate proper configuration and operation of the tools provided
  • Documentation or logs that show proper maintenance of the tools provided

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: Q.19.1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev.5: SI-3, SI-8

options.text: Signature-based up-to-date real-time, host-based anti-virus/malware software to prevent operation of malicious code
Heuristics-based up-to-date real-time, host-based anti-virus/malware software to prevent operation of malicious code
Anomaly-based up-to-date real-time, host-based anti-virus/malware software to prevent operation of malicious code
Signature-based network- or gateway-based malware scanning
Heuristics-based network- or gateway-based malware scanning
Anomaly-based network- or gateway-based malware scanning

questions.title: WI:CM-7.Q3
questions.text: How does the organization monitor for unauthorized personnel? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Unauthorized personnel, in addition to posing a physical risk to employees, can accidentally or inadvertently introduce unauthorized devices into a system, such as by connecting USB drives to computers or computers to physical network ports. Unsupervised individuals also may have gain access to paper-based files or other materials left on desks or in conference spaces.

Question Intent: This question tries to identify the types of monitoring in place for monitoring of unauthorized personnel.

Physical access monitoring includes publicly accessible areas within organizational facilities. Examples of physical access monitoring include the employment of guards, video surveillance equipment (i.e., cameras), and sensor devices. Reviewing physical access logs can help identify suspicious activity, anomalous events, or potential threats  Physical access points can include facility access points, interior access points to systems that require supplemental access controls, or both.

Employing guards at selected internal and external physical access points to the facility provides a more rapid response capability for organizations. Guards also provide the opportunity for human surveillance in areas of the facility not covered by video surveillance.

Organizational incident response capabilities include investigations of physical security incidents and responses to the incidents. Incidents include security violations or suspicious physical access activities.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented policy and procedure for appropriate monitoring of unauthorized personnel. At least one of the listed methods must be employed.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • One of the listed methods may be in place but executed in an ad hoc manner  .
  • Or, the capability is in development and partially implemented.  

Possible evidence

  • Documented process and procedures for various monitoring activities
  • Implemented video surveillance system and logs detailing events generated through monitoring
  • Logs detailing guard actions
  • Physical access audit logs for defined internal and external entry or exit points

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-12, CA-7, CM-3, CM-8, PE-3, PE-6, PE-20, SI-4

options.text: Employee training in identifying unauthorized personnel
The organization does not monitor for unauthorized personnel

questions.title: WI:CM-8.Q3
questions.text: What is the frequency of the scans? (Select one)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Vulnerabilities can be identified in a variety of ways, which enables automated scanning and other methods that may prevent threat actors from exploiting them before being identified and patched. Once identified, vulnerabilities are promulgated to many organizations as warning and to enable scanning activities to identify and either prevent or eliminate infection. This process, however, would not be successful unless the organization is properly advised of these vulnerabilities in a timely manner.

Question Intent: This question tries to establish the periodicity of scanning for the environment.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization may have direction in place through policy and procedure that specifies periodicity of scanning for its environment. Clearly, the greater frequency would be desired, however, the context of the organization and its risk appetite may indicate that greater duration between scans is warranted. The analyst must determine what is appropriate once they have measured and assessed the organizational risk appetite.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may mandate the frequency of scans for the organization. However, only parts of the organization may abide by that direction. Otherwise, the frequency of scanning may not properly align with the risk appetite or operational demands of the system.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy or procedure related to scanning in the environment
  • Documentation or logs that provide indication of scanning completion
  • Scanning results

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • VRRA: 10.3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-5

questions.title: WI:SG-1.Q3
questions.text: What technologies does the organization use to implement segmentation on computing platforms or hosts? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Question Intent: Identify and evaluate the organization’s use of techniques to isolate computing platforms or individual endpoints, as required, based on the sensitivity of the system or data.

Detonation Chamber: Detonation chambers, also known as dynamic execution environments, allow organizations to open email attachments, execute untrusted or suspicious applications, and execute Universal Resource Locator requests in the safety of an isolated environment or a virtualized sandbox. Protected and isolated execution environments provide a means of determining whether the associated attachments or applications contain malicious code. While related to the concept of deception nets, the employment of detonation chambers is not intended to maintain a long-term environment in which adversaries can operate and their actions can be observed. Rather, detonation chambers are intended to quickly identify malicious code and either reduce the likelihood that the code is propagated to user environments of operation or prevent such propagation completely.

Deception Net:

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has developed and executed a network segmentation strategy commensurate with the sensitivity levels of the systems and data. The assessment team should determine, collectively, the optimal network segmentation strategy for the system or application under assessment. If the system or application under assessment is reasonably isolated, in accordance with the optimal strategy, utilizing appropriate techniques to isolate computing platforms or individual endpoints, the response should be graded “Full Implementation.”

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • If the system or application under assessment is reasonably isolated, but there are other techniques that would more optimally implement the network segmentation strategy, the response should be graded “Partial Implementation.”
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Control implementation descriptions in the System Security Plan (SSP) describing the technologies used to achieve adequate computing platform or endpoint isolation

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST SP 800-160; NIST SP 800-53r5, SC-3(1), SC-7(29), SC-44
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-3(1), SC-7(29), SC-44, CM-7 (6)

questions.title: WI:SI-1.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization employ code-signing or other cryptographic mechanisms to affirm the validity of all executables before installation?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The employment of code-signing or other cryptographic mechanisms to affirm the validity of executables before installation can prevent supply chain insertion attacks.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization’s cyber security practices include the employment of code-signing or other cryptographic mechanisms to affirm the validity of software and firmware components.

Discussion: Software and firmware components are prevented from installation unless signed with recognized and approved certificates. Software and firmware components include software and firmware version updates, patches, service packs, device drivers, and basic input/output system updates. Organizations can identify applicable software and firmware components by type, by specific items, or a combination of both. Digital signatures and organizational verification of such signatures is a method of code authentication.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization can demonstrate the employment of code-signing or other cryptographic mechanisms to affirm the validity of all system software executables and firmware components before installation.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization can demonstrate the employment of code-signing or other cryptographic mechanisms to affirm the validity of some system software executables and firmware components before installation.  

Possible evidence:

  • A list of code-signing or other cryptographic mechanisms and associated procedures
  • Document out from the from the procedures detailing valid executables.  

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-160, Rev. 1

questions.title: WI:SI-2.Q3
questions.text: In accordance with organizationally defined requirements, does the organization prevent the installation of software and firmware components without verification that the component has been digitally signed using a certificate that is recognized and appropriate?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Software and firmware components should be prevented from installation unless signed with recognized and approved certificates include software and firmware version updates, patches, service packs, device drivers, and basic input/output system updates. Organizations can identify applicable software and firmware components by type, by specific items, or a combination of both. Digital signatures and organizational verification of such signatures is a method of code authentication.

Question Intent: Has the organization defined requirements to prevent the installation of software and firmware components without verification that the component has been digitally signed? Are these requirements documented in a policy or procedure?

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented requirements, in a policy or procedure, to prevent the installation of software and firmware components without verification that the component has been digitally signed. The organization presents evidence that installed software and firmware components are digitally signed.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization presents evidence that either installed software or installed firmware components are digitally signed but not both.   

Possible evidence

  • Documented requirements, in a policy or procedure, against installation of software and firmware components without verification that the component has been digitally signed.
  • Evidence that installed software and firmware components are digitally signed.

Reference to standards/source assessments

questions.title: RE:AN-2.Q3
questions.text: Is the impact to the organization's services assessed in the course of incident analysis?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Without information about how an incident has affected an organization, incident responders cannot accurately plan containment, remediation, or eradication efforts.

Question Intent: To determine if incident analysis includes assessing the impact of the incident on the organization. The purpose of impact analysis is to determine the breadth and severity of an incident to facilitate additional steps in the incident response process.

Incident management personnel may use the results of impact analysis to further prioritize incidents and related events during and after the triage process.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The impact on the organization is assessed for all incidents.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The impact on the organization is assessed for some incidents.

Possible evidence

  • Records of incident analyses containing impact assessments
  • Standardized forms or categories for recording and assessing impact

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: IR:G2.Q4.
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4

questions.title: RE:AN-4.Q3
questions.text: Are incidents prioritized?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Incident prioritization can help the organization understand, communicate, and manage the severity and potential impact that an incident might have on the organization.

Question Intent: To determine if incidents are prioritized within the incident response activity. Incidents may be prioritized by severity (e.g., critical, high, medium, low) or required response time, or other priorities.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization prioritizes all incidents relevant to the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization prioritizes some incidents

Possible evidence

  • A report, list, or document that illustrates incidents being prioritized in a meaningful way

questions.title: RE:AN-5.Q3
questions.text: Are vulnerabilities being actively discovered?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Vulnerability identification is a continuous activity which requires ongoing active discovery of vulnerabilities.

Question Intent: To determine if vulnerabilities are actively being discovered.

Vulnerabilities are discovered from an active review of the organization’s standard list of vulnerability sources.

Techniques used to discover vulnerabilities include:

  • performing internal vulnerability audits or assessments
  • performing assessments of external entities
  • reviewing the results of internal and external audits
  • periodically reviewing vulnerability catalogs, such as the US-CERT
  • reviewing notifications from identified vendor services
  • reviewing notifications from identified vulnerability services
  • reviewing reports from industry groups
  • using reports of vulnerabilities from other processes such as the organization’s service desk

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Vulnerabilities are actively being discovered for all assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Vulnerabilities are actively being discovered for some assets that support the critical service; OR;
  • Vulnerabilities are inconsistently being discovered for all assets that support the critical service.

Possible evidence

  • Vulnerability data and information
  • Vulnerability repository

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: VM:G2.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-5, PM-15

questions.title: RE:AM-1.Q3
questions.text:
Does the organization:
(a) Analyze communications traffic and event patterns for the system;
(b) Develop profiles representing common traffic and event patterns; and
(c) Use the traffic and event profiles in tuning system-monitoring devices?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Identifying and understanding common communications traffic and event patterns help organizations provide useful information to system monitoring devices to more effectively identify suspicious or anomalous traffic and events when they occur. Such information can help reduce the number of false positives and false negatives during system monitoring.

Question Intent: Does the organization perform activities a – c in support of continuous monitoring?

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented its performance of activities a – c in a policy or procedure.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented its performance of some of the a – c activities in a policy or procedure.

Possible evidence

  • Policy or procedure, evidence of its execution.

Reference to standards/source assessments

questions.title: RE:AM-3.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization analyze malicious code and/or other residual artifacts remaining in the system after the incident?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Understanding the kinds of malware being deployed against an organization can provide better insight into the organization’s threat landscape and further inform organizational threat intelligence and incident response functions.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization possesses malware analysis capabilities that are able to provide information about malicious code and/or other residual artifacts remaining in organizational systems after an incident.

  • When conducted carefully in an isolated environment, analysis of malicious code and other residual artifacts of a security incident or breach can give the organization insight into adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures.
  • Malicious code can also indicate the identity or provide defining characteristics of the adversary.
  • Information gleaned from malicious code analysis can help the organization develop responses to future incidents.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has mature in-house capabilities to perform analysis of malware and other forensic artifacts.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization is in the process of growing its in-house capabilities to perform analysis of malware and other forensic artifacts.

Possible evidence

  • Malware analysis reports.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4(12)

questions.title: RE:CO-1.Q3
questions.text: Are staff held accountable for performing event management on assets that support the organization’s critical services?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Personnel assigned the responsibility for event detection and reporting should be made aware of the assets that support the organization’s critical services and instructed to prioritize event management for these assets. Managers should initiate corrective measures to address all identified issues.

Question Intent: To ensure that event and incident handling and response personnel are aware of the assets that support the organization’s critical services and instructed to prioritize event management for these assets,

  • Managers are ultimately responsible for ensuring that incident response activities are performed properly. The immediate level of managers responsible for the process should review the event handling and response activities, status, and results, and identify issues.
  • These reviews are intended to provide the immediate level of managers with appropriate information about those activities.
  • The reviews can be:
  • periodic (for example, planned as part of a regular audit of the organization’s event handling capability or of an employee’s performance). The frequency to be defined by the organization.
  • event-driven (if needed, between periodic reviews).

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization periodically (as defined by the organization) evaluates all event handling and response activities and ensures that  staff prioritize assets that support the organization’s critical services.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has not established a review frequency for evaluating the event handling and response activities and ensuring that staff prioritize assets that support the organization’s critical services.
  • Or, only some staff are evaluated.
  • Or, only some of the event handling and response duties are evaluated.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation of reviews being held periodically to evaluate event handling and response activities and duties, results of event handling and response process audits.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: EH:G3.Q7
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, CP-3, IR-3, IR-8

questions.text: Are incidents declared?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Incident declaration defines the point at which the organization has established that an incident has occurred, is occurring, or is imminent.

Question Intent: To determine if incidents are declared.

  • Incident declaration may occur based on a specific event or when multiple events are occurring.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization declares all incidents relevant to the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization declares some incidents.

Possible evidence

  • Notification or ticketing demonstrating an incident being declared.

questions.title: RE:CO-3.Q3
questions.text: Are there documented information exchange interfaces in use with all internal and external stakeholders?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should ensure that information exchange interfaces among the groups involved in incident management functions are described and understood by all participants. Identify the appropriate communications protocols and channels (media and message) for each type of stakeholder. Various message types and levels of communications may be appropriate for various stakeholders.

Question Intent: To determine if there are documented methods of exchanging incident management information between incident handling and response personnel and internal and external stakeholders.

Information exchange interfaces are documented methods for the exchange of incident management information between stakeholders. The interfaces should define the type of inputs and outputs expected between the incident handling and response personnel and appropriate stakeholders.

  • Documented methods ensure that information exchange interfaces among the groups involved in incident management activities are described and understood by all participants.
  • Identify the appropriate communications protocols and media for each type of stakeholder, because message types and levels of communications may vary for stakeholders.
  • Documentation should identify member groups and define the incident management information that is exchanged (e.g., process, authority, mechanism). Mechanisms might include email exchanges, ticketing systems, or documented phone trees.
  • Examples of what would be documented include
  • the means of informing stakeholders (e.g., email, report, phone, etc.)
  • the feedback required/desired by the stakeholders (e.g., approval, review, etc.)
  • the way feedback from stakeholders should be provided (e.g., email, report, phone, etc.)
  • the frequency of communications between stakeholders
  • activities of the incident handling and response personnel and all internal and external stakeholders, to include roles and responsibilities for all parties

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Documented information exchange interfaces, to include roles and responsibilities for all parties, are in use with all internal and external stakeholders.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Documented information exchange interfaces, to include roles and responsibilities for all parties, are in use with some internal and external stakeholders.
  • Or, information exchange interfaces are in development and partially documented.

Possible evidence

  • Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), Memorandum of Agreement (MOA), Letter of Agreement (LOA), Service-Level Agreement (SLA), Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: PR:G3.Q1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CA-2, CA-7, CP-2, IR-4, IR-8, PE-6, RA-5, SI-4

questions.title: RE:CO-4.Q3
questions.text: Has a documented communication plan for incident management activities been established?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The organization should have a documented communication plan for its incident management activities. During an incident, it is critical that the designated people receive the appropriate information in a timely manner. The plan should include management notification, and incident response and coordination. The communication plan should also include guidance on internal and external communication requirements. This communication plan may be part of a larger organizational plan or crisis management plan.

Question Intent: To determine that a communication plan has been established and documented for use during incident management activities to assist with quick and effective response.

  • The communication plan for incident management activities may be incorporated into the organization’s larger communication plan and should be readily available to the incident handling and response personnel and appropriate stakeholders.
  • The incident management communication plan should include
  • the individuals, groups, and designated POCs to be contacted (both internal and external)
  • criteria for contacting and communicating with stakeholders
  • the process and mechanism for contacting each POC, including required secure mechanisms
  • the timeframe(s) for contacting (possibly guided by contracts, SLAs, or other regulatory guidance)
  • information that specifically should NOT be communicated externally
  • the approving authorities for external communication messages, where applicable
  • guidance that describes the handling of media questions and calls related to incidents and vulnerabilities

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented communication plan for incident management activities.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The communication plan is in development and partially documented.

Possible evidence

  • Documented communication plan for incident management activities

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: PR:G2.Q1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4, IR-8

questions.title: RE:CO-5.Q3
questions.text: Is threat information communicated to stakeholders?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Threat information must be communicated according to established requirements, including to stakeholders.

Question Intent: To determine if threat information is communicated to all identified internal and external stakeholders. The intent of communicating threat information is to ensure that the organization is operating under a common understanding of the threat environment.

  • Threat information must be communicated according to established requirements.
  • Communication requirements may dictate that various communications methods and channels should be considered and identified.
  • The infrastructure to support those methods may need to be developed and implemented.
  • Example methods of communicating threat information include:
  • threat communication standards and guidelines
  • standardized report templates
  • communication escalation protocols
  • communication channels (email, text, mobile phone, etc.)
  • Typical work products include:
  • list of stakeholders and contact information
  • stakeholder communication requirements
  • documented methods and channels (by stakeholder class or requirement)
  • tools and techniques for communication

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Threat information is communicated to all identified stakeholders as required.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Threat information is communicated to some of the identified stakeholders.
  • Or; some threat information is communicated to all identified stakeholders.

Possible evidence

  • List of stakeholders and contact information, stakeholder communication requirements, documented methods and channels (by stakeholder class or requirement), tools and techniques for communication

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: SA:G3.Q1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-5, PM-15

questions.title: RE:IM-1.Q3
questions.text: Are post-incident analysis reports generated and archived?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Post-incident analysis reports provide lessons learned and possible training material that should be used to improve the organization’s incident handling and response activities.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization generates post-incident analysis reports and stores them in a controlled manner.

  • It is important to document all lessons learned, the major points of agreement, and action items, and to communicate them to parties who could not attend the meeting. Lessons learned should be incorporated into incident response procedures, and training, and testing processes.
  • Lessons learned should be documented according to the organization’s required format and needs to meet any regulatory reporting requirements.
  • The report provides a reference that can be used to assist in handling similar incidents.
  • Reports from these meetings or reviews are good material for training new team members by showing them how more experienced team members respond to incidents

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Post incident analysis reports are documented and archived for all incidents that require a post incident review.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Post incident analysis reports are documented and archived for some incidents that require a post incident review.

Possible evidence

  • Documented and archived post-incident analysis reports.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: PI:G1.Q5.
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4, IR-8

questions.title: RE:IM-2.Q3
questions.text: Do key cyber personnel participate in the review and update process of the response strategies?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: It is important that organizations develop and implement a coordinated approach to incident response to address system and organizational changes and problems encountered during plan implementation, execution, or testing.

Question Intent: To determine if key cyber personnel participate in the review and update process of the response strategy/plan.

  • It is important that organizations develop and implement a coordinated approach to incident response.
  • An effective incident handling capability includes coordination among many organizational entities (e.g., mission or business owners, system owners, authorizing officials, human resources offices, physical security offices, personnel security offices, legal departments, risk executive [function], operations personnel, procurement offices, information security offices).
  • Update the incident response plan to address system and organizational changes or problems encountered during plan implementation, execution, or testing
  • Key cyber personnel can be:
  • information technology managers,
  • system and network administrators, and/or operations personnel,
  • procurement managers and personnel
  • Incident Response/Management
  • Disaster recovery
  • Data backup archive and recovery
  • Alternative site
  • Service Continuity

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All key cyber personnel have been identified and documented
  • And, all key personnel participate in the response strategy/plan review and update process.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A list of key cyber personnel is in development and partially documented.
  • Or, the list exists, but all key cyber personnel do not participate in the response strategy/plan review and update process.

Possible evidence

  • A documented list of key cyber personnel.  Note this list may be incorporated into the plan.
  • Documented response strategy/plan review reports showing the participation of the key cyber personnel.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: 10.2 C-IST Cybersecurity Plan. 
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4, IR-8

questions.title: RE:MI-2.Q3
questions.text: For vulnerabilities that cannot be fully mitigated, are they documented as accepted risks?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Managing and remediating legitimate vulnerabilities will help protect the organization from potential attacks by adversaries.

Question Intent: This question is trying to determine if the vulnerability management program properly responds to identified vulnerabilities.  More specifically, risk acceptance should be a meaningful decision where the rationale is documented and approved in accordance with the organizational risk appetite.

The organization must demonstrate that they are using risk-based decision making and documenting the result.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization must have a policy and procedure in place for the proper management of vulnerabilities.  More specifically, the organization must also demonstrate that it is properly following that procedure with demonstrable evidence that shows vulnerability identification and disposition.
  • The vulnerability may not be patched for any given circumstance.  If so, the organization must demonstrate that the choice of acceptance is done in accordance with risk management policy and appetite.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may have proper policy and procedure in place.  However, portions of the organization may not be properly discerning or executing prioritization decisions.
  • ·       Risk acceptance rationale may not be properly documented or reviewed to minimize risk exposure as threats and tactics shift.

Possible evidence

  • Policy and procedure related to vulnerability management
  • Risk management policy and procedure
  • Documentation or logs that provides evidence of risk analysis to include business impact analysis, threat analysis, and vulnerability assessment

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CA-7, RA-3, RA-5

questions.title: RE:RD-2.Q3
questions.text: Does the organization address surplus capacity in service-level agreements with external suppliers?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should ensure that their suppliers have enough surplus capacity to respond to sudden increases in the need for services. Suppliers that are unable to make these sorts of adjustments can increase an organization’s risk of degraded performance of its mission essential functions.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization addresses the delivery of surplus capacity (including spare parts) in formal agreements, such as service-level agreements, with external suppliers.

  • Maintain extra capacity, including spare parts where appropriate, for information storage, processing, or communications. Do not economize on resources; provide surge capacity.
  • Where possible, use diverse resources to provide surplus capacity (including spare system components).
  • Organizations should determine and document the suppliers that are required to supply or deliver surplus capacity for the critical service/HVA environment.
  • Service-level agreements define the expectations of performance, describe measurable outcomes, and identify remedies and response requirements for identified instances of noncompliance.
  • Types of agreements may include:
  • contracts
  • service level agreements
  • memoranda of agreement
  • purchase orders
  • licensing agreements
  • The agreement should:
  • be enforceable by the organization
  • include detailed and complete requirements that must be met by the external entity
  • include required performance standards and/or work products
  • be updated to reflect changes in requirements over the life of the relationship

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization includes requirements for the delivery of surplus capacity in service level agreements with all suppliers that are required to supply or deliver surplus capacity in support of the critical service/HVA environment.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization includes requirements for the delivery of surplus capacity in service level agreements with some of the suppliers that are required to supply or deliver surplus capacity in support of the critical service/HVA environment.

Possible evidence

  • Service level agreements with external suppliers
  • Contracts or purchase orders with external suppliers

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-160, Rev. 1 
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: MA-6, CP-2(2)

questions.title: RE:RD-3.Q3
questions.text: When transferring information between different security domains, implement content filtering solutions that provide redundant and independent filtering mechanisms for each data type.
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Redundant and independent content filtering systems eliminates a single point of failure.

Question Intent: To determine if redundant content filtering solutions have been implemented and that the solutions are independent or use different code base and supporting libraries.

  • Content filtering is the process of inspecting information as it traverses a cross-domain solution and determines if the information meets a predefined policy.
  • Redundant and independent content filtering eliminates a single point of failure filtering system.
  • Independence is defined as the implementation of a content filter that uses a different code base and supporting libraries (e.g., two JPEG filters using different vendors’ JPEG libraries) and multiple, independent system processes.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Redundant and independent content filtering mechanisms are implemented for each data type when transferring information to and from the critical service/HVA environment security zone(s).

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Redundant and independent content filtering mechanisms are implemented for some of the data types when transferring information to and from the critical service/HVA environment security zone(s).
  • Or, redundant content filtering mechanisms are implemented but they are not independent in their design.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the implementation and configuration of the redundant and independent content filtering mechanisms.
  • Log files showing the operation of each independent content filtering mechanism.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-4(27)

questions.title: AD:CO-3.Q4
questions.text: Are staff are assigned authority and accountability for carrying out the communications plan?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The diverse and expansive nature of communications requirements for supporting Incident management and recovery processes requires knowledgeable, skilled, and experienced staff to be successful.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization’s communications plans associated with incident management and recovery include staffing that is formally assigned and held accountable for its performance.

Resources must be available in the organization to staff or support all types of communications as needed. Internal communications and public relations activities tend to be carried out by communications professionals—staff who have specific training and skills in communications and who work primarily in communications roles in the organization. Notification, escalation, and coordination of communications may be carried out by anyone in the organization who is in a primary or supporting incident response or recovery management role. Thus, staff on an incident response team may be involved in communications roles because of the nature of their work. These types of communications are typically supported by a communications infrastructure and knowledgeable staff who support the infrastructure or are trained in effective communications during times of stress and disruption.

Regardless of the communications type, the organization must provide training (sometimes specialized) to staff who support and enable communications processes. This may begin with a skills inventory and gap analysis so that effective training programs can be identified and used. For staff involved in communications roles during the execution of service continuity plans, communications training may be extensive and may involve frequent exercises and tests to ensure effectiveness.

Communications resources may be internal or external to the organization. Thus, where the organization does not have direct control over communications resources, it must attempt to ensure that proper training is provided to carry out plan and program requirements.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All staff required for incident and recovery communications have their authority, responsibilities, and accountability formally documented.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some staff required for incident and recovery communications are documented, or their authority, responsibility, and accountability information is incomplete. (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Job descriptions for roles and responsibilities in the plan
  • List of available and skilled resources
  • List of skill and resource gaps
  • Mitigation plans to address skill and resource gaps
  • Updated communications plan with resources assigned

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CERT RMM COMM:SG2.SP3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4

questions.title: AD:RL-2.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization impose requirements on and perform oversight of external system services?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The responsibility for managing risks from the use of external system services remains with the organization’s authorizing officials.

Question Intent: To determine if (1) the organization requires providers of external system services to comply with organizational requirements and (2) if the organization performs oversight of those services.

  • Require that providers of external system services comply with organizational security and privacy requirements.
  • Define and document organizational oversight and user roles and responsibilities with regard to external system services.
  • External system services are provided by an external provider, and the organization has no direct control over the implementation of the required controls or the assessment of control effectiveness.
  • For services external to organizations, a chain of trust requires that organizations establish and retain a certain level of confidence that each provider in the consumer-provider relationship provides adequate protection for the services rendered.
  • Organizations document the basis for the trust relationships so that the relationships can be monitored.
  • External system services documentation includes government, service providers, end user security roles and responsibilities, and service-level agreements.
  • Service-level agreements define the expectations of performance for implemented controls, describe measurable outcomes, and identify remedies and response requirements for identified instances of noncompliance.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has identified and documented security and privacy control requirements for all appropriate external system services.

AND

  • The organization enforces those requirements for all appropriate external system services.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization is in the process of identifying and documenting security and privacy control requirements for all appropriate external system services. 
     OR
  • The organization has identified and documented security and privacy control requirements but is in the process of establishing enforcement of those requirements for all appropriate external system services.

Possible Evidence

  • Documented organizational oversight and user roles and responsibilities with regard to external system services.
  • Documented requirements that external service providers must comply with.
  • Agreements with the external providers that define performance expectations
  • Documented results from the review of external provider performance.

Reference to standards/source assessments:

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SA-9

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:AR-1.Q4
questions.text: Do IDS solutions employ a capability to update analysis based on sources of threat intelligence?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: IDS solutions are not static and need to be regularly updated to address current and relevant threats.

Question Intent: Determine if the system is utilizing a data source to inform IDS detection rulesets based on current and relevant information. 

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Threat intelligence feeds are used to inform IDS rulesets.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • IDS are in place but do not incorporate threat intelligence data.

Possible Evidence

  • System Security Plans, Runbooks for IDS

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-6(1), PM-16(1)

questions.title: AN:AR-2.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization have the capability to deploy storage or compute resources dynamically?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Static system resources introduce bottlenecks in terms of accessibility and capacity.

Question Intent: Determine if the system dynamically deploys storage or compute resources. Managing capacity ensures that sufficient capacity is available to counter flooding attacks. Managing capacity includes establishing selected usage priorities, quotas, partitioning, or load balancing.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization can deploy both storage and compute resources, as needed, for all system components without intervention.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization can provision storage and compute resources, but that capability requires direct human intervention.

Possible Evidence

  • System Security Plans

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-4(3), SC-5(2), CP-13

questions.title: AN:BE-3.Q4
questions.text: Are services and assets prioritized based on analysis of the potential impact if the services are disrupted?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: This question is asked to understand the prioritization criteria. Services should be prioritized based on potential impact, otherwise one could perform prioritization that is simply done based on tradition, politics, or other factors.

Question Intent: Determine if services and facilities are prioritized based on analysis of potential impact.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization must have documented prioritization of facilities or services.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A prioritization scheme exists, but there is no list of prioritized facilities or services.
  • All services and facilities have a business impact analysis, but there is no list of prioritized facilities or services.

Possible Evidence

  • Prioritized list of high-value organizational services, activities, and associated assets
  • Results of security risk assessment and business impact analyses

questions.text: Are dependencies on external relationships that are critical to the service identified?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: This question is asked to assess whether the organization tracks its dependencies on external relationships that are critical to the high value service.

Question Intent: Determine if dependencies on external relationships that are critical to critical services are identified

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • List of external dependencies and entities is documented and there is a documented process for updating this.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • List of external dependencies and entities is only partial, or only for some critical services.

Possible Evidence

  • List of external dependencies and entities
  • Documented process for updating the list of external dependencies and entities.

questions.title: AN:BE-5.Q4
questions.text: Select the time interval at which the organization reviews and updates resilience requirements for all external dependencies. If the time intervals vary from among dependencies, select the longest interval. (Select one)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Frequent changes in the cybersecurity landscape require regular updates in resilience requirements if an organization is going to maintain its resilience posture.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization has a process to periodically review and update resilience requirements for infrastructure providers that support the critical service.

  • The organization’s dependence on infrastructure providers may change in scope and importance based on business and service considerations, or on factors outside the acquirer’s control. Therefore, it is important that the acquirer has a process to periodically review and update resilience requirements for infrastructure providers.
  • Periodically means that the acquirer has a documented time interval for the activity.
  • Having an established process means that:
  • There are specific steps or activities that acquirer staff must complete.
  • The process is supported by appropriate documentation. For example, there may be a documented schedule of meetings to identify requirements.
  • The acquirer’s staff is aware that the process exists and that they are expected to follow it.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Responsibility for monitoring the performance of each infrastructure provider that supports the critical service has been assigned.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Responsibility for monitoring the performance of some infrastructure providers has been assigned, or the practice appears otherwise incomplete.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Internal policy or command media documenting activity and period
  • Notes from recurring meetings
  • Internal correspondence
  • Staff job descriptions assigning responsibility

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • EDM: RMG:G6.Q1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, CP-2(7), SR-1, SR-3, SR-7

questions.title: AN:CP-1.Q4
questions.text: Are both network and host-based intrusion detection employed for the protection of the HVA/critical service?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Network and host-based intrusion detection systems should be employed concurrently as they can detect different activity.

Question Intent: This question will determine if the organization employs both network and host-based intrusion detection solutions.

  • Host-based intrusion detection systems monitor the activity of a single host for anomalous and suspicious behavior.
  • Network-based intrusion detection systems monitor network traffic for abnormal and suspicious network activity.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization employs both network and host-based intrusion detection solutions for the protection of critical services infrastructure and high value assets.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization employs a network-based or host-based intrusion detection solution. However, they do not utilize both.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Software inventory for the organization showing licenses for host-based and network-based IDS solutions, Device configurations.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-2(1)
  • NIST 800-160, Rev. 1

questions.title: AN:CP-2.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization coordinate contingency plan development with organizational elements responsible for related plans?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: incident response plans, business continuity plans, disaster recovery plans, and contingency plans are all related, therefore their development should be coordinated with each other.

Question Intent: if the organization coordinates contingency plan development with organizational elements responsible for related plans.

Organizational elements responsible for related plans may include

  • Cloud service providers
  • Incident response teams
  • Business continuity teams
  • Hot/warm/cold site providers
  • IT administrators responsible for backup management solutions

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization coordinates the development of contingency plan with all organizational elements responsible for related plans.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization coordinates the development of contingency plan with some organizational elements responsible for related plans.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Attestation from applicable personnel that multiple organizational elements are involved in the development of contingency plans, incident response plans, business continuity plans, and disaster recovery plans.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-6(7)
