questions.title: AN:CP-3.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization coordinate incident handling activities involving supply chain events with other organizations involved in the supply chain?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: If an organization experiences an incident due to a vulnerability that affects other organizations involved in the supply chain, there are specific reporting channels and processes the organization should follow to ensure responsible disclosure of the vulnerability.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization coordinates its incident handling activities that involve supply chain events with other organizations involved in the supply chain

Organizations involved in supply chain activities include product developers, system integrators, manufacturers, packagers, assemblers, distributors, vendors, and resellers. Supply chain incidents can occur anywhere through or to the supply chain and include compromises or breaches that involve primary or sub-tier providers, information technology products, system components, development processes or personnel, and distribution processes or warehousing facilities. Organizations consider including processes for protecting and sharing incident information in information exchange agreements and their obligations for reporting incidents to government oversight bodies (e.g., Federal Acquisition Security Council).

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization coordinates all incident handling activities involving supply chain events with other organizations involved in the supply chain.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization coordinates some incident handling activities involving supply chain events with other organizations involved in the supply chain.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Supply chain risk management plan, communications management plan

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4(10)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:CP-4.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization employ a penetration testing process that includes attempts to bypass or circumvent controls associated with physical access points to the facility?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Contingency plans should be tested to ensure that protections are implemented properly.

Question Intent: This question seeks to determine if the organization tests systems using planned disruptions that have an adverse effect on system performance to validate that the protections in place are effective.

  • Example: Stress testing can be used to test the efficacy of load balancing solutions.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • the organization tests all relevant systems using planned disruptions that have an adverse effect on system performance to validate that the protections in place are effective.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • the organization tests some systems using planned disruptions that have an adverse effect on system performance to validate that the protections in place are effective.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Reports or documentation created as a result of contingency plan tests.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CA-8(2), CP-4(5)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:DI-2.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization employ out-of-band channels for the physical delivery or electronic transmission of organization-defined information, system components, or devices to organization-defined individuals or systems?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: To improve security, organizations may employ out-of-band channels in the delivery or transmission of organizational items, including authenticators and credentials; cryptographic key management information; system and data backups; etc.  

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization employs out-of-band channels for the physical delivery or electronic transmission of organization-defined information, system components, or devices to organization-defined individuals or systems. 

Out-of-band channels include local, non-network accesses to systems; network paths physically separate from network paths used for operational traffic; or non-electronic paths, such as the U.S. Postal Service. 

The use of out-of-band channels is contrasted with the use of in-band channels (i.e., the same channels) that carry routine operational traffic. Out-of-band channels do not have the same vulnerability or exposure as in-band channels. Therefore, the confidentiality, integrity, or availability compromises of in-band channels will not compromise or adversely affect the out-of-band channels.

Organizations may employ out-of-band channels in the delivery or transmission of organizational items, including authenticators and credentials; cryptographic key management information; system and data backups; configuration management changes for hardware, firmware, or software; security updates; maintenance information; and malicious code protection updates.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has implemented and is employing out-of-band channels for the physical delivery or electronic transmission of organization-defined information, system components, or devices to organization-defined individuals or systems.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization is in the process of implementing out-of-band channels for the physical delivery or electronic transmission of organization-defined information, system components, or devices.

Possible Evidence

  • Documented process showing the setup and use of out-of-band channels for the physical delivery or electronic transmission of organization-defined information, system components, or devices to organization-defined individuals or systems.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-37

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:DI-3.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization take measures to ensure an adequate supply of critical system components?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Adversaries can attempt to impede organizational operations by disrupting the supply of critical system components or corrupting supplier operations.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization identifies critical system components and takes measures to ensure the adequate supply of those components 

The results from a supply chain risk assessment can guide and inform the strategies, tools, and methods that are most applicable to the situation.

Organizations may track systems and component mean time to failure to mitigate the loss of temporary or permanent system function.

Controls to ensure that adequate supplies of critical system components include:

  • the use of multiple suppliers throughout the supply chain for the identified critical components
  • stockpiling spare components to ensure operation during mission-critical times
  • the identification of functionally identical or similar components that may be used, if necessary.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented and implemented measures (controls) to ensure an adequate supply of critical system components.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented and implemented some measures (controls) to ensure an adequate supply of critical system components.

Possible Evidence

  • A list of supply chain related controls and associated documentation related to ensuring an adequate supply of critical system components.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SR-5(1)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q4
questions.text: Is there a documented policy for vulnerability management?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should have a documented policy for vulnerability management as it establishes the organizational expectations for planning and performing the vulnerability management process as well as communicates those expectations to the organization.

Question Intent: This question determines if a policy for performing vulnerability management activities exists.

A policy is a written communication from the organization’s senior management to employees.

The vulnerability management policy should address:

  • responsibility, authority, ownership, and the requirement to perform vulnerability management activities
  • establishment of procedures, standards, and guidelines
  • requirements for periodically assessing the vulnerability management activities
  • measuring adherence to policy, exceptions granted, and policy violations
  • compliance with legal, regulatory, contractual, and government obligations

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented policy for performing vulnerability management.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A policy is in development and partially documented
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation) 

Possible Evidence

  • A Standard Operating Procedure for vulnerability Management or Other relevant organizational policy covering vulnerability management.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: VM:MIL2.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-1, RA-5

questions.title: AN:GV-2.Q1
questions.text: Have stakeholders for asset management activities been identified and made aware of their roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Stakeholders are more likely to be invested in asset management activities when they are well informed and aware of their roles in the process.

Question Intent: This question determines if stakeholders for asset management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Stakeholders of the asset management process have the following responsibilities:

  • creating an asset inventory baseline
  • associating assets with the critical service
  • overseeing the asset management process
  • managing the risk resulting from unresolved problems (gaps in the inventory of asset protection and sustainment requirements, insufficient staffing, or funding, etc.)

Examples of stakeholders include:

  • critical service owners
  • asset management staff
  • owners and custodians of assets that underpin the service (to include facility security personnel)
  • critical service staff
  • external entities responsible for some part of the service
  • information technology staff
  • human resources
  • internal and external auditors

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All stakeholders for the asset management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some stakeholders for the asset management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.
  • Or, stakeholders are identified but have not been made aware of their roles.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation) 

Possible Evidence

  • A Standard Operating Procedure for asset management or other relevant organizational policy that includes a section on roles and responsibilities for asset management functions

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: AM:MIL2.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PS-7, PM-1, PM-2

questions.title: AN:GV-3.Q4
questions.text: Is there a process to ensure event evidence is handled as required by law or other obligations?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Failure to comply with statutory requirements for evidence handling can result in legal ramifications. Therefore, it is critical that organizations abide by the industry-specific, national, regional, and state regulations for the areas in which the organization operates.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has implemented a process to ensure event evidence is handled as required by law or other obligations.

Based on applicable requirements the organization should develop a process using standards and guidelines for the collection, documentation, and preservation of event evidence. 

Staff should be trained on the organizational process for proper identification and handling of evidence to ensure that the evidence is not altered, and that integrity is maintained. 

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • There is a documented process to ensure event evidence is handled as required by law or other obligations.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A process is in development and partially documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Incident response plan, Standard Operating Procedure for Incident Management, or Other relevant organizational policy covering incident management.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: IM:G2.Q9
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-1, IR-8(1), AU-10

questions.title: AN:GV-4.Q4
questions.text: Is there adequate funding to perform vulnerability management activities as planned?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Funding is an indication of higher-level management support and sponsorship of vulnerability management activities

Question Intent: This question determines if adequate funding has been provided for vulnerability management activities. The intent of the question is to evaluate the completeness of the funding, not the completeness of the plan.

Funding should be available to support the proper oversight, execution, and maintenance of vulnerability management activities

Considerations for funding planned vulnerability management activities include:

  • defining funding needs
  • establishing a budget
  • resolving funding gaps
  • funding the process activities including staffing, tools, training, etc.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Adequate funding has been provided to perform all planned vulnerability management activities.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The planned activities have only been partially funded.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  •  Attestation from stakeholders regarding funding for vulnerability management activities.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: VM:MIL3.Q3

questions.title: AN:RA-1.Q4
questions.text: Do personnel check the identified trusted sources of information on a daily or weekly basis?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Incident management personnel should look for evidence of regular monitoring of a variety of security, news, and other trusted sites for information related to computing technologies, attacks, and threats, and for socio-political, economic, or legal information related to malicious computer security events and incidents.

Question Intent: This question determines if organization personnel are monitoring trusted sources of information relevant to the security of the organization.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • There is checking of trusted sources of information on a daily to weekly basis.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • There is checking of trusted sources of information only occasionally and not regularly conducted. (Monthly or Quarterly basis)
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Demonstrations of research and monitoring of identified websites
  • Mechanisms or methods used to monitor, synthesize, and disseminate information
  • Records of gathered information
  • Addresses or lists of websites monitored, including security, “black-hat,” news, and legal websites and archives

  • The information that has been captured through monitoring activities has been archived in a searchable form.

  • The information that has been captured through monitoring activities has been archived in an unsearchable form.

questions.title: AN:RA-3.Q4
questions.text: Does guidance exist for assessing the level of risk and corresponding impact relative to the constituency?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Business units and individuals need to understand what threats or vulnerabilities might impact them, the associated level of risk, and how to protect against or mitigate them. Incident management personnel work to provide such notifications and warnings to promote awareness of threats and malicious activity and to help support organizational response actions.

Question Intent: To determine if incident management has created guidance for assessing the level of risk and corresponding impact relative to the constituency.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Guidance exists for assessing the level of risk and corresponding impact relative to the constituency.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Guidance is being developed for assessing the level of risk and corresponding impact relative to the constituency.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Copies of threats, warnings, advisories, event/incident notifications, and so forth. that were sent to organizational stakeholders, business units, or relevant external parties
  • Mechanisms, with instructions and examples, for notifying the organization about current or potential events/incidents (e.g., email, web, mailing list, text, SMS)
  • Documented sources for information-gathering on current and potential threats and attacks

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has identified and implemented standards and guidelines for risk management activities.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has identified standards and guidelines for risk management activities,

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

questions.title: AN:SC-1.Q4
questions.text: Are resilience requirements included in formal agreements with external entities?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: External entity performance should be monitored to identify any performance gaps that may pose a risk to the acquirer. This monitoring should inform any corrective actions that must be undertaken by the supplier to remedy identified performance issues.

Question Intent: This question determines if corrective actions are taken to address issues with the performance of external entities (as related to resilience requirements). The intent of any corrective action is to minimize disruption to the critical service.

The range of corrective actions should be established in the agreement with the external entity.

Typical work products include:

  • corrective action reports or documentation
  • correspondence with an external entity documenting corrective actions

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has taken corrective actions to address performance issues for all external entities that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has taken corrective actions to address performance issues for some external entities
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Corrective action reports or documentation, correspondence with an external entity documenting corrective actions

questions.title: WI:AC-1.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization prohibit the use of fixed or default authenticators in system components?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Use of known/fixed/default passwords and credentials significantly elevates the risk that an attacker can compromise a given system.

Question Intent: To determine if fixed or default passwords are prohibited from use in the system.

Network equipment and some software often ship with default passwords that are generally known or easily discoverable. Before that equipment or software is deployed, and especially before it is exposed to a public network, the default authenticators (both usernames and passwords) must be changed.

Organizations can work with their supply chains to change default authenticators prior to shipping, or they can change them after receiving the system, but before deployment.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Default authenticators are changed for all system components.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Default passwords are changed for all system components with some usernames remaining unchanged.

Possible evidence

  • Supplier contracts or bills of sale indicating authenticator change.
  • Shipping documentation indicating non-default authenticator
  • IT service tickets indicating authenticator changes
  • System or software configuration procedures indicating a requirement for authenticator changes

Anonymous access to public-facing websites or document repositories is not included under this control if all content at those locations is intended for public consumption.

  • “All users” is selected.  All users would include contractors and other third parties.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

questions.title: WI:IP-9.Q4
questions.text: The organization has a defined disaster recovery plan, which (at a minimum) contains: (Select one)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: A disaster recovery (DR) plan provides the organization with a roadmap for restoring disrupted services. A formal, coordinated approach to service restoration helps ensure smooth resumption of operations in a crisis.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization has a documented DR plan

  • The DR plan should address the identification, analysis, and response to a service disruption.
  • An incident is one or more occurrences that affect organizational assets and have the potential to disrupt operations.
  • An incident significantly impacts the mission critical service and requires the organization to respond to prevent or limit impact to the critical service and the organization.
  • An incident may result from an event or a series of events that requires a response that is beyond standard operating procedures for managing events.
  • An effective DR plan includes coordination among many organizational entities (e.g., mission or business owners, system owners, authorizing officials, human resources offices, physical security offices, personnel security offices, legal departments, risk executive [function], operations personnel, procurement offices).
  • DR plans typically identify specific hardware, software, and other technology resources and how they are to be recovered in specific scenarios.
  • The organization must plan for how it will:
  • Identify events and incidents
  • Analyze these events and incidents and determine an appropriate response
  • Develop incident declaration criteria
  • Respond to incidents
  • Communicate incident information to stakeholders
  • Staff the plan to meet plan objectives
  • Structure the incident management staff (including roles and responsibilities)
  • Train staff to identify, analyze, and respond to incidents

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • There is a documented disaster recovery plan.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented some procedures and roles but lacks a comprehensive disaster recovery plan.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Documented DR plan.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: Q.25.1

Assigned roles but no documented procedures

questions.title: WI:MA-1.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization have any assets that are end-of-life or out of vendor support such that they are ineligible for security or stability updates? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Controlling system maintenance addresses the information security aspects of the system maintenance program and applies to all types of maintenance conducted by local or nonlocal entities. Determining assets that are out of vendor support is an important aspect as these assets pose a security risk to the organization.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization has assets that are currently end-of-life or out of vendor support.

  • Schedule, document, and review records of maintenance, repair, and replacement on system components, including assets that are out of vendor support, in accordance with manufacturer or vendor specifications and/or organizational requirements
  • Approve and monitor all maintenance activities, whether performed on site or remotely and whether the system or system components are serviced on site or removed to another location
  • Require the explicit approval of the removal of the system or system components from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, or replacement
  • Sanitize equipment to remove organization-defined information from associated media prior to removal from organizational facilities,

  • No elements are checked, that is, no assets that support the critical service/HVA environment are end-of-life or out of vendor support.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • There are some assets at end-of-life, but the organization has mitigation plans in place to reduce the associated risk.

questions.title: WI:NP-1.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization employ minimal functionality and information storage on organization-defined system components?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Disallowing writeable storage eliminates the possibility of malicious code insertion via persistent, writeable storage within the designated system components.

Question Intent: to determine if system components with non-writeable storage that is persistent across component restart or power on/off are employed where feasible for organization-defined system components.

  • The operating environment for a system contains the code that hosts applications, including operating systems, executives, or virtual machine monitors (i.e., hypervisors). It can also include certain applications that run directly on hardware platforms.
  • The use of non-modifiable storage ensures the integrity of software from the point of creation of the read-only image.
  • Hardware-enforced, read-only media include Compact Disc-Recordable (CD-R) and Digital Versatile Disc-Recordable (DVD-R) disk drives as well as one-time, programmable, read-only memory.
  • The use of reprogrammable, read-only memory can be accepted as read-only media provided that integrity can be adequately protected from the point of initial writing to the insertion of the memory into the system, and there are reliable hardware protections against reprogramming the memory while installed in organizational systems

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has implemented system components with no writeable storage that is persistent across component restart or power on/off for all organization-defined system components that support the critical service/HVA.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has implemented system components with no writeable storage that is persistent across component restart or power on/off for some organization-defined system components that support the critical service/HVA.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the implementation and configuration of system components no writeable storage that is persistent across component restart or power on/off for those components that support the critical service/HVA environment

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53 SC-34(1)

questions.title: WI:PR-1.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization employ organization-defined data mining prevention and detection techniques for  organization-defined data storage objects to detect and protect against unauthorized data mining?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Unauthorized data mining and/or exfiltration can be extremely difficult to detect and may require tools or techniques specifically targeted at the problem.

Question Intent: Determine if data mining prevention and detection techniques are defined and implemented, and if data storage objects to be protected against unauthorized data mining are defined.

Discussion: Data mining is an analytical process that attempts to find correlations or patterns in large data sets for the purpose of data or knowledge discovery. Data storage objects include database records and database fields. Sensitive information can be extracted from data mining operations. When information is personally identifiable information, it may lead to unanticipated revelations about individuals and give rise to privacy risks. Prior to performing data mining activities, organizations determine whether such activities are authorized. Organizations may be subject to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, or policies that address data mining requirements. 

Organizational personnel consult with the senior agency official for privacy and legal counsel regarding such requirements.

Data mining prevention and detection techniques include limiting the number and frequency of database queries to increase the work factor needed to determine the contents of databases, limiting types of responses provided to database queries, applying differential privacy techniques or homomorphic encryption, and notifying personnel when atypical database queries or accesses occur. Data mining protection focuses on protecting information from data mining while such information resides in organizational data stores. In contrast, AU-13 focuses on monitoring for organizational information that may have been mined or otherwise obtained from data stores and is available as open-source information residing on external sites, such as social networking or social media websites.

EO 13587 requires the establishment of an insider threat program for deterring, detecting, and mitigating insider threats, including the safeguarding of sensitive information from exploitation, compromise, or other unauthorized disclosure. Data mining protection requires organizations to identify appropriate techniques to prevent and detect unnecessary or unauthorized data mining. Data mining can be used by an insider to collect organizational information for the purpose of exfiltration.

Definition of any key words with examples:

  • Data mining: an analytical process that attempts to find correlations or patterns in large data sets for the purpose of data or knowledge discovery.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Data mining prevention and detection techniques are defined; and
  • Data storage objects to be protected against unauthorized data mining are defined; and
  • Data mining prevention and detection techniques are implemented; and
  • Identified data storage objects, from (b), are protected against unauthorized data mining, using (c).

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Data mining prevention and detection techniques are implemented, as per (c), but only against less than 80% of data storage objects identified in (b).

Possible evidence

  • Access control policy; procedures for preventing and detecting data mining; policies and procedures addressing authorized data mining techniques; procedures addressing protection of data storage objects against data mining; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; system audit logs; system audit records; procedures addressing differential privacy techniques; notifications of atypical database queries or accesses; documentation or reports of insider threat program; system security plan; privacy plan.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53 AC-23

questions.title: WI:PR-3.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization prevent organization-defined software from executing at higher privilege levels than users executing the software?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: If software executes at a higher privilege level than the people using the software, that may allow the users higher levels of access than they otherwise would be granted.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization prevents organization-defined software from executing at higher privilege levels than users executing the software.

Discussion: In certain situations, software applications or programs need to execute with elevated privileges to perform required functions. However, depending on the software functionality and configuration, if the privileges required for execution are at a higher level than the privileges assigned to organizational users invoking such applications or programs, those users may indirectly be provided with greater privileges than assigned.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Software to be prevented from executing at higher privilege levels than users executing the software is defined; and
  • Software defined above is prevented from executing at higher privilege levels than users executing the software.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A limited set of software is prevented from executing at higher privilege levels than users executing the software, but there is no comprehensive enterprise review of software to ensure no software executes at higher privilege levels than users executing the software.

Possible evidence

  • Access control policy; procedures addressing least privilege; list of software that should not execute at higher privilege levels than users executing software; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; system audit records; system security plan.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-6(8)

Question Intent: Determine if the event data repository is protected from unauthorized modification or deletion.

  • A subset of privileged users or roles are able to access, modify or delete the event data repository though they have not been reviewed or approved for this.

Possible evidence

Audit and accountability policy; system security plan; privacy plan; access control policy and procedures; procedures addressing protection of audit information; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; system-generated list of privileged users with read-only access to audit information; access authorizations; access control list; system audit records.

questions.title: WI:CM-1.Q4
questions.text: For what purpose does the organization perform monitoring in regard to the system? (Check all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Situational awareness for threats is directly related to the critical assets of the organization as they support achievement of organizational objectives. Therefore, the organization must have a clear connection between its organizational strategic objectives and the value delivered by continuous monitoring.

Question Intent: This question seeks out the connection between the organizational strategy and the fundamental functions of the Continuous Monitoring System. The criteria provided by the question provide some of the hallmark features provided by most programs.

Continuous monitoring may utilize tools that perform logging, alerting, and reporting.

Alternative terms used could include “ConMon” or an abbreviation of “Continuous Monitoring”. See also “CSM” for “Continuous Security Monitoring”.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • A Full Implementation would include all aspects of the following criteria:
    •  Problem/event identification
    • Performance monitoring
    • Configuration control
    • Data loss monitoring
    • Threat/incident monitoring

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may demonstrate some of the elements listed.
  • Alternatively, the organization may conduct operations that support all of the criteria listed above. However, the implementation may not be adequate based upon poor use of the tool, improper tool configuration, or limited resources for application implementation.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Reports that are result of the activities from the criteria listed
  • Operator demonstration of specific activities for any of the listed criteria
  • Automated activity that delivers the above criteria may be evident in operational logs or reports

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: Q.20.2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-2, AU-12, CA-7, CM-3, SC-5, SC-7, SI-4

questions.title: WI:CM-4.Q4
questions.text: Are anti-virus/malware scans conducted on a periodic basis across the complete extent of the organization’s information technology environment?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations must continuously monitor their systems and related networks to prevent the intrusion of threat actors and avoid the injection of malicious code. Scanning enables and organization to monitor for malicious code injection and avoid significant breach.

Question Intent: The question tries to determine the malicious code scanning practices of the organization as it relates to continuous monitoring practices.

Scanning and testing help organizations reduce their exposure to threats by evaluating external network presence by monitoring public, static Ips for accessible services and vulnerabilities. Similarly, application scanning seeks out known and publicly accessible websites for bugs and improper configuration. Once discovered, the identified vulnerabilities can be prioritized and addressed in accordance with the organizational risk appetite.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has and properly utilizes tools to conduct regular scanning for vulnerabilities. Policy and procedure exist to guide the workforce in appropriate scanning practices. Documentation or logs reflect those scans are conducted in a timely fashion. Tools are updated on a periodic basis to ensure that new vulnerabilities are detected before risks may come to fruition.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has the proper tools and policies that enable scanning. However, the organization may fail to properly configure the tools or update them with any regular periodicity. Scans may take place, but the organization fails to prioritize and act upon necessary patching.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Organizational policies and procedures that direct the proper use of scanning tools
  • Documentation or logs that indicate scanning activities
  • Scanning activity results along with evidence of disposition and risk-based decisions to patch vulnerabilities

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53: SI-3, SI-8

questions.title: WI:CM-7.Q4
questions.text: How does the organization monitor for unauthorized connections? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Unauthorized operations in the network must be eliminated as soon as it is identified. This includes proper monitoring for unauthorized connections, devices/hardware, and/or software installations. By monitoring for these events, the organization should avoid a variety of potentially successful cyber-attacks and exploitation.

Question Intent: This question is trying to identify practices that look for unauthorized connections to other networks.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization must have policy or procedure that mandates the use of tools and practices that regularly monitor for unauthorized connections. Similarly, the policy should call out and define what a “cyber-relevant time frame” is for the organization in terms of response in accordance with the organizational risk appetite.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may have policy or procedure that mandates the use of tools and practices that regularly monitor for unauthorized connections. However, the organization may fail to do so in a consistent and standardized manner. Furthermore, the organization may lack the ability to respond in a timely manner. (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy and procedure related to consistent monitoring of the organization’s networks
  • Documentation and or logs that demonstrate regular monitoring
  • Documentation or logs that provide information related to timely responses to alerts

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53: AU-12, CA-7, CM-3, CM-8, PE-3, PE-6, PE-20, SI-4

The organization does not monitor for unauthorized connections

questions.title: WI:CM-8.Q4
questions.text: How often are vulnerability signatures/indicators updated? (Select one)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Vulnerabilities and malware, among other risk elements, can be identified in a variety of ways, which enables automated scanning and other methods that may prevent threat actors from exploiting them before being identified. Once identified, scanning information may be promulgated to many organizations as warning and to enable others to respond accordingly. These practices may not be entirely effective unless the signatures are updated as new vulnerabilities, malware, etc. are identified.

Question Intent: This question is trying to determine if the organization regularly updates their scanning tools for most recent signatures and related indicators.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization conducts regular updates to their scanning tools. This also means that emerging, urgent signature updates are conducting in a timely fashion.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may be updating their scanning tools. However, this may not be done in a proper or timely manner, which would expose the organization to potential threats.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Scanning tools implemented in the organization
  • Demonstration that the scanning tools are regularly updated

Reference to standards/source assessments

questions.title: WI:SG-1.Q4
questions.text: Are decisions on how to segment based on analysis of risk, criticality, and trustworthiness?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: An effective network, computing platform, and system segmentation strategy is informed by an analysis of system and data sensitivity, threats, and risks.

Question Intent: Determine how the organization developed the network, computing platform, and system segmentation strategy.

Dynamic Segmentation and Isolation: Change the configuration of enclaves or protected segments, or isolate resources while minimizing operational disruption.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization conducted an analysis of system and data sensitivity, threats, and risks to inform the development of a comprehensive segmentation strategy that addresses network, computing platform, and system segmentation, in accordance with an organizational cyber security strategy or policy.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization conducted an analysis of system and data sensitivity, threats, and risks to inform the development of a segmentation strategy. However, the strategy is not comprehensive or was not developed in accordance with an organizational cyber security strategy or policy.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Analysis documents, segmentation strategy, Control implementation descriptions in the System Security Plan (SSP) describing network, computing platform, and system segmentation

Reference to standards/source assessments:

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-3, SC-7

questions.title: WI:SI-1.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization restrict information flow between different security domains based on data type identifiers, restricting the movement of sensitive data to areas of lower sensitivity?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Information flow control regulates where information can travel within a system and between systems (in contrast to who is allowed to access the information) and without regard to subsequent accesses to that information. Flow control restrictions include blocking external traffic that claims to be from within the organization, keeping export-controlled information from being transmitted in the clear to the Internet, restricting web requests that are not from the internal web proxy server, and limiting information transfers between organizations based on data structures and content.[1]

Question Intent: Does the organization have a documented data type format specification that includes defined data type identifiers? Are these data type identifiers used to control the flow of data, specifically, restricting the movement of sensitive data to an environment of lower sensitivity?

Data Type Identifiers:

Discussion: Data type identifiers include filenames, file types, file signatures or tokens, and multiple internal file signatures or tokens. Systems only allow transfer of data that is compliant with data type format specifications. Identification and validation of data types is based on defined specifications associated with each allowed data format. The filename and number alone are not used for data type identification. Content is validated syntactically and semantically against its specification to ensure that it is the proper data type. [2]

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented data type format specification that includes defined data type identifiers. The organization can demonstrate that the specification is used to determine permitted/prohibited data flows.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has an incomplete data type format specification or cannot demonstrate the use of the specification to determine permitted/prohibited data flows.
  •  (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Data type format specification or data dictionary that contains data type identifiers; policies that describe permitted/prohibited data flows

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-4(12)

[1] NIST SP 800-53r5, p. 28

[2] Ibid, p. 32

questions.title: RE:AN-2.Q4
questions.text: Is there a standard set of tools and/or methods in use to perform incident correlation?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: This question is asked because having a standard set of tools and/or methods would indicate a higher level of process maturity.

Question Intent: To determine if a standard set of tools and/or methods are in use for incident correlation during all phases of the incident management life cycle.

  • Incident correlation can identify where activity is more widespread than originally thought, and identify any relationships among malicious attacks, compromises, and exploited vulnerabilities, or deconflicting with non-malicious activity. Often incidents are declared individually; correlation enables analysts to recognize that the underlying cause of the incident may have affected more systems in the infrastructure than identified in the single incident.
  • Pre-approving tools, techniques, and methods ensures consistency, as well as validity, of results.
  • The tools and methods can be both procedural (such as log review) and automated.
  • The tools and methods should cover all asset types.

Examples of incident correlation data sources are:

  • metadata-tagged logs or data sources within an organization, such as IP addresses, ports, protocols, timestamps, etc.
  • domain names, IP addresses (source and target), hostnames, ports, protocols, and services
  • vulnerability scans
  • exercises
  • penetration testing
  • system configuration changes

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a standard set of tools and/or methods that are used in incident correlation.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A standard set of tools and/or methods to perform incident correlation is in development

Possible evidence

  • A report, list, or document illustrating a standard set of tools and/or methods used in incident correlation
  • A set of training slides on analysis tools and techniques along with records of staff completing the training
  • results of incident correlation

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: IR:G2.Q3.
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4

questions.title: RE:AN-5.Q4
questions.text: Are vulnerabilities analyzed to determine relevance to the organization?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: With vulnerabilities growing exponentially, no organization can address them all, instead the organization should only address those that are relevant to them.

Question Intent: To determine if vulnerabilities are analyzed to determine relevance to the organization.

  • Through vulnerability analysis, the organization seeks to understand the potential threat that the vulnerability represents.
  • The organization should assign a course of action to each vulnerability based upon its relevance to the organization.
  • Vulnerability analysis includes activities to:
  • understand the threat and exposure
  • review trend information to determine whether the vulnerability existed before and what actions were taken to reduce or eliminate it
  • identify and understand underlying causes for exposure to the vulnerability

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization analyzes all vulnerabilities to determine their relevance to the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization analyzes some vulnerabilities to determine their relevance to the critical service.

Possible evidence

  • Vulnerability Prioritization guidelines
  • Vulnerability analysis
  • List of vulnerabilities prioritized for disposition
  • Updated vulnerability repository

questions.title: RE:AM-1.Q4
questions.text:
Does the organization monitor open-source information and/or information sites for evidence of unauthorized disclosure of organizational information?
If an information disclosure is discovered does the organization notify designated personnel and take additional organization-defined actions?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Unauthorized disclosures can result in the organization having a degraded ability to perform its mission. An adversary could acquire possession of the organization’s sensitive or proprietary information and place the organization’s technology or personnel assets at risk or use the information for target development or to achieve a competitive advantage. The unauthorized disclosure of personally identifiable information (PII) might cause the organization to incur financial costs, in the form of fines or remediation expenses, e.g., credit monitoring. Either situation might result in damage to the organization’s reputation.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization is proactively identifying unauthorized disclosures. Does the organization have a remediation plan, in the event of an unauthorized disclosure?

Discussion: Unauthorized disclosure of information is a form of data leakage. Open-source information includes social networking sites and code-sharing platforms and repositories. Examples of organizational information include personally identifiable information retained by the organization or proprietary information generated by the organization.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a policy or procedure to proactively identify unauthorized disclosures; and
  • The organization has a documented policy, plan, or procedure for the remediation of unauthorized disclosures.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has one of the items in “Criteria for Full Implementation Response.”

Possible evidence

  • Policy, plan, or procedure

Reference to standards/source assessments

questions.title: RE:CO-1.Q4
questions.text: Are staff members assigned to execute specific service continuity plans?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The activities documented in the service continuity plan must be assigned to responsible and skilled individuals in the event that the plan must be executed.

Question Intent: To determine if staff members are assigned to execute specific service continuity plans.

  • These staff members may be internal or external (through outsourcing arrangements and service contracts) to the organization.
  • Typical work products include:
  • service continuity plan staff requirements
  • list of potential staff members
  • staff and task assignments (internal and external)
  • staff commitments to service continuity plans

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has assigned staff required for the execution of each service continuity plan established for the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has assigned staff required for the execution of some plans.

Possible evidence

  • Service continuity plans

questions.title: RE:CO-2.Q4
questions.text: Are incidents declared in accordance with a documented process?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should follow an established process to declare incidents. Incident declaration defines the point at which the organization has established that an incident has occurred, is occurring, or is imminent, and will need to be handled and responded to.

Question Intent: To determine if incidents are declared based on a documented process.

  • Incident declaration defines when the organization has established that an incident has occurred, is occurring, or is imminent.
  • Incident declaration may occur based on a specific event or when multiple events are occurring to ensure that the organization makes a distinction between events and incidents (and the respective processes and differences in its handling).

  • The organization declares all incidents based on a documented process.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization declares some incidents.

questions.title: RE:CO-4.Q4
questions.text: Are key contacts identified in the service continuity plans?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: If the organization has external assets and services provided via external partnership that it depends on for the operation of critical services, then key contacts must be clearly defined and available.

Question Intent: To determine if key contacts are identified in service continuity plans.

  • The critical service may depend on assets both internal and external to the organization.
  • Services may also rely on external partnerships such as public agencies and infrastructure providers (public utilities, telecommunications, etc.).
  • Key contacts can therefore be internal or external to the organization.
  • Typical work products include:
  • list of public service providers on which the critical service is dependent
  • list of external entities, including business partners and vendors, that facilitate critical service delivery
  • list of key contacts (both internal and external)

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has identified key contacts in each service continuity plan established for the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has identified key contacts in some of the service continuity plans.
  • Or; The organization has identified some key contacts in the service continuity plans.

Possible evidence

  • List of public service providers on which the critical service is dependent, list of external entities, including business partners and vendors, that facilitate critical service delivery, list of key contacts (both internal and external)

questions.text: What types of cybersecurity information does the organization share with outside organizations? (Select all that apply)

Importance: Organizations that share threat intelligence with external organizations improve the overall resilience of the sector and the nation.

Question Intent: To determine what cybersecurity information the organization shares with external organizations.

External organizations can include governmental agencies such as CISA, industry or trade organizations, or even public threat feeds, to name just a few options.

The methods of information sharing can range from automated reporting in a machine-readable format to face-to-face conversations with stakeholders at other organizations.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Threat communications with outside organizations, threat communication standards and guidelines

questions.title: RE:RD-3.Q4
questions.text: Does the organization implement an alternate audit capability?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Having an alternate logging and record review capability in the event of a failure with the primary capability will allow the mission critical service/HVA to continue to operate if the primary capability fails.

Question Intent: To determine if an alternate audit logging and alternate audit record review capability exists.

  • Duplicate hardware, information, backups, or functionality in multiple locations, and keep them synchronized.
  • Replicate capabilities in multiple locations and keep them synchronized. Where possible, replicate capabilities using diverse resources.
  • Redundancy is a well-established design principle. Approaches to Redundancy include surplus capacity and replication (e.g., cold spares, hot or inline spares, etc.) and can be implemented in conjunction with backup and failover procedures. It can enhance the availability of critical capabilities but requires that redundant resources be protected.
  • Provide an alternate audit logging capability in the event of a failure in the primary capability.  Since an alternate audit logging capability may be a short-term protection, organizations may determine that the alternate audit logging capability need only provide a subset of the primary audit logging functionality.
  • Audit record review, analysis, and reporting covers information security- and privacy-related logging performed by organizations, including logging that results from the monitoring of account usage, remote access, wireless connectivity, mobile device connection, configuration settings, system component inventory, physical access, communications at system interfaces, etc. If organizations are prohibited from reviewing and analyzing audit records or unable to conduct such activities, the review or analysis may be carried out by other organizations granted such authority.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • An alternate audit logging and alternate audit record review capability has been implemented for the critical service/HVA environment.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • An alternate audit logging and alternate audit record review capability is in development and the configuration is partially implemented.

Possible evidence

  • Documentation detailing the implementation and configuration of audit logging and alternate audit record review capability (SIEM cluster, backup/replica of Syslog server, etc.).

questions.title: AD:CO-3.Q5
questions.text: Has the organization implemented the methods and channels needed to execute the communication plan?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The methods and channels that the organization chooses for communications regarding incident response and recovery must be able to support and enable communications requirements as stated in the communications plan and program.

Question Intent: To determine if the communications methods and channels related to incident response and recovery are identified and appropriate to the needs of the organization and its stakeholders.

Communications methods and channels may be formal or informal, oral or written, peer-to-peer, peer-to-subordinate, or peer-to-superior. Messages can also be delivered non-verbally through actions and gestures. Communications methods and channels can include:

  • policy statements
  • procedures manuals and company handbooks
  • specific press releases and wires
  • company hotlines, such as those that allow for reporting of ethics violations
  • email messages and text messaging
  • intranet and internet sites and webcasts
  • newsletters, posters, and flyers, as well as bulletin boards and other gathering spots
  • newspapers, magazines, and other print media
  • television, radio, podcasts, videocasts, and other public media
  • presentations, tutorials, and symposia
  • emergency broadcast systems and methods
  • closed communications channels such as two-way radio, CB radio, and satellite phone
  • secured communications channels (to provide for classified conversations) such as STUs (secure telephone units)

Methods and tools for communicating with staff, customers, end users, service provider staff, and other stakeholders during the course of service delivery are also part of the enterprise-wide communications strategy and execution. These methods and tools have to be regularly reviewed, tailored, and possibly supplemented to meet ongoing communications requirements.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented all communications channels and methods required for incident response and recovery communications.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented some of the communications channels and methods required for incident response and recovery communications. (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Documented communications methods and channels (by stakeholder class or requirement)
  • Tools, techniques, and methods for communication

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CERT RMM COMM:SG3.SP1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2, IR-4

  • The system has an endpoint detection and response solution that is capable of host isolation, but that capability does not automatically isolate system components, or it is only employed on a manual or  ad hoc basis.

questions.title: AN:CP-1.Q5
questions.text: Does the organization implement controls that monitor physical access to the system in addition to the physical access monitoring of facilities (where there is a concentration of system components, including server rooms, media storage areas, and communications centers)?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Monitoring physical access to systems provides additional monitoring for those areas within facilities where there is a concentration of system components, including server rooms, media storage areas, and communications centers.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization implements physical access controls to organizational systems in addition to the physical access monitoring of facilities.

Physical access monitoring can be coordinated with intrusion detection systems and system monitoring capabilities to provide comprehensive and integrated threat coverage for the organization.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization implements controls that monitor physical access on all organizational systems.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization implements controls that monitor physical access on some organizational systems.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Configuration baselines showing that physical access controls are configured.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PE-6(4)

questions.title: AN:CP-3.Q5
questions.text: Does the organization have an integrated incident response team that can be deployed to any location identified by the organization within specified time periods?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: If an organization does not have an on-call incident response capabilities, they may consider keeping an incident response retainer to comply with relevant regulations and laws.

Question Intent: This question determines whether the organization has an incident response team that can be deployed to any location identified by the organization within specified time periods

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has an integrated incident response team—or equivalent supplied services--that can be deployed to any location identified by the organization within specified time periods.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has an integrated incident response team—or equivalent supplied services--that can be deployed to any location identified by the organization, however there is not a guarantee they can be deployed within specified time periods.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Incident response plan, incident management plan, contract with incident response service provider for a retainer

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4(11)

questions.title: AN:CP-4.Q5
questions.text:
Does the organization require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to perform penetration testing:

a. at a given level of rigor (breadth and depth) and

b. under organization-defined constraints?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Standard red-team exercises do not always leverage the most useful threat modeling techniques. Crafting an adversary emulation that is informed by organizational threat intelligence and leverages adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures the organization has experienced previously can provide real-world conditions for use in penetration testing engagements.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization uses red-team exercises that simulate attempts by adversaries in real-world conditions to compromise organizational systems.

Rules of engagement define the vectors, tactics, tools, and systems that are in-scope for the red-team exercise.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization periodically conducts red-team exercises that simulate attempts by adversaries in real-world conditions to compromise organizational systems. These exercises abide by applicable rules of engagement.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization periodically conducts red-team exercises to simulate the compromise of organizational systems. However, these exercises do not have realistic rules of engagement defined which can affect the value of exercise results and make the simulated attacks stray too far from what the organization is likely to see in a real-world scenario.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • An after-action report or lessons learned report from a red-team exercise conducted against the organization, rules of engagement used in red-team exercises.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CA-8(3)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:DI-2.Q5
questions.text: Does the organization establish alternate communications paths for system operations organizational command and control?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Alternate communications paths reduce the risk of all communications paths being affected by the same incident. 

Question Intent: This question determines if alternate communications paths for system operations organizational command and control have been implemented and are in use by the organization. 

An incident, whether adversarial or non-adversarial based, can disrupt established communications paths used for system operations and organizational command and control. Alternate communications paths reduce the risk of all communications paths being affected by the same incident. 

The inability of organizational officials to obtain timely information about disruptions or to provide timely direction to operational elements after a communications path incident, can impact the ability of the organization to respond to such incidents in a timely manner. 

Establishing alternate communications paths for command-and-control purposes, including designating alternative decision makers if primary decision makers are unavailable and establishing the extent and limitations of their actions, can greatly facilitate the organization’s ability to continue to operate and take appropriate actions during an incident. 

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Alternate communications paths have been documented and implemented and are in use for system operations organizational command and control.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Alternate communications paths are under development and are in the process of being documented and implemented.

Possible Evidence

  • Configuration documentation detailing the implantation of the alternate communications paths

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-47

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q5
questions.text: Is there a documented policy for incident management?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should have a documented policy for incident management as such a policy establishes the organizational expectations for planning and performing the incident management process and communicates those expectations to the organization.

Question Intent: This question determines if a policy for performing incident management activities exists.

A policy is a written communication from the organization’s senior management to its employees.

The policy should address:

  • responsibility, authority, ownership, and the requirement to perform incident management activities
  • establishment of procedures, standards, and guidelines
  • requirements for periodically assessing incident management activities
  • post-incident review, problem resolution, and closure
  • measuring adherence to policy, exceptions granted, and policy violations
  • compliance with legal, regulatory, contractual, and government obligations

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented policy for performing incident management.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A policy is in development and partially documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  •  A Standard Operating Procedure for Incident Management or Other relevant organizational policy covering incident management.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: IM:MIL2.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-1

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:GV-2.Q2
questions.text: Have stakeholders for controls management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Stakeholders are more likely to be invested in controls management activities when they are well informed and aware of their roles in the process.

Question Intent: This question determines if stakeholders for controls management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Stakeholders of the controls management process have the following responsibilities:

  • defining and managing control objectives and controls, including ensuring the effectiveness of controls
  • overseeing the controls management process
  • managing the risk resulting from unresolved problems (gaps in controls, insufficient staffing, or funding, etc.)

Examples of stakeholders include:

  • critical service owners
  • management
  • controls management staff
  • owners and custodians of assets that underpin the service
  • critical service staff
  • external entities responsible for some part of the service
  • information technology staff
  • staff responsible for physical security
  • human resources
  • internal and external auditors

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All stakeholders for the controls management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some stakeholders for the controls management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.
  • Or, stakeholders are identified but have not been made aware of their roles.

Possible Evidence

  •  A Standard Operating Procedure for controls management or other relevant organizational policy that includes a section on roles and responsibilities for controls management functions

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: CM:MIL2.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PS-7, PM-1, PM-2

questions.title: AN:GV-4.Q5
questions.text: Is there adequate funding to perform incident management activities as planned?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Funding is an indication of higher-level management support and sponsorship of incident management activities.

Question Intent: This question determines if adequate funding has been provided for incident management activities. The intent of the question is to evaluate the completeness of the funding, not the completeness of the plan.

Funding should be available to support the proper oversight, execution, and maintenance of incident management activities

Considerations for funding planned incident management activities include:

  • defining funding needs
  • establishing a budget
  • resolving funding gaps
  • funding the process activities including staffing, tools, training, etc.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Adequate funding has been provided to perform all planned incident management activities

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The planned activities have only been partially funded
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Attestation from stakeholders regarding funding for incident management activities.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: IM:MIL3.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SA-2, PM-3, PM-7, PM-9, PM-10, PM-11

questions.title: WI:AE-3.Q5
questions.text: Is access to the audit log repository restricted to those with a business need?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: It is imperative that only trusted subjects are only given the minimum privileges necessary for satisfying organizational mission/business needs relative to the organizations policy. This is most applicable when there is a mandate that establishes a policy regarding access to controlled unclassified information or classified information and some users of the system/repository are not authorized access to all such information resident in the system/repository.

Question Intent: To determine if there are restrictions to the audit log repositories based on mission/business need.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • There exists policy and controls that restrict access to systems/repositories based on business need.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • There exists policy and controls that restricts access to systems/repositories, but they are not based on business need.

Possible evidence

  • Access enforcement policy
  • List of users and what systems they have access to
  • List of all user account types and holders
  • Example of denying access due to account restrictions

questions.title: WI:AM-1.Q5
questions.text: Are both owners and custodians of assets documented in asset descriptions?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: As security events and incidents occur, it may become necessary to talk with system owners to determine if a given activity is typical. It also will be important to communicate with owners and custodians regarding routine maintenance and a number of other activities.

Question Intent: To determine if owners and custodians of assets are documented in asset descriptions.

  • Asset owners are the people or organizational entities, internal or external to the organization, that have primary responsibility for the viability, productivity, and resilience of the asset. 

Example asset owners include:

  • service owners
  • managers and staff supervisors
  • organizational units
  • lines of business

Asset custodians are people or organizational entities, internal or external to the organization, who are responsible for satisfying the protection and sustainment requirements for the asset established by the asset owner.

Example asset custodians include:

  • System or database administrator
  • Facility manager
  • IT support organization
  • Contractors hosting and managing data (e.g., cloud service provider)

Note: Inventories of assets may exist in multiple forms or physical locations.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization documents owners and custodians in asset descriptions for all assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization documents owners and custodians in asset descriptions for some assets.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Asset inventories for hardware, software, IT systems, etc.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: AM:G2.Q3-T (PIF)
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-8, CM-8(4), PM-5
