questions.title: WI:IP-10.Q5
questions.text: How often does the organization review responses to actual business continuity/disaster recovery events  to see if they are consistent with the  response procedures/plan that support the critical service?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Periodic reviews for adherence to the business continuity/disaster recovery procedures/plan ensures business continuity/disaster recovery activities are performed as intended.

Question Intent: To determine if and how often actual business continuity/disaster recovery events are reviewed for the purpose ensuring the responses are consistent with the business continuity/disaster recovery procedures/plan.

Periodic reviews for adherence to the business continuity/disaster recovery procedures/plan are needed to ensure that:

  • Activities are performed as planned and adhere to process descriptions, standards, and procedures
  • Deviations from the plan are identified and evaluated
  • Problems in the plan for performing business continuity/disaster recovery management activities are identified
  • Non-compliance is addressed
  • Needed plan, process or procedure changes are identified when expected results or outputs are not met

To help response activities function as intended, organizations may use metrics and evaluation criteria to assess response programs as part of an effort to continually improve response performance.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • responses to all actual business continuity/disaster recovery events are reviewed within a formally defined time after incident resolution, business continuity or disaster recovery plan execution, as part of follow-on actions.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Responses to some actual business continuity/disaster recovery events are reviewed within a formally defined time after incident resolution, business continuity or disaster recovery plan execution, as part of follow-on actions.
  • Or, responses to all actual business continuity/disaster recovery events are reviewed at least annually (not defined as part of follow-on actions).

Possible evidence

  • Documented results from the reviews detailing the timeframe of the review.
  • Documented business continuity/disaster recovery plan, process, policy or procedure that indicates the type of review must take place and the period of the review.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: Q.25.1 
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-4

questions.title: WI:MA-1.Q5
questions.text: Are software and firmware flaws patched or mitigated in a timeframe consistent with the level of risk associated with the vulnerability?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Prompt patching of system flaws can prevent their exploitation by attackers.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization patches or mitigates flaws in its systems in a time frame consistent with the level of risk associated with the vulnerability.

Attackers routinely exploit flaws to gain control over systems. Particularly in large organizations, the number of systems can lead to a very large number of flaws that require mitigation or management. Need to maintain system uptime and business processes can therefore require careful prioritization of remediation efforts to address the most important flaws first.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization patches or mitigates all system flaws in a timeline consistent with the associated level of risk.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization patches or mitigates some system flaws in a timeline consistent with the associated level of risk OR does not differentiate flaw remediation by risk.

Possible evidence

  • Vulnerability management policies and procedures.
  • Change management records

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53 Rev. 5 SI-2

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: WI:PR-1.Q5
questions.text: Does the organization enforce dual authorization for the movement and deletion of organization-defined audit information?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Attackers often try to cover their tracks by moving or deleting audit information. Requiring dual authorization reduces the ability of a single individual or account to do so.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization enforces dual authorization for the movement and deletion of organization-defined audit information?

Discussion: Organizations may choose different selection options for different types of audit information. Dual authorization mechanisms (also known as two-person control) require the approval of two authorized individuals to execute audit functions. To reduce the risk of collusion, organizations consider rotating dual authorization duties to other individuals. Organizations do not require dual authorization mechanisms when immediate responses are necessary to ensure public and environmental safety.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization defines audit information which requires dual authorization for movement and deletion; and
  • The organization requires dual authorization for the movement and deletion of audit information defined in (a).

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • This practice is either Fully Implemented or Not Implemented. No Partial Implementation.

Possible evidence

  • Audit and accountability policy; access control policy and procedures; procedures addressing protection of audit; information; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; access authorizations; system audit records.
  • Dual authorization policy and/or procedures
  • List of audit logs that requiring dual authorization for movement or deletion.
  • Evidence that attempts to carry out movement or deletion by only one user are not successful,

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53 AU-9(5)

questions.title: WI:PR-3.Q5
questions.text: Does the organization require individuals accessing the system to employ supplemental authentication techniques or mechanisms under specific organization-defined circumstances or situations?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: An automated approach to requiring supplemental authentication reduces the likelihood of an attacker gaining access using compromised credentials.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization requires individuals accessing the system to employ supplemental authentication techniques or mechanisms under specific organization-defined circumstances or situations.

Discussion: Adversaries may compromise individual authentication mechanisms employed by organizations and subsequently attempt to impersonate legitimate users. To address this threat, organizations may employ specific techniques or mechanisms and establish protocols to assess suspicious behavior. Suspicious behavior may include accessing information that individuals do not typically access as part of their duties, roles, or responsibilities; accessing greater quantities of information than individuals would routinely access; or attempting to access information from suspicious network addresses. When pre-established conditions or triggers occur, organizations can require individuals to provide additional authentication information. Another potential use for adaptive authentication is to increase the strength of mechanism based on the number or types of records being accessed. Adaptive authentication does not replace and is not used to avoid the use of multi-factor authentication mechanisms but can augment implementations of multi-factor authentication.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Supplemental authentication techniques or mechanisms to be employed when accessing the system under specific circumstances or situations are defined; and
  • Circumstances or situations that require individuals accessing the system to employ supplemental authentication techniques or mechanisms are defined; and
  • Individuals accessing the system are required to employ supplemental authentication techniques  or mechanisms, defined in (a), under specific circumstances or situations, defined in (b).

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Looking at this control from a system-level perspective it is either Fully Implemented or Not Implemented. If the perspective is enterprise-wide, this should be implemented across the critical services and HVAs to be Fully Implemented.

Possible evidence

  • Identification and authentication policy; procedures addressing adaptive/supplemental identification and authentication techniques or mechanisms; system security plan; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; supplemental identification and authentication techniques or mechanisms; system audit records.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IA-10

questions.title: WI:CM-1.Q5
questions.text: What types of logs are reviewed? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Continuous monitoring is a rigorous process that demands significant data collection, sensing, and processing. This process must be extensive and integral across the entire organization to maintain situational awareness. Although the context and strategic goals of the organization may dictate the required logs to maintain, it is critical that this assessment clarifies the consistency and regularity of the reviews.

Question Intent: This question tries to gain a better understanding of the security practices and processes of the organization. Logs provide insight into organizational activities, events, and incidents. Consistent practice in terms of log maintenance as much as regular review and analysis can greatly enhance the effectiveness security as much as it is a hallmark of continuous monitoring.

Continuous monitoring may utilize tools that perform logging, alerting, and reporting.

Alternative terms used could include “ConMon” or an abbreviation of “Continuous Monitoring”. See also “CSM” for “Continuous Security Monitoring”.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Continuous monitoring practices and policy should mandate the usage and maintenance of logs within the organization, which should include but not be limited to the criteria provided by this question (e.g., servers, authentication, services, applications, firewalls, network devices, etc.).

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Although the organization maintains logs within the organization, the practice is inconsistent. Events are not documented, incidents may not be captured with sufficient information, information is not maintained for a sufficient period of time, etc.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Examples or portions of logs as listed in the question criteria
  • Policy and procedure related to log maintenance
  • Analytic results from log research and analysis
  • After action reports and investigation related evidence that demonstrates utilization of logs for incidents

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: Q.21.1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-2, AU-12, CA-7, CM-3, SC-5, SC-7, SI-4

The organization does not perform log review.

questions.title: WI:CM-4.Q5
questions.text: Are anti-virus/malware scans conducted on a periodic basis across the complete extent of the organization’s operational technology environment?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations must continuously monitor their systems and related networks to prevent the intrusion of threat actors and avoid the injection of malicious code. Scanning enables and organization to monitor for malicious code injection and avoid significant breach.

Question Intent: The question tries to determine the malicious code scanning practices of the organization as it relates to continuous monitoring practices.

Scanning and testing help organizations reduce their exposure to threats by evaluating external network presence by monitoring public, static Ips for accessible services and vulnerabilities. Similarly, application scanning seeks out known and publicly accessible websites for bugs and improper configuration. Once discovered, the identified vulnerabilities can be prioritized and addressed in accordance with the organizational risk appetite.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has and properly utilizes tools to conduct regular scanning for vulnerabilities. Policy and procedure exist to guide the workforce in appropriate scanning practices. Documentation or logs reflect those scans are conducted in a timely fashion. Tools are updated on a periodic basis to ensure that new vulnerabilities are detected before risks may come to fruition.
  • If the organization does not have an operational technology environment, select full implementation.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has the proper tools and policies that enable scanning. However, the organization may fail to properly configure the tools or update them with any regular periodicity. Scans may take place, but the organization fails to prioritize and act upon necessary patching.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Organizational policies and procedures that direct the proper use of scanning tools
  • Documentation or logs that indicate scanning activities
  • Scanning activity results along with evidence of disposition and risk-based decisions to patch vulnerabilities

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53: SI-3, SI-8

questions.title: WI:CM-7.Q5
questions.text: How does the organization monitor for unauthorized devices? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Unauthorized operations in the network must be eliminated as soon as it is identified. This includes proper monitoring for unauthorized connections, devices/hardware, and/or software installations. By monitoring for these events, the organization should avoid a variety of potentially successful cyber-attacks and exploitation.

Question Intent: This question is trying to identify practices that look for unauthorized devises that try to link to the networks.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization must have policy or procedure that mandates the use of tools and practices that regularly monitor for unauthorized devices. Similarly, the policy should call out and define what a “cyber-relevant time frame” is for the organization in terms of response in accordance with the organizational risk appetite.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may have policy or procedure that mandates the use of tools and practices that regularly monitor for unauthorized devices. However, the organization may fail to do so in a consistent and standardized manner. Furthermore, the organization may lack the ability to respond in a timely manner.

Possible evidence

  • Policy and procedure related to consistent monitoring of the organization’s networks
  • Documentation and or logs that demonstrate regular monitoring
  • Documentation or logs that provide information related to timely responses to alerts

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53: AU-12, CA-7, CM-3, CM-8, PE-3, PE-6, PE-20, SI-4

Host-based detection of unauthorized external storage or peripherals
The organization implements technical solutions that prohibit unauthorized devices from gaining network or host access
The organization does not monitor for unauthorized devices

questions.title: WI:CM-8.Q5
questions.text: Is the effectiveness of vulnerability scanning reviewed?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Vulnerabilities can be identified in a variety of ways, which enables automated scanning and other methods that may prevent threat actors from exploiting them before being identified and patched. Once identified, vulnerabilities are promulgated to many organizations as warning and to enable scanning activities to identify and either prevent or eliminate infection. This process, however, would not be successful unless the organization is properly advised of these vulnerabilities in a timely manner.

Question Intent: This question tries to gain an understanding of the vulnerability management process within the organization. This includes the steps taken to advise the organization on identified vulnerabilities and patching process. More importantly, the organization should be taking stock of their practices to see if it is effective in managing its vulnerabilities.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization must have a policy or procedure that guides the scanning practices of the organization. More specifically, the direction should mandate means of measurement for scanning performance.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may be looking to measure vulnerability scanning and patching performance. However, the organization may not be doing so in a consistent or timely manner.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Scanning tools implemented in the organization
  • Demonstration that the scanning tools are regularly updated
  • Documentation and logs that demonstrate proper and timely response to alerts from the scans

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CERT RMM VAR:SG3.SP1
  • CRR, VM:G3.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-5, RA-7

questions.title: WI:SI-1.Q5
questions.text: Does the organization implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the integrity of audit information and audit tools?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Protecting the integrity of audit information ensures that individuals with privileged access to a system and who are also subject to an audit of that system cannot inhibit audit activities or modify audit records.

Question Intent: Has the organization implemented cryptographic mechanisms to protect the integrity of audit information and tools?

Discussion: Cryptographic mechanisms used for protecting the integrity of audit information include signed hash functions using asymmetric cryptography. This enables the distribution of the public key to verify the hash information while maintaining the confidentiality of the secret key used to generate the hash.[1]

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization presents a policy or procedure that describes the use of cryptographic mechanisms to protect the integrity of audit information. The organization confirms that the mechanisms are used to protect the audit information derived from the system being assessed and the audit tools used to monitor the system.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization satisfies one of the requirements in “Criteria for Full Implementation Response
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy or procedure that describes the use of cryptographic mechanisms to protect the integrity of the audit information and tools; security control implementation descriptions in the System Security Plan (SSP) that describe the use of cryptographic mechanisms to protect the integrity of audit information and tools

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-9(3)

[1] NIST SP 800-53r5, p.75

questions.title: RE:AN-5.Q5
questions.text: Are vulnerabilities categorized and prioritized?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Categorization and prioritization provides the organization a foundation for taking appropriate mitigations.

Question Intent: To determine if vulnerabilities are categorized and prioritized.

Examples of categories based on actions to be taken for vulnerability resolution:

  • take no action; ignore
  • fix immediately (typically the case for vendor updates or changes)
  • develop and implement a vulnerability resolution strategy (typically the case when the resolution is more extensive than simple actions such as vendor updates)
  • perform additional research and analysis
  • refer the vulnerability to the risk management process for formal risk consideration
  • Prioritization can be:
  • qualitative (high, medium, or low)
  • quantitative (through a numerical scale)

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization prioritizes and categorizes vulnerabilities for all assets that support the critical service

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization prioritizes and categorizes vulnerabilities for some assets.

Possible evidence

  • Vulnerability categorization and prioritization guidelines,
  • List of vulnerabilities categorized and prioritized for disposition,
  • Updated vulnerability repository

Reference to standards/source assessments

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q6
questions.text: Is there a documented policy for service continuity?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should have a documented policy for service continuity management as it establishes the organizational expectations for planning and performing the service continuity management process and communicates those expectations to the organization.

Question Intent: This question determines if a policy for performing service continuity management activities exists.

A policy is a written communication from the organization’s senior management to employees.

The policy should address:

  • responsibility, authority, ownership, and the requirement to perform service continuity management activities
  • establishment of procedures, standards, and guidelines
  • requirements for periodically assessing the service continuity management activities
  • communication of plans to stakeholders
  • responsibility for testing plans on a regular basis
  • measuring adherence to policy, exceptions granted, and policy violations
  • compliance with legal, regulatory, contractual, and government obligations
  • post-plan review and revision

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented policy for performing service continuity management.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • A Standard Operating Procedure for Service Continuity Management or Other relevant organizational policy covering service continuity management.

questions.title: AN:GV-2.Q3
questions.text: Have stakeholders for change management activities been identified and made aware of their roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Stakeholders are more likely to be invested in change management activities when they are well informed and aware of their roles in the process.

Question Intent: This question determines if stakeholders for change management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Stakeholders of the change management process have the following responsibilities:

  • creating asset baselines
  • overseeing the change management process
  • capacity management planning
  • configuration management
  • requesting and approving changes to assets
  • resolving issues in the change management process

Examples of stakeholders include:

  • critical service owners
  • management
  • change management staff
  • owners and custodians of assets that underpin the service
  • critical service staff
  • external entities responsible for some part of the service
  • information technology staff
  • staff responsible for physical security
  • human resources
  • internal and external auditors

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All stakeholders for the change management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some stakeholders for the change management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.
  • Or, stakeholders are identified but have not been made aware of their roles.

Possible Evidence

  •  A Standard Operating Procedure for change management or other relevant organizational policy that includes a section on roles and responsibilities for change management functions

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: CCM:MIL2.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PS-7, PM-1, PM-2

questions.text: Does the acquirer participate in or take advantage of industry consortia (i.e., InfraGard, Coordinating Councils, Council of Supply Chain Management) to detect threats to the acquirer and external entities?

questions.title: AN:RA-2.Q6
questions.text: Does the acquirer identify external entities that it should include as part of its threat monitoring activities?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Acquirers may choose to include threats to external entities as part of their threat monitoring activities in cases where, for example, a supplier lacks its own threat monitoring program. An acquirer may decide that sustaining the critical service requires a more complete understanding of threats to critical infrastructure than it receives through its relationships with the specific infrastructure providers.

Question Intent: This question determines if the acquirer has identified external entities that support the critical service, that it should include as part of its threat monitoring activities for the purpose of detecting threats to these external entities.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The acquirer has analyzed its external dependencies relevant to the organization’s critical services to identify all external entities that it should include as part of its threat monitoring, and it monitors threats against these entities.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The acquirer monitors threats against only a subset of all identified external entities it would like to monitor, or it monitors threats to external entities inconsistently, or the practice appear otherwise incomplete.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Internal correspondence and meeting notes
  • list of entities to include as part of threat monitoring

questions.title: WI:AE-3.Q6
questions.text: Are staff identified and assigned to event analysis?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Designated incident response staff is a team of experts that assesses, documents, and responds to incidents so that organizational systems and networks can recover quickly and implement the necessary controls to avoid future incidents. Incident response team personnel include forensic and malicious code analysts, tool developers, systems security and privacy engineers, and real-time operations personnel. The incident handling capability includes performing rapid forensic preservation of evidence and analysis of and response to intrusions events.

  • Staff are both identified and assigned to the event analysis team.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations frequently have resilience or security events that affect a specific site or office. Understanding where an asset is located is important in planning an appropriate response.

Question Intent: To determine if the physical locations of assets are documented in the asset inventory.

  • Physical locations of assets can be internal or external to the organization.
  • The location details should be sufficient enough to support the resilience requirements of the service.

Note: Inventories of assets may exist in multiple forms or physical locations.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization documents the location of all assets that support the critical service in the asset inventory.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization documents the location of some assets in the asset inventory.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • An inventory that includes an attribute for the physical location of assets.

questions.title: WI:AC-4.Q6
questions.text: Are the methods of MFA selected based on an analysis of risk associated with user roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: . While MFA is an important safeguard against account compromise, some methods of MFA are more resistant to tampering than others.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization selects MFA methods based on an analysis of risk associated with user roles (versus, for example, accepting default MFA platform options).

Multi-factor authentication requires the use of two or more different factors to achieve authentication. The authentication factors are defined as follows: something you know (e.g., a personal identification number [PIN]), something you have (e.g., a physical authenticator such as a cryptographic private key), or something you are (e.g., a biometric). Multi-factor authentication solutions that feature physical authenticators include hardware authenticators that provide time-based or challenge-response outputs and smart cards such as the U.S. Government Personal Identity Verification card or the DoD Common Access Card. In addition to authenticating users at the system level, organizations may also employ authentication mechanisms at the application level, at their discretion, to provide increased information security. Regardless of the type of access (i.e., local, network, remote), non-privileged accounts are authenticated using multi-factor options appropriate for the level of risk. Organizations can provide additional security measures, such as additional or more rigorous authentication mechanisms, for specific types of access. NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IA-2 (2)

The type of MFA required for different user roles typically would be recorded in a policy or procedure document.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a formal written policy or procedure document that determines the types of MFA required for all accounts.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has a formal written policy or procedure document that determines the types of MFA required for some accounts.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Identity and access management policy or procedure documents

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IA-4, IA-5

questions.title: WI:IP-10.Q6
questions.text: How often do you review responses to actual cyber incidents to see if they are consistent with the incident response procedures/plan specific to the CCS? (Select one)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Periodic reviews for adherence to the incident response procedures/plan ensures incident response activities are performed as intended.

Question Intent: To determine if and how often actual cyber incident responses are reviewed for the purpose ensuring the responses are consistent with the incident response procedures/plan.

Periodic reviews for adherence to the incident response procedures/plan are needed to ensure that:

  • Activities are performed as planned and adhere to process descriptions, standards, and procedures
  • Deviations from the plan are identified and evaluated
  • Problems in the plan for performing incident management activities are identified
  • Non-compliance is addressed
  • Needed process changes are identified when expected results or outputs are not met

To help incident response activities function as intended, organizations may use metrics and evaluation criteria to assess incident response programs as part of an effort to continually improve response performance.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Responses to all actual cyber incidents are reviewed within a formally defined time after incident resolution, as part of follow-on actions.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Responses to some actual cyber incidents are reviewed within a formally defined time after incident resolution, as part of follow-on actions.
  • Or, responses to actual cyber incidents are reviewed at least annually (not defined as part of follow-on actions).

Possible evidence

  • Documented results from the incident response reviews detailing the timeframe of the review.
  • Documented incident response plan, process, policy or procedure that indicates that this type of review must take place and the period of the review.

Reference to standards/source assessments

questions.title: WI:PR-1.Q6
questions.text: Does the organization authorize read-only access to audit information to an organization-defined subset of privileged users or roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The organization should minimize access to audit information that could be used in incident investigation to those with an absolute business need to access. Access to audit info should be the minimum required to allow individuals to perform needed work roles to reduce the possibility of attackers corrupting audit information with a compromised account.

Question Intent: Determine if a subset of privileged users or roles with authorized read-only access to audit information is defined; and read-only access to audit information is authorized only to that subset of privileged users or roles.

Discussion: Restricting privileged user or role authorizations to read-only helps to limit the potential damage to organizations that could be initiated by such users or roles, such as deleting audit records to cover up malicious activity.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization defines a subset of privileged users or roles with authorized read-only access to audit information; and
  • Read-only access to audit information is authorized only to that subset (a) of privileged users or roles.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • This practice is either Fully Implemented or Not Implemented. No Partial Implementation.

Possible evidence

  • Audit and accountability policy; system security plan; privacy plan; access control policy and procedures; procedures addressing protection of audit information; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; system-generated list of privileged users with read-only access to audit information; access authorizations; access control list; system audit records.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53 AU-9(6)

questions.title: WI:CM-1.Q6
questions.text: What is the frequency with which the organization reviews event logs (Select the lowest frequency performed)?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Continuous monitoring is a rigorous process that demands significant data collection, sensing, and processing. The results of this process must be regularly reviewed and analyzed to maintain situational awareness. Although the context and strategic goals of the organization may dictate the required periodicity of these reviews, it is critical that this assessment clarifies the consistency and regularity of the reviews.

Question Intent: This question seeks to identify the periodicity of event log reviews. Clearly, the lowest frequency would provide indication of priority and quality of the reviews being performed.

Continuous monitoring may utilize tools that perform logging, alerting, and reporting.

Alternative terms used could include “ConMon” or an abbreviation of “Continuous Monitoring”. See also “CSM” for “Continuous Security Monitoring”.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Not all criteria must be met to gain a full implementation response here. Rather, the assessor should seek out the defined periodicity for automated, and manual reviews and determine whether this is being met. A standardized review process with consistent steps would be desired.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Reviews do take place. However, they review periodicity is not defined and is done in an ad hoc fashion. Furthermore, the nature of the reviews may be inconsistent in the actual execution of them.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Documentation of review results.
  • Reports or metrics that are products from the reviews.
  • Documentation of significant actions taken as a result of review analysis.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • Cyber IST: Q.21.1
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AC-2, AU-12, CA-7, CM-3, SC-5, SC-7, SI-4

questions.title: WI:CM-7.Q6
questions.text: How does the organization monitor for unauthorized software? (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Unauthorized operations in the network must be eliminated as soon as it is identified. This includes proper monitoring for unauthorized connections, devices/hardware, and/or software installations. By monitoring for these events, the organization should avoid a variety of potentially successful cyber-attacks and exploitation.

Question Intent: This question is trying to identify practices that look for unauthorized software resident in the networks.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization must have policy or procedure that mandates the use of tools and practices that regularly monitor for unauthorized software. Allowlists and blocklists must be maintained regularly and up to date. Similarly, the policy should call out and define what a “cyber-relevant time frame” is for the organization in terms of response in accordance with the organizational risk appetite.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization may have policy or procedure that mandates the use of tools and practices that regularly monitor for unauthorized software. The organization may not properly maintain allow lists and block lists for the organization. However, the organization may fail to do so in a consistent and standardized manner. Furthermore, the organization may lack the ability to respond in a timely manner.

Possible evidence

  • Policy and procedure related to consistent monitoring of the organization’s networks
  • Documentation and or logs that demonstrate regular monitoring
  • Documentation or logs that provide information related to timely responses to alerts
  • Allow list and block lists

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-10, CM-11(3)

options.text: The organization implements a software allowlist that prohibits the use of unauthorized software.
The organization does not monitor for unauthorized software

questions.title: WI:CM-8.Q6
questions.text: Are detected vulnerabilities reported to system owners?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Vulnerabilities can be identified in a variety of ways, which enables automated scanning and other methods that may prevent threat actors from exploiting them before being identified and patched. Once identified, vulnerabilities are promulgated to many organizations as warning and to enable scanning activities to identify and either prevent or eliminate infection. This process, however, would not be successful unless the organization is properly advised of these vulnerabilities in a timely manner.

Question Intent: This question tries to gain an understanding of the vulnerability management process within the organization. This includes the steps taken to advise the organization on identified vulnerabilities and patching process.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization must have policy and procedure in place that mandates regular scanning for system vulnerabilities. Furthermore, there must be direction and demonstrable proof that actions are taken when vulnerabilities are identified. System owners should also be prioritizing, and patching identified vulnerabilities.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • There may be policies and procedures in place that are driving the organization to identify and patch vulnerabilities. However, the organization may not follow the procedure properly. For example, vulnerabilities may be identified, but they may not be properly dispositioned. System owners may not be notified in a timely manner or at all. Finally, system owners may not be taking proper action.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy and procedure that directs the management of vulnerabilities
  • Documentation or logs that demonstrate the identification and disposition of known vulnerabilities
  • Documentation related to the prioritization and planning process for patching of vulnerabilities

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-5(11), RA-7

questions.supplemental:
Importance: Integrity checks on system boot ensure that hardware and firmware have not been subject to unauthorized modification.

Question Intent: Does the organization employ mechanisms to check the integrity of hardware and firmware on system boot?

Discussion: Security-relevant events include the identification of new threats to which organizational systems are susceptible and the installation of new hardware, software, or firmware. Transitional states include system startup, restart, shutdown, and abort.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented policy or procedure that describes mechanisms used to check the integrity of hardware and firmware on system boot and can demonstrate that the mechanisms are currently in use.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization presents one of the items in “Criteria for Full Implementation Response
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy or procedure

questions.title: RE:AN-5.Q6
questions.text: Is a repository used for recording information about vulnerabilities and their resolution?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: A vulnerability repository as the central source of vulnerability life-cycle information is an essential construct that is vital to the efficiency and effectiveness of other operational resilience management processes.

Question Intent: To determine if a repository for recording information about vulnerabilities and their resolution is used.

  • a vulnerability repository should be used as the central source of vulnerability lifecycle information.
  • a vulnerability repository supports analysis, disposition, trending, root cause analysis, and vulnerability management Information that should be recorded includes:
  • a unique identifier
  • description of the vulnerability
  • date entered into the repository
  • references to the source of the vulnerability
  • the priority of the vulnerability (high, medium, low)
  • categorization and disposition of the vulnerability
  • individuals or teams assigned to analyze and remediate the vulnerability
  • a log of actions taken to reduce or eliminate the vulnerability

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization uses a repository to record all vulnerability information for all the assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization uses a repository to record some vulnerability information; Or;
  • the organization uses a repository to record all vulnerability information for some assets.

Possible evidence

  • Vulnerability repository
  • Vulnerability data and information

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: VM:G2.Q6.
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-5, PM-15

questions.title: RE:AM-1.Q6
questions.text: Are techniques being used to detect hardware faults for the technology assets that support the critical service or high value system?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: In critical systems, organizations may require the system to never fail. Hardware fault detection does not prevent the fault from occurring, rather it detects the issue as it happens so that prompt action may be taken.

Question Intent: to determine if the organization uses techniques to detect hardware faults for the technology assets that support the critical service or high value system

  • The focus of availability management is the monitoring of all servers, storage devices, routers, switches, network links, power distribution, and other equipment for hardware faults and software errors.
  • Performance management looks for the causes of degraded response time, latency or indicators of insufficient processor power or poorly designed applications, insufficient network bandwidth, excessive input/output transactions, inappropriate database design, incorrect query design, software loops, etc.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization employs performance monitoring and availability management mechanisms against all of its technology assets that support critical services or high value systems. The performance management tools used by the organization are able to detect hardware faults.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization employs performance monitoring and availability management mechanisms against some of its technology assets that support critical services or high value systems. The techniques used by the organization are able to detect hardware faults.

Possible evidence

  • Hardware fault protection implementation

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SA-10(3)

questions.title: RE:CO-2.Q6
questions.text: Does guidance exist that includes the categories of incidents to report, along with the required information, timeframes, and contact mechanisms for internal and external stakeholders?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should have clear guidance on how to report incidents so the correct information gets to the right people at the right time. Incident information reported should include the timeframes, details, and any other relevant information. Relevant stakeholder can include asset owners, information technology staff, physical security staff, auditors, and legal staff, as well as external stakeholders such as vendors and suppliers, law enforcement staff, and others.

Question Intent: To identify if guidance exists that describes what (categories of incidents to report, and required information), when (timeframes), and how (contact mechanisms) they will be provided to external and internal stakeholders.

  • Accessible and well-documented guidance of this information ensures that the data shared is accurate, timely, and complete.
  • Special consideration should be made for insider threat-related incidents, because they often require unique handling in an organization due to the sensitivity and legalities involved.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented guidance that describes categories of incidents to report, required information, timeframes, and contact mechanisms for internal and external stakeholders.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The guidance is in development or partially documented.

Possible evidence

  • Documented guidance explaining how to report incidents

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: IR:G3.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-6, IR-6, IR-8

questions.title: AN:CP-3.Q7
questions.text: Does the organization implement security functions as a layered structure minimizing interactions between layers of the design and avoiding any dependence by lower layers on the functionality or correctness of higher layers?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Layered security is a core concept of defense-in-depth.

SC-3:  Security functions may be isolated by boundaries to minimize interactions between layers of design. The isolation boundary controls access to and protects the integrity of the hardware, software, and firmware that perform system security functions. Systems implement code separation in many ways, such as through the provision of security kernels via processor rings or processor modes. For non-kernel code, security function isolation is often achieved through file system protections that protect the code on disk and address space protections that protect executing code. Systems can restrict access to security functions using access control mechanisms and by implementing least privilege capabilities. 

Question Intent: This question seeks to determine if the organization designs its security functions with layered security in mind.

Security functions should be isolated from non-security functions by means of an isolation boundary implemented within a system via partitions and domains

The isolation boundary controls access to and protects the integrity of the hardware, software, and firmware that perform system security functions.

The implementation of layered structures with minimized interactions among security functions and non-looping layers (i.e., lower-layer functions do not depend on higher-layer functions) enables the isolation of security functions and the management of complexity.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization prioritizes layered security when implementing new security functions and is cognizant to ensure that any interactions and dependencies between the layered of the design are kept to an absolute minimum, with security functions existing independently of each other

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization prioritizes layered security when implementing new security functions and tries to limit interactions and dependencies between layers of the design. However, there are security functions that are provided at the same layer with no redundant functions and/or depend on the functioning of another.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Security architecture diagram

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-3(5)

questions.title: AN:CP-4.Q7
questions.text: Does the organization disrupt and adversely affect the system or system component to validate the effectiveness of protections?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The quality of penetration testing engagements can vary; therefore, organizations should specify the level of rigor and scope of such tests to accurately model the types of attacks they are likely to face as an organization.

Question Intent: This question seeks to determine if the organization holds penetration testing exercises to quality standards such as rigor and organization-defined constraints.

Penetration tests should incorporate adversary emulation techniques, use pre-determined levels of rigor, and consider any organization-defined constraints that may limit the scope of the testing

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization requires the developers of systems, system components, or system services to perform penetration testing and specifies a given level of rigor (breadth and depth) as well as any additional organization-defined constraints that the penetration test must follow.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization requires the developers of systems, system components, or system services to perform penetration testing, however the organization does not specify a given level of rigor (breadth and depth) or organization-defined constraints for the penetration testing.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation) 

Possible Evidence

  • Rules of engagement for a penetration test performed against the system, system component, or system service that includes description of the level of rigor used, as well as the constraints the penetration testers had to work under.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-9(1)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q7
questions.text: Is there a documented policy for risk management?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should have a documented policy for risk management as it establishes the organizational expectations for planning and performing the risk management process and communicates those expectations to the organization.

Question Intent: This question determines if a policy for performing risk management activities exists.

A policy is a written communication from the organization’s senior management to employees.

The policy should address:

  • responsibility, authority, ownership, and the requirement to perform risk management activities
  • establishment of procedures, standards, and guidelines
  • requirements for periodically assessing the risk environment
  • measuring adherence to policy, when exceptions are granted, and policy violations
  • compliance with legal, regulatory, contractual, and government obligations

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented policy for performing risk management.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A policy is in development and partially documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation) 

Possible Evidence

  • A Standard Operating Procedure for Risk Management or Other relevant organizational policy covering risk management.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: RM:MIL2.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-1, SR-1

questions.title: AN:GV-2.Q4
questions.text: Have stakeholders for vulnerability management activities been identified and made aware of their roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Stakeholders are more likely to be invested in vulnerability management activities when they are well informed and aware of their roles in the process.

Question Intent: To determine if stakeholders for vulnerability management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Stakeholders of the vulnerability management process have the following responsibilities:

  • overseeing the vulnerability management process
  • resolving issues with the vulnerability management process
  • establishing vulnerability prioritization guidelines
  • assessing collected vulnerability data
  • providing feedback to those responsible for providing vulnerability data
  • reviewing and appraising the effectiveness of vulnerability management activities

Examples of stakeholders include:

  • critical service owners
  • management
  • owners of external entity relationships
  • vulnerability management program staff
  • owners and custodians of assets that underpin the service
  • critical service staff
  • external entities responsible for some part of the service
  • information technology staff
  • staff responsible for physical security
  • human resources
  • internal and external auditors
  • acquisition and procurement staff
  • enterprise risk management staff
  • service continuity staff

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All stakeholders for the vulnerability management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some stakeholders for the vulnerability management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.
  • Or, stakeholders are identified but have not been made aware of their roles.

Possible Evidence

  •  A Standard Operating Procedure for vulnerability management or other relevant organizational policy that includes a section on roles and responsibilities for vulnerability management functions

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: VM:MIL2.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PS-7, PM-1, PM-2

questions.title: AN:GV-4.Q7
questions.text: Is there adequate funding to perform risk management activities as planned?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Funding is an indication of higher-level management support and sponsorship of risk management activities.

Question Intent: This question determines if adequate funding has been provided for risk management activities. The intent of the question is to evaluate the completeness of the funding, not the completeness of the plan.

Funding should be available to support the proper oversight, execution, and maintenance of risk management activities.

Considerations for funding planned risk management activities include:

  • defining funding needs
  • establishing a budget
  • resolving funding gaps
  • funding the process activities, including staffing, tools, training, etc.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • This must be true to mark a Yes.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The planned activities have only been partially funded.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  •  Attestation from stakeholders regarding funding for risk management activities.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: RM:MIL3.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SA-2, PM-3, PM-7, PM-9, PM-10, PM-11

questions.text: Have internal stakeholders (such as the critical service owner and incident management staff) been identified to whom threat information must be communicated?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Internal stakeholders are identified to ensure communications about ongoing threat monitoring activities, promote threat awareness, and ensure that the organization is performing under a common operating picture.

Question Intent: This question determines if internal stakeholders who must receive threat information have been identified.

External stakeholders may have a stated role in communication plans, or the service continuity plans of the organization

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some internal stakeholders have been identified and documented.

questions.title: AN:RA-5.Q7
questions.text: Are risks related to the performance of planned controls management activities identified, analyzed, disposed of, monitored, and controlled?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The intent is to determine risks that prevent the organization from performing controls management activities (controls management process), not the risks to the organization if the activities are not performed.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization identifies, analyzes, and mitigates risks related to the performance of the controls management activities.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Risks to the performance of all planned controls management activities are identified, analyzed, disposed of, monitored, and controlled.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Risks to the performance of some of the planned controls management activities are identified, analyzed, disposed of, monitored, and controlled. risks to the performance of planned controls management activities are identified, but are not analyzed, disposed of, monitored, or controlled.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Risk register
  • Risk management plan
  • Change management documentation

questions.title: AN:RM-1.Q8
questions.text: Are the owners of high-value or critical systems included in risk management processes?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Including system owners in the risk management process can ensure a more complete picture of organizational risk.

Question Intent: This question determines if system owners are considered relevant stakeholders in order to provide a sufficient understanding of risk management processes. 

Qualities of key idea being sought with examples

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization formally include owners of high-value or critical systems in the risk management process.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization informally includes high-value or critical systems owners in the risk management process,
  • Or, the organization formally includes only some, but not all, owners of high-value or critical systems in the risk management process
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Documentation of high-value or critical systems owners or similar roles included in the risk management process

questions.title: AN:SC-1.Q7
questions.text: Are providers of external system services required to employ security controls in accordance with applicable policies, regulations, standards, guidance, and established service level agreements?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: If an organization is held to certain regulatory compliance standards, then the providers of external system services they use must be compliant with such standards as well. Therefore, the organization must evaluate their providers to determine if they employ the required security controls, this can be accomplished through audits, test results, or other forms of evaluations to ensure that the provider is abiding by applicable, policies, regulations, standards, guidance, and established service level agreements.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization requires providers of external system services to abide by applicable policies, regulations, standards, guidance, and established service level agreements.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization fully documents compliance requirements when entering into agreements with providers of external system services. Agreements contain explicit language regarding applicable policies, regulations, standards, guidance, and service level agreements that the provider must comply with.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization partially documents compliance requirements when entering into agreements with providers of external system services. Agreements contain some language regarding applicable policies, regulations, standards, guidance, and service level agreements that the provider must comply with.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Agreements and/or contracts between the organization and its providers.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • VADR: Contractors/Vendors/Procurement
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SR-5(1)

questions.title: WI:AE-3.Q7
questions.text: Are events analyzed in a timeframe consistent with the criticality of the system?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Reported incidents that uncover system vulnerabilities are analyzed by organizational personnel related to the system. The analysis can serve to prioritize mitigation actions to address the discovered system vulnerability. Timely implementation of the mitigation actions proposed during event analysis plays a crucial role in protecting critical systems in the future.

Question Intent: To determine if events are analyzed in a timeframe consistent with the criticality of the system.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Events are analyzed in a timeframe consistent with the criticality of the system, based on the organizations incident response policies and procedures.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Events are analyzed, but not in the relevant timeframe of the organizations proposed incident response procedures.

Possible evidence

  • Incident response policy & procedures
  • Mitigation actions report after an event
  • Incidence response report and timeline of previous events

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-6, CA-7, IR-4, IR-5, IR-8, SI-4

questions.title: WI:AM-1.Q7
questions.text: Does the organization establish criteria that define which assets are mission critical?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: If everything is important, then nothing is important. Establishing criteria on how to define “critical” will help ensure that only truly important systems are included in the critical listing.

Question Intent: To determine if organizations have defined criteria to designate which systems and data are mission critical.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Documented criteria exist to define systems and data as mission critical.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Documented criteria are being developed to define systems and data as mission critical.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Up-to-date list or database of critical systems and data
  • Up-to-date list of POCs for critical systems and data
  • Procedures for designating systems and data as critical

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 1.2.3.01
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-9, CM-8, PM-5

questions.title: WI:AC-4.Q7
questions.text: On what systems is MFA enforced (Select all that apply)
questions.supplemental:
Importance: For MFA to be fully effective, it should apply to all routes that an attacker might exploit to gain access to a system.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization deploys MFA in a comprehensive manner across multiple potential attack vectors.

While many organizations protect remote access and cloud resources with MFA, there are often gaps in coverage. For an organization to assess risk fully, it needs to understand what systems continue to employ single-factor authentication.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All systems are checked.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some systems are checked.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • MFA solution control panel
  • User inventory
  • Identity and Access Management solution user records
  • Employee lists
  • Lists of contractors or other third parties with access
  • Identity and access management policy or procedure documents

questions.title: WI:IP-3.Q7
questions.text: Are modifications to technology assets reviewed?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Effective configuration and change management requires appropriate review of changes to assets.

Question Intent: To determine if modifications to technology assets are reviewed.

  • Proposed changes to assets are analyzed to determine the impact to the critical service including the resilience requirements.
  • Changes are also evaluated for their potential impact to multiple services.

  • All modifications to technology assets that support the critical service are reviewed.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some modifications to technology assets are reviewed.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

  • Documentation of policies or procedures for reviewing modifications of technology assets.

questions.title: WI:IP-4.Q7
questions.text: Are backups protected from unauthorized access, alteration, or deletion?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Maintaining the integrity of backups is an important part of an organization’s resilience planning and execution.

Question Intent: Whether the organization maintains access control and integrity verification and validation capabilities for backups.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization protects all backups from unauthorized access and alteration and deletion

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization protects all backups from unauthorized access or alteration or deletion
  • Or, the organization protects some backups on an ad hoc basis
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Documentation showing access control and integrity protection measures for backups

questions.title: WI:PR-1.Q7
questions.text: Does the organization enforce dual authorization for implementing changes to organization-defined system components and system-level information?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Here as elsewhere, dual authorization imposes an additional barrier to attackers’ ability to attack a system and cover their tracks by requiring collusion with an employee or a second compromised privileged account.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization enforces dual authorization for implementing changes to organization-defined system components and system-level information.

Discussion: Organizations employ dual authorization to help ensure that any changes to selected system components and information cannot occur unless two qualified individuals approve and implement such changes. The two individuals possess the skills and expertise to determine if the proposed changes are correct implementations of approved changes. The individuals are also accountable for the changes. Dual authorization may also be known as two-person control. To reduce the risk of collusion, organizations consider rotating dual authorization duties to other individuals. System-level information includes operational procedures.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • System components requiring dual authorization for changes are defined; and
  • System-level information requiring dual authorization for changes is defined; and
  • Dual authorization for implementing changes to system components and system-level information is enforced.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Dual authorization is implemented for changes to system components only; or
  • Dual authorization is implemented for changes to system-level information only.

Possible evidence

  • Dual authorization policy and/or procedures
  • List of system components requiring dual authorization for changes.
  • List of system-level information requiring dual authorization for changes.
  • Evidence that attempts to carry out changes to specified system components or information by only one user are not successful.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-5(4)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: WI:SI-1.Q7
questions.text: Does the organization automatically shut down or otherwise isolate systems on which hardware/firmware integrity violations are detected?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Hardware/firmware integrity violations indicate potential unauthorized modification. When hardware/firmware integrity violations are detected, the host systems should be isolated.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization has established procedures to detect hardware/firmware integrity violations. When integrity violations are detected, does the organization have a procedure to isolate the affected system(s).

Provenance Tracking: Identify and track the provenance of data, software, or hardware elements. Verify the source of the system elements on which the organization depends.

Discussion: Organizations may define different integrity-checking responses by type of information, specific information, or a combination of both. Types of information include firmware, software, and user data. Specific information includes boot firmware for certain types of machines. The automatic implementation of controls within organizational systems includes reversing the changes, halting the system, or triggering audit alerts when unauthorized modifications to critical security files occur.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a mechanism to detect hardware/firmware integrity violations. The mechanism is documented in a policy, procedure, or relevant security control implementation descriptions in a System Security Plan (SSP).

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization presents one of the items in “Criteria for Full Implementation Response
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

  • Policy, procedure, or System Security Plan (SSP)

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-7(5)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: RE:AN-5.Q7
questions.text: Is the status of unresolved vulnerabilities monitored?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The organization must develop and implement an appropriate resolution strategy for unresolved vulnerabilities which the organization has determined that exposure must be reduced or eliminated.

Question Intent: To determine if the status of unresolved vulnerabilities is monitored.

  • Unresolved vulnerabilities should be regularly monitored and reported.
  • Unresolved vulnerabilities are typically those whose disposition is:
  • To monitor a vulnerability resolution strategy that remains incomplete
  • To perform additional research and analysis
  • To refer the vulnerability to the risk management process for formal risk consideration

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization monitors the status of all unresolved vulnerabilities.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization monitors the status of some unresolved vulnerabilities.

Possible evidence

  • Vulnerability management strategies (and status reports)
  • Vulnerability repository with resolution status information

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: VM:G3.Q3.
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-5, PM-15

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: RE:AM-1.Q7
questions.text: Are techniques being used to detect application faults for the technology assets that support the critical service or high value system?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: in critical systems, organizations may require the system to never fail. Application fault detection does not prevent the fault from occurring, rather it detects the issue as it happens so that prompt action may be taken.

Question Intent: to determine if the organization uses techniques to detect application faults for the technology assets that support the critical service or high value system

  • The focus of availability management is the monitoring of all servers, storage devices, routers, switches, network links, power distribution, and other equipment for hardware faults and software errors.
  • Performance management looks for the causes of degraded response time, latency or indicators of insufficient processor power or poorly designed applications, insufficient network bandwidth, excessive input/output transactions, inappropriate database design, incorrect query design, software loops, etc.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization employs performance monitoring and availability management mechanisms against all its technology assets that support critical services or high value systems. The performance management tools used by the organization are able to detect application faults.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization employs performance monitoring and availability management mechanisms against some of its technology assets that support critical services or high value systems. The techniques used by the organization are able to detect application faults.

Possible evidence

  • Application fault protection implementation

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SA-10(3)

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

questions.title: RE:CO-2.Q7
questions.text: Does the guidance include operational and information security requirements?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: An organization’s incident reporting guidance should address the stakeholders with whom communications about incidents are required, and include specific details such as the methods, and under what operational circumstances the stakeholders must be notified.

Additionally, it should document the information security requirements, because not all stakeholders may have access to the same communication methods, and not all may be authorized to receive the full details of the incident. Document the process, procedures, and any other guidance to identify what information is provided to individual or organizational stakeholders.

Question Intent: To determine if the guidance contains operational and information security requirements. It is essential to protect sensitive information that could further damage the organization if exposed.

For each stakeholder who is notified or leveraged for response to the incident, there may be specific security requirements that must be met to communicate details about the incident. These requirements may include:

  • specific encrypted communications (that the recipients have a capability to decrypt)
  • omission of certain information that is not appropriate to be shared with certain individuals or organizations
  • specific marking/classification schema that may be different than those of the internal organization

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • There is documented guidance that includes operational and information security requirements for each stakeholder

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The guidance is in development and partially documented.

Possible evidence

  • Documented guidance explaining how to report incidents that includes instructions on how to handle sensitive information

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMR: IR:G3.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-6, IR-6, IR-8

questions.title: AN:CP-3.Q8
questions.text: Does the organization synchronize duplicate systems or system components?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: If the organization has duplicate systems for the purpose of service continuity, such systems should be synchronized to ensure a smooth transition to the secondary site if required.

Question Intent: The question is seeking to determine if the organization synchronizes duplicate systems and/or system components.

Systems and/or system components should be duplicated in distributed locations. The synchronization of duplicated and redundant services and data helps to ensure that information contained in the distributed locations can be used in the mission or business functions of organizations, as needed.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization synchronizes all duplicate systems or system components.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization synchronizes some duplicate systems or system components.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Configuration of systems/system components at secondary sites.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SC-36(2)

questions.title: AN:CP-4.Q8
questions.text: Does the organization test backup information with certain frequency to verify media reliability and information integrity?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Threat actors can gain access to physical organizational facilities through means of social engineering, lock picking, hardware hacking, and other adversarial techniques. Therefore, penetration tests should incorporate testing of physical facilities and access points as well.

Question Intent: This question ascertains whether the organization conducts physical penetration testing exercises that circumvent controls associated with physical access points to the facility.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • the organization has conducted penetration testing that includes attempts to bypass or circumvent controls associated with physical access points to organizational facilities.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • the organization has not incorporated physical facility access into the scope of its penetration testing engagements, however there are plans in place to conduct such an engagement in the future.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Penetration test report or write up that includes findings pertaining to the physical security of organizational facilities.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SA-11(5)
