questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q8
questions.text: Is there a documented policy for external dependency management?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizations should have a policy for external dependencies management as it establishes the organizational expectations for planning and performing the external dependencies management process and communicates those expectations to the organization.

Question Intent: This question determines if a policy for performing external dependency management activities exists.

A policy is a written communication from the organization’s senior management to employees.

The policy should address:

  • responsibility, authority, ownership, and the requirement to perform external dependency management activities
  • establishment of procedures, standards, and guidelines
  • requirements for periodically assessing the external dependency management activities
  • requesting, approving, providing, and terminating access for external entities
  • requesting, approving, providing, and terminating agreements with external entities
  • measuring adherence to policy, exceptions granted, and policy violations
  • compliance with legal, regulatory, contractual, and government obligation.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a documented policy for performing external dependency management.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • A policy is in development and partially documented.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • A Standard Operating Procedure for External Dependencies Management or Other relevant organizational policy covering External Dependencies management.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: EDM:MIL2.Q2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SR-1, SA-1

questions.title: AN:GV-2.Q5
questions.text: Have stakeholders for incident management activities been identified and made aware of their roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Stakeholders are more likely to be invested in incident management activities when they are well informed and aware of their roles in the process.

Question Intent: This question determines if stakeholders for incident management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Stakeholders of the incident management process have the following responsibilities:

  • overseeing the incident management process
  • making critical decisions during the incident management process
  • resolving issues with the incident management process
  • detecting events and incidents
  • planning for incident handling, management, and response
  • collecting, documenting, and preserving event and incident evidence
  • analyzing events and incidents
  • declaring incidents

Examples of stakeholders include:

  • critical service owners and staff
  • management
  • incident managers
  • incident owners
  • staff who serve key roles in incident communication activities, such as public relations
  • owners and custodians of assets that underpin the service
  • external entities responsible for some part of the service
  • information technology staff
  • staff responsible for physical security
  • human resources
  • internal and external auditors
  • acquisition and procurement staff
  • service continuity staff

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All stakeholders for the incident management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some stakeholders for the incident management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.
  • Or, stakeholders are identified but have not been made aware of their roles

Possible Evidence

questions.title: AN:SC-1.Q8
questions.text: Does the acquirer have a documented list of triggering events or changes that require testing of controls at suppliers that support the critical service?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Certain changes and events may challenge the de-facto implementation of controls; therefore, organizations should define a list of events and/or changes that would require the testing of controls outside of the organization's purview.

Question Intent: This question determines if the acquirer has documented criteria, issues, or changes that trigger tests/reviews of controls at suppliers to ensure that they continue to meet the acquirer’s control objectives.

In addition to testing or validating controls at external entities periodically, acquirers should identify and document events or changes that trigger testing or validation. This practice is intended to guard against the possibility that the acquirer may miss important changes to the control environment at the external entity until the next scheduled test or validation. 

Example triggering events include 

  • changes in the external entities’ technical environment, for example, new servers or other hardware
  • changes in the composition of sub-contractors (the supplier’s external dependencies)
  • receiving threat or vulnerability information that may affect a supplier
  • the occurrence of incidents or “near-miss” incidents

Typical work products: 

  • documented list of triggering events
  • external entity controls testing policies, standards, and procedures

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • or all relevant suppliers that support the critical service, the acquirer has a documented list of events that will trigger the testing or validation of suppler controls to ensure they continue to meet control objectives.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The acquirer has a documented list of triggering events that apply to some suppliers, or the acquirer’s list is partial, or the practice appears otherwise incomplete.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Documented list of triggering events, external entity controls testing policies, standards, and procedures

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-4(17), RA-9, RA-2, RA-3, SA-15, PM-9, SR-1, SR-6(1)

questions.title: WI:PR-1.Q8
questions.text: Does the organization limit privilege to change system components and system-related information within a production or operational environment?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The ability to modify system components should be limited to a subset of the most skilled and experienced system administrators to reduce the likelihood of accidental or intentional compromises of system resilience.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization limits privileges to change system components and system-related information within a production or operational environment.

Discussion: In many organizations, systems support multiple mission and business functions. Limiting privileges to change system components with respect to operational systems is necessary because changes to a system component may have far-reaching effects on mission and business processes supported by the system. The relationships between systems and mission/business processes are, in some cases, unknown to developers. System-related information includes operational procedures.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Privileges to change system components within a production or operational environment are limited for all system components that support the critical service; and
  • Privileges to change system-related information within a production or operational environment are limited for all system information that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  •  Privileges to change system components within a production or operational environment are limited for some system components that support the critical service, OR
  • Privileges to change system-related information within a production or operational environment are limited for some system related information.

Possible evidence

  • Configuration management policy; procedures addressing access restrictions for changes to the system; configuration management plan; system design documentation; system architecture and configuration documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; user privilege reviews; user privilege recertifications; system component inventory; change control records; system audit records; system security plan.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • 800-53 CM-5(5)

questions.title: AN:CP-4.Q9
questions.text:
Does the organization:
(a) Prevent the exfiltration of information; and
(b) Conduct exfiltration tests?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: While organizational data flows can be monitored, and data loss prevention solutions can help stop the unauthorized exfiltration of information, these mechanisms should be tested to ensure that they function properly.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization prevents the exfiltration of information and conducts tests of the data exfiltration prevention mechanisms in place.

Techniques used to prevent the exfiltration of information from systems may be implemented at internal endpoints, external boundaries, and across managed interfaces and include adherence to protocol formats, monitoring for beaconing activity from systems, disconnecting external network interfaces except when explicitly needed, employing traffic profile analysis to detect deviations from the volume and types of traffic expected, call backs to command and control centers, conducting penetration testing, monitoring for steganography, disassembling and reassembling packet headers, and using data loss and data leakage prevention tools.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has security controls and solutions implemented to prevent the exfiltration of information and they undergo testing to ensure proper functionality.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has security controls and solutions implemented to prevent the exfiltration of information however they are not tested to ensure proper functionality.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation).

Possible Evidence

  • Report of a data exfiltration test conducted against anti-exfiltration security countermeasures.

Reference to standards/source assessments

questions.text: Have stakeholders for service continuity activities been identified and made aware of their roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Stakeholders are more likely to be invested in service continuity management activities when they are well informed and aware of their roles in the process.

Question Intent: This question determines if stakeholders for service continuity activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Stakeholders of the service continuity management process have the following responsibilities:

  • overseeing the service continuity management process
  • developing service continuity plans
  • coordinating service continuity activities
  • participating in the test and execution of service continuity plans
  • resolving issues with the service continuity management process
  • ensuring that service continuity plans reflect all external dependencies
  • reviewing and appraising the effectiveness of service continuity activities

Examples of stakeholders include:

  • critical service owners
  • management
  • owners and custodians of assets that underpin the service
  • critical service staff
  • external entities responsible for some part of the service
  • information technology staff
  • staff responsible for physical security
  • regulatory and legal entities to which the organization is required to submit service continuity plans
  • internal and external auditors
  • service continuity staff

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All stakeholders for the service continuity management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some stakeholders for the service continuity management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.
  • Or, stakeholders are identified but have not been made aware of their roles.

Possible Evidence

  •  A Standard Operating Procedure for service continuity management or other relevant organizational policy that includes a section on roles and responsibilities for service continuity management functions

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • CRR: SCM:MIL2.Q3
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PS-7, PM-1, PM-2

Question Intent: This question determines if risks due to external dependencies are identified and managed as part of operational risk management at the acquirer.

This question is separated into the three types of external entities in this assessment. In order to answer the question affirmatively for each type of entity, the organization’s risk management activities must encompass or include the identification and management of risks relating to each type of entity.

  • assessment or audit reports of third parties to confirm they are meeting contractual obligations

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The acquirer identifies risks associated with external dependencies in each entity type specified, and all risks are managed (impacts identified and analyzed, and the disposition of risk determined).

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

questions.title: AN:GV-2.Q7
questions.text: Have stakeholders for risk management activities have identified and made aware of their roles?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Stakeholders are more likely to be invested in risk management activities when they are well informed and aware of their roles in the process.

Question Intent: This question determines if stakeholders for risk management activities have been identified and made aware of their roles. 

Stakeholders of the risk management process have the following responsibilities:

  • identifying risk
  • analyzing risk
  • developing and implementing risk mitigation plans
  • reviewing the effectiveness of the risk management process
  • managing the risk resulting from unresolved problems (gaps in processes, insufficient staffing, or funding, etc.)

Examples of stakeholders include:

  • critical service owners
  • management
  • owners and custodians of assets that underpin the service

questions.title: WI:PR-1.Q10
questions.text: Does the organization enforce dual authorization for the deletion or destruction of organization-defined backup information?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Backups are a cornerstone of resilience and business continuity, and so need additional protection from deletion or destruction. Backups also may represent the only avenue by which investigators may gain access to deleted audit content. Dual authorization imposes an additional barrier to attackers’ ability to attack a system and cover their tracks by requiring collusion with an employee or a second compromised privileged account.

Question Intent: Determine if the organization enforces dual authorization for the deletion or destruction of organization-defined backup information?

Discussion (800-53): Dual authorization ensures that deletion or destruction of backup information cannot occur unless two qualified individuals carry out the task. Individuals deleting or destroying backup information possess the skills or expertise to determine if the proposed deletion or destruction of information reflects organizational policies and procedures. Dual authorization may also be known as two-person control. To reduce the risk of collusion, organizations consider rotating dual authorization duties to other individuals.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization defines which backup information requires dual authorization for deletion or destruction.
  • The organization implements dual authorization for the deletion or destruction of organization-defined backup information from (a).

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization publishes a policy on dual authorization for the deletion or destruction of organization-defined backup information but doesn’t follow it.
  • Or, the organization use dual authorization for the deletion or destruction of certain backup information but doesn’t define which backup information requires dual authorization.

Possible evidence

  • Contingency planning policy; procedures addressing system backup; contingency plan; system design documentation; system configuration settings and associated documentation; system generated list of dual authorization credentials or rules; logs or records of deletion or destruction of backup information; system security plan.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-9(7)

Importance: Stakeholders are more likely to be invested in risk management activities when they are well informed and aware of their roles in the process.

Importance: Stakeholders are more likely to be invested in external dependencies management activities when they are well informed and aware of their roles in the process.

Question Intent: This question determines if stakeholders for external dependency activities have been identified and made aware of their roles.

  • managing the operational risk that arises from external dependencies

  • management
  • owners of external entity relationships
  • external dependency management program staff
  • owners and custodians of assets that underpin the service
  • critical service staff

  • staff responsible for physical security
  • human resources
  • internal and external auditors
  • acquisition and procurement staff
  • service continuity staff

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

Importance: Organizations should have information disclosure policies in place to ensure that personnel are educated on data classification standards within the organization

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has an information disclosure policy that sufficiently details dissemination guidance for organizational information.

If personnel are uneducated on information disclosure processes, accidental disclosure introduces significant risk to the organization. Therefore, organizations should create formal documentation that describes an information disclosure policy or specific guidance. This policy should include information regarding what kind of data and information is allowed to be disclosed as well as detail information regarding any waiting periods or timeframes as to when disclosure should occur.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a fully documented information disclosure policy that describes what information can be distributed to whom and in what timeframe. 

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has a partially documented information disclosure policy
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation) 

Possible Evidence

  • Formal documentation for the information disclosure policy or guidance

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 1.2.2.04
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-1

questions.title: AN:GV-2.Q11
questions.text: Are documented cybersecurity roles and responsibilities are reviewed at least yearly?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Personnel performing incident management activities should be aware of their roles and responsibilities with regards to the incident management plan. Plans must be reviewed to ensure that roles and responsibilities are appropriately designated.

Question Intent: This question determines if the incident management plan is reviewed at least yearly to ensure that the roles and responsibilities designated for incident management activities are relevant and appropriate.

Organizations may choose to review the incident management plan in accordance with a defined frequency, however it is important to ensure that the plan is also reviewed when personnel with incident management responsibilities leave the organization so their roles and responsibilities can be reassigned to someone else within the organization.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization reviews roles and responsibilities within the incident management plan at least annually as well as when an employee with incident management responsibilities leaves the organization.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization reviews roles and responsibilities within the incident management plan, however there is not a defined frequency with which this review occurs.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Document review history or correspondence that substantiates review activities have occurred within the appropriate frequency.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 1.1.3.04
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PS-7, PM-1, PM-2

questions.title: AN:RA-5.Q14
questions.text: Are security RA results are archived in a secure and protected manner according to organizational guidelines?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: The organization should have some guidance on how it protects its sensitive risk data (e.g., encryption, access control lists [ACLs], special physical storage). If the organization doesn’t have any such guidelines, it should have a policy stating that protection of risk data is not a concern for the organization.

Question Intent: This question determines if organizations have a secure and protected location where security RAs are stored according to organizational guidelines.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • Organizational guidelines exist for archiving security RA results in a secure and protected manner.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Organizational guidelines are in the process of being developed for archiving security RA results in a secure and protected manner.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Copy of security RA protections, policy, procedures, or guidance
  • List of secure storage types and providers
  • List of individuals with access to secure systems that hold RA results

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 2.1.1.08
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PM-4, PM-9

questions.title: AN:RM-1.Q15
questions.text: Does the organization have a process and criteria for evaluating the quality of RA performance and artifacts?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: A higher level review of risk management performance indicates a more mature organizational risk management practice.

Question Intent: This question determines whether criteria and process exist within the organization to review the quality of the risk management functions. 

Qualities of key idea being sought with examples

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has documented criteria for evaluating the quality of risk management performance and artifacts
  • And, the organization has a documented process for evaluating the quality of risk management performance and artifacts

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has an ad hoc set of criteria or processes to evaluate the quality of risk management performance and artifacts

Possible Evidence

  • Documented criteria for evaluating the quality of risk management performance and artifacts
  • Documented processes for evaluating the quality of risk management performance and artifacts

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 2.1.1.18
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PM-9

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q15
questions.text: Does the organization maintain a documented media relations policy (a document that describes how questions, calls, and other interactions from the media are handled related to incidents and vulnerabilities)?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: organizations should have media relations policy or guidance in place to avoid the accidental disclosure of sensitive information for organizational incidents or vulnerabilities.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has established a media relations or guidance to be used when organizational personnel are faced with questions, calls, or other interactions from the media.

Organizations can suffer reputationally if public and media relations are not properly managed in the aftermath of an organizational incident. Media relations policies or guidance help organizational personnel navigate press and media inquiries while incidents are occurring.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response       

  • The organization has a fully documented media or public relations policy that informs organizational personnel how to respond to questions, calls, and other inquiries from the media in the event of an organizational cyber incident.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization has a partially documented media or public relations policy that informs organizational personnel how to respond to questions, calls, and other inquiries from the media in the event of an organizational cyber incident.
    •    
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence        

  • Documented media or public relations policy

Reference to standards/source assessments

       
  • IMCA: 1.2.2.03
    •    
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-1, IR-4(15)

questions.title: AN:GV-2.Q12
questions.text: Is there a clear understanding of roles and responsibilities between the organization and its third-party partners regarding cybersecurity?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Understanding of roles and responsibilities is critical in organizations, specifically pertaining to monitoring, reporting, and collateral security functions when shared between internal roles and external partners.

Question Intent: This question determines how the organization performs monitoring, reporting, and collateral security functions.

Many organizations outsource specific security functions, such as digital forensics engagements and 24/7 incident response capabilities. When roles and responsibilities between parties are divided between the internal organization and an external service provider, it is important to have defined expectations for such responsibilities to verify that they are being performed by the expected party, and either incorporate deliberate redundant functions or eliminate redundancy that does not serve a specific purpose.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization documents and defines role and responsibilities between parties for monitoring, reporting, and collateral security functions.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization partially defines role and responsibility assignments between parties for monitoring, reporting, and collateral security functions.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • RACI Matrix, Responsibility Assignment Matrix

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • HVA: NETWORK PROTECTIONS:INTERCONNECTIONS:Q5
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PS-7, PM-1, PM-2

questions.title: AN:RM-1.Q16
questions.text: Are the quality and effectiveness of risk management processes are evaluated at least annually, and appropriate improvements are made?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Evaluating the effectiveness of risk management processes can improve overall risk outcomes for the organization when appropriate improvements are made as a result.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has a defined frequency for evaluating the quality and effectiveness of risk management processes, and whether appropriate improvements result from the evaluation.

Qualities of key idea being sought with examples

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization evaluates the quality and effectiveness of risk management processes at least annually,
  • And, the organization makes appropriate improvements as a result of the evaluation

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization evaluates the quality and effectiveness of risk management processes on an ad hoc basis,
  • Or, the organization makes improvements to the risk management process on an ad hoc basis.

Possible Evidence

  • Documentation which outlines the evaluation of the quality and effectiveness of risk management processes.
  • Documentation which establishes appropriate improvements as a result of an evaluation of the risk management processes.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 2.1.1.19
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PM-9

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q16
questions.text: Are organizational policies and procedures easily available to personnel?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Personnel should be able to access and reference organizational policies and procedures, if an employee is unsure as to whether they are acting in accordance with organizational policy, it should be easily referenceable so they may be informed.

Question Intent: Organizational should be able to access and reference organizational policies and procedures, one component of this is informing employees where such documentation is located. This would likely be addressed in training and/or the onboarding process.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All organizational personnel are aware of the location where written organizational policy is located and this information is conveyed via mandatory training.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Most organizational personnel are aware of the location where written organizational policy is located and this information is conveyed via training.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Verbal attestation from organizational personnel regarding where the organizational policy lives and confirmation that they are able to access it.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 4.2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: All -1 controls from all security control families. As all policies are covered by this question.

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q17
questions.text: Does the organization review and update policies and procedures at time intervals that are informed by risk and criticality, but in any event no less frequently than once each year?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Policies and procedures should be kept current to accurately reflect the organizational cybersecurity posture and strategy.

Question Intent: This question understands if policies and procedures are updated appropriately.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • All organizational policies and procedures are reviewed at the organization-defined frequency.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • Some organizational policies and procedures are reviewed at the organization-defined frequency
  • Or, organizational policies and procedures are reviewed, however on an infrequent basis.
  • (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

  • Document revision or review history for policies and procedures,

questions.title: AN:GV-1.Q18
questions.text: Is there a defined process for communicating changes and revisions to policy throughout relevant parts of the organization?
questions.supplemental:
Importance: Organizational personnel should be informed of relevant changes and revisions to policy so they can abide by it.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has a defined process in place to notify affected personnel of changes to organizational policy.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

  • The organization has a fully documented and defined process for notifying employees and specific business units of relevant changes or revisions to policy.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

  • The organization notifies personnel of changes to policy, however the process by which notifications regarding such changes are disseminated to appropriate personnel are not standardized or fully documented.

Possible Evidence

  • Correspondence showing a standard notification received by organizational personnel when updates have been made to policy, documentation describing the procedures for notification when changes to policy are made.

Reference to standards/source assessments

  • IMCA: 4.2
  • NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: All -1 controls from all security control families. As all policies are covered by this question.
